It examines screen-based interaction and keyboard, mouse and touch control, alongside transferability and long-sequence decision-making challenges.

items.name: AdaptAgent: Adapting Multimodal Web Agents with Few-Shot Learning from Human Demonstrations
items.summary: Adapts multimodal web agents to unfamiliar websites using a small number of human demonstrations through prompting or meta-learning.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

items.name: Improved GUI Grounding via Iterative Narrowing
items.summary: Uses iterative visual narrowing to improve localization of requested GUI elements with general or specially trained vision-language models.

items.name: ScribeAgent: Towards Specialized Web Agents Using Production-Scale Workflow Data
items.summary: Studies fine-tuning open language models on production web-workflow traces, including training choices for specialized web agents.

items.name: ShowUI: One Vision-Language-Action Model for GUI Visual Agent
items.summary: Combines visual token selection, interleaved visual-action history, and curated instruction data in a compact GUI action model.
items.venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition

items.name: Automated Test Transfer Across Android Apps Using Large Language Models
items.summary: LLMigrate uses LLMs to transfer usage-based UI tests between mobile apps with similar functions, reducing the need to write tests for each app.

items.name: Large Language Model-Brained GUI Agents: A Survey
items.summary: Survey of LLM-brained GUI agents that carry out natural-language instructions across web, mobile, and desktop interfaces, organizing research and industry progress.

items.name: DroidCall: A Dataset for LLM-powered Android Intent Invocation
items.summary: Introduces data and a generation pipeline for translating natural-language requests into Android intent invocations using compact language models.

items.name: Ponder & Press: Advancing Visual GUI Agent towards General Computer Control
items.summary: Separates interpretation of user instructions from precise GUI localization using general-purpose and specialized visual-language components.
items.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025

items.name: Aguvis: Unified Pure Vision Agents for Autonomous GUI Interaction
items.summary: Uses screenshots, a unified action space, and staged grounding and reasoning training for cross-platform GUI interaction.

items.name: BigDocs: An Open Dataset for Training Multimodal Models on Document and Code Tasks
items.summary: BigDocs-7.5M provides multimodal document data, while BigDocs-Bench includes GUI reasoning and image-to-code tasks relevant to screen understanding.

items.name: The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research
items.summary: Describes BrowserGym's shared web interaction environment and AgentLab tooling for consistent experiments across multiple agent benchmarks.

items.name: Falcon-UI: Understanding GUI Before Following User Instructions
items.summary: Pretrains GUI-context understanding with instruction-free web interactions before fine-tuning Falcon-UI on instructed GUI tasks.

items.name: AgentTrek: Agent Trajectory Synthesis via Guiding Replay with Web Tutorials
items.summary: Converts public tutorials into task specifications and executes them with an agent to synthesize multimodal interaction trajectories.

items.name: Large Action Models: From Inception to Implementation
items.summary: Uses a Windows-agent case study to describe a development workflow for large action models, covering data collection, training, grounding, environment integration, and evaluation.

items.name: Iris: Breaking GUI Complexity with Adaptive Focus and Self-Refining
items.summary: Combines information-sensitive image cropping with a learning loop between element description and grounding for complex interface understanding.

items.name: WEPO: Web Element Preference Optimization for LLM-based Web Navigation
items.summary: Uses web-element preference optimization with sampled negative HTML elements to align high-level user intent with navigation actions.

items.name: Attention-driven GUI Grounding: Leveraging Pretrained Multimodal Large Language Models without Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Locates GUI targets by identifying and aggregating attention maps in pretrained multimodal models without task-specific fine-tuning.

items.name: Proposer-Agent-Evaluator(PAE): Autonomous Skill Discovery For Foundation Model Internet Agents
items.summary: Combines autonomous task proposal, web interaction, and visual success evaluation to discover skills and improve browser-agent policies.

items.name: GUI Agents: A Survey
items.summary: Categorizes GUI-agent benchmarks, evaluation metrics, architectures, and training methods, and proposes a unified perception, reasoning, planning, and acting framework.
items.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025

items.name: CAD-Assistant: Tool-Augmented VLLMs as Generic CAD Task Solvers
items.summary: CAD-Assistant plans CAD tasks and executes actions through FreeCAD's Python API, using the changing design state to guide later commands.

items.name: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
items.summary: Simulates a software-company workplace to evaluate agents on professional tasks involving websites, programs, files, and coworker communication.

items.name: Aria-UI: Visual Grounding for GUI Instructions
items.summary: Introduces a vision-based grounding model trained with diverse synthetic instructions and action histories for context-sensitive GUI targeting.
items.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025

items.name: PC Agent: While You Sleep, AI Works -- A Cognitive Journey into Digital World
items.summary: Combines PC Tracker interaction capture, completion of action and reasoning annotations, and planning and grounding agents for desktop workflows.

items.name: AutoDroid-V2: Boosting SLM-based GUI Agents via Code Generation
items.summary: Recasts mobile UI automation as on-device code generation, using app-specific documentation and synthetic tasks to guide smaller models.

items.name: GUI Testing Arena: A Unified Benchmark for Advancing Autonomous GUI Testing Agent
items.summary: Evaluates GUI testing through test-intent generation, execution, and defect detection using real, modified, and synthetic mobile application data.

items.name: OS-Genesis: Automating GUI Agent Trajectory Construction via Reverse Task Synthesis
items.summary: Builds GUI trajectories by exploring environments first and deriving tasks retrospectively, with reward-model filtering of generated trajectories.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

items.name: A3: Android Agent Arena for Mobile GUI Agents with Essential-State Procedural Evaluation
items.summary: Introduces Android Agent Arena with online application tasks and procedural evaluation based on reaching essential intermediate states.

items.name: Beyond Pass or Fail: Multi-Dimensional Benchmarking of Foundation Models for Goal-based Mobile UI Navigation
items.summary: Sphinx benchmarks foundation models on goal-based mobile UI navigation, using app test cases and a toolkit that identifies different failure modes.

items.name: InfiGUIAgent: A Multimodal Generalist GUI Agent with Native Reasoning and Reflection
items.summary: Uses staged supervised training to combine GUI understanding and grounding with hierarchical reasoning and expectation-based reflection.

items.name: WebWalker: Benchmarking LLMs in Web Traversal
items.summary: Introduces WebWalkerQA and an exploration-and-critique framework for gathering information by traversing multiple levels of a website.

items.name: Learn-by-interact: A Data-Centric Framework for Self-Adaptive Agents in Realistic Environments
items.summary: Learn-by-interact synthesizes agent interaction trajectories from documentation and derives instructions from their histories for training or in-context use across web and desktop tasks.

items.name: Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training
items.summary: Builds self-critique training examples from searched recovery paths to improve agents' ability to detect and correct errors during interaction.

items.name: Mobile-Agent-E: Self-Evolving Mobile Assistant for Complex Tasks
items.summary: Uses hierarchical mobile agents and persistent tips and reusable action shortcuts to improve complex tasks from accumulated experience.

items.name: UI-TARS: Pioneering Automated GUI Interaction with Native Agents
items.summary: Studies a screenshot-driven native GUI model with unified actions, deliberate reasoning, and iterative training on interaction traces.

items.name: R2D2: Remembering, Replaying and Dynamic Decision Making with a Reflective Agentic Memory
items.summary: R2D2 gives web agents a replay-buffer map of visited pages and a reflection step for analyzing errors and revising navigation strategies.

items.name: GUI-Bee: Align GUI Action Grounding to Novel Environments via Autonomous Exploration
items.summary: Collects environment-specific interaction data through autonomous exploration to adapt grounding models to previously unseen GUIs.

items.name: A Comprehensive Survey of Agents for Computer Use: Foundations, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.summary: Reviews 87 computer-use agents and 33 datasets through a taxonomy of operating domain, observation and action modalities, and agent design.

items.name: CowPilot: A Framework for Autonomous and Human-Agent Collaborative Web Navigation
items.summary: Introduces CowPilot, a web-navigation framework where agents suggest actions and users can pause, reject, override, or resume them. It evaluates autonomous and collaborative use through task success and human effort.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (System Demonstrations)

items.name: Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Interactive LLM Agents
items.summary: LOOP trains interactive digital agents with reinforcement learning in stateful, multi-app environments where tasks are performed through API calls.

items.name: AutoGUI: Scaling GUI Grounding with Automatic Functionality Annotations from LLMs
items.summary: Infers element functionality from UI changes before and after interaction to produce verified annotations for grounding-model training.

items.name: ReachAgent: Enhancing Mobile Agent via Page Reaching and Operation
items.summary: Splits mobile tasks into reaching the required page and operating on it, using subtask data and preferred GUI trajectories for training.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)

items.name: MobileA3gent: Training Mobile GUI Agents Using Decentralized Self-Sourced Data from Diverse Users
items.summary: Studies automatic annotation and federated training of mobile GUI agents from decentralized user interaction data with heterogeneous distributions.

items.name: RWKV-UI: UI Understanding with Enhanced Perception and Reasoning
items.summary: RWKV-UI is a visual language model for high-resolution web interfaces that uses layout detection and reasoning-chain visual prompts to understand pages.

items.name: AppVLM: A Lightweight Vision Language Model for Online App Control
items.summary: AppVLM first learns app actions from AndroidControl and then refines its policy through data collected in AndroidWorld. The study compares offline action prediction and online task completion for a lightweight vision-language smartphone agent.

items.name: InSTA: Towards Internet-Scale Training For Agents
items.summary: InSTA builds a pipeline that creates website tasks, collects web-agent trajectories and filters them by judged success to train smaller web navigation agents.

items.name: Symbiotic Cooperation for Web Agents: Harnessing Complementary Strengths of Large and Small LLMs
items.summary: Couples large- and small-model web-agent exploration with trajectory synthesis and distillation to improve both model types iteratively.

items.name: Advancing Autonomous VLM Agents via Variational Subgoal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Uses variational subgoal-conditioned reinforcement learning to improve learning efficiency on sparse-reward mobile and web-control tasks.

items.name: WorldGUI: An Interactive Benchmark for Desktop GUI Automation from Any Starting Point
items.summary: Introduces desktop and web tasks with varied initial states to test planning recovery and adaptability beyond canonical starting configurations.

items.name: TRISHUL: Towards Region Identification and Screen Hierarchy Understanding for Large VLM based GUI Agents
items.summary: Combines hierarchical screen parsing with spatially enriched element descriptions to support both locating GUI targets and describing indicated elements.

items.name: Explorer: Scaling Exploration-driven Web Trajectory Synthesis for Multimodal Web Agents
items.summary: Synthesizes multimodal web trajectories through exploration and refinement, then trains a browser agent to study the effect of scaling interaction data.
items.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025

items.name: Scaling Autonomous Agents via Automatic Reward Modeling And Planning
items.summary: Introduces a framework that learns a reward model from agent trajectories to guide multi-step planning, with online shopping among its decision-making settings.

items.name: UXAgent: An LLM Agent-Based Usability Testing Framework for Web Design
items.summary: Introduces UXAgent, which uses simulated users and a browser connector to test website usability and present their actions, responses, and recordings to UX researchers.

items.name: Evaluating the Robustness of Multimodal Agents Against Active Environmental Injection Attacks
items.summary: Examines active environmental injection against mobile agents, testing whether adversarial interface content redirects decisions during task execution.

items.name: Magma: A Foundation Model for Multimodal AI Agents
items.summary: Introduces Magma, a multimodal agent model trained with labels for clickable GUI elements and video motion traces, and evaluated on UI navigation and robot tasks.

items.name: Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report
items.summary: Reports Qwen2.5-VL, a vision-language model that can act as a visual agent for tasks involving computer and mobile-device operation, alongside broader visual tasks.

items.name: PC-Agent: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Collaboration Framework for Complex Task Automation on PC
items.summary: Uses active perception and hierarchical agents for instruction decomposition, progress tracking, action selection, and reflection in PC workflows.

items.name: Advancing Language Multi-Agent Learning with Credit Re-Assignment for Interactive Environment Generalization
items.summary: Introduces CollabUIAgents, a multi-agent RL framework that assigns LLM-based process rewards to help agents generalize across interactive settings including mobile operations and web browsing.

items.name: Digi-Q: Learning Q-Value Functions for Training Device-Control Agents
items.summary: Learns action-value functions from offline device-control experience and uses them to rank candidate actions for policy improvement.

items.name: MobileSteward: Integrating Multiple App-Oriented Agents with Self-Evolution to Automate Cross-App Instructions
items.summary: Introduces MobileSteward, which coordinates app-specific phone agents, schedules cross-app tasks, and reuses successful experience; CAPBench evaluates cross-app instructions.

items.name: Mobile-Agent-V: A Video-Guided Approach for Effortless and Efficient Operational Knowledge Injection in Mobile Automation
items.summary: Extracts operational guidance from video for mobile task execution and introduces Mobile-Knowledge to evaluate the contribution of external knowledge.

items.name: Towards Sustainable Web Agents: A Plea for Transparency and Dedicated Metrics for Energy Consumption
items.summary: Examines energy and carbon-accounting limitations in web-agent evaluation and argues for transparent, dedicated sustainability measurements.

items.name: WebGames: Challenging General-Purpose Web-Browsing AI Agents
items.summary: Introduces WebGames, a browser-agent benchmark with 50+ interactive challenges in a self-contained test environment and verifiable solutions.

items.name: Programming with Pixels: Can Computer-Use Agents do Software Engineering?
items.summary: Introduces a visual IDE environment and benchmark for software-engineering tasks, comparing screenshot-based control with access to editing and shell tools.

items.name: VEM: Environment-Free Exploration for Training GUI Agent with Value Environment Model
items.summary: Trains GUI agents with a frozen value model learned from offline interactions, guiding action exploration without predicting complete next observations.

items.name: Why Are Web AI Agents More Vulnerable Than Standalone LLMs? A Security Analysis
items.summary: Analyzes web-agent vulnerabilities at the component level, examining goal placement in prompts, multistep action generation, and observations as sources of increased susceptibility.

items.name: Smoothing Grounding and Reasoning for MLLM-Powered GUI Agents with Query-Oriented Pivot Tasks
items.summary: Uses inference of possible user queries from screenshots and target coordinates as a training bridge between GUI grounding and action reasoning.

items.name: Towards Enterprise-Ready Computer Using Generalist Agent
items.summary: Describes the CUGA enterprise-agent development process, emphasizing iterative evaluation, failure analysis, and refinement on software-task benchmarks.

items.name: ATLaS: Agent Tuning via Learning Critical Steps
items.summary: Selects critical steps from expert interaction trajectories for targeted agent fine-tuning, studying efficiency and generalization across tasks.

items.name: AppAgentX: Evolving GUI Agents as Proficient Smartphone Users
items.summary: Records interaction history and converts repeated action sequences into reusable high-level shortcuts for mobile GUI tasks.

items.name: AutoEval: A Practical Framework for Autonomous Evaluation of Mobile Agents
items.summary: Generates reward signals from UI-state changes and uses a judging system to evaluate mobile agents with reduced manual evaluator construction.

items.name: MPO: Boosting LLM Agents with Meta Plan Optimization
items.summary: Refines reusable high-level meta plans with execution feedback to guide language-agent planning across interactive environments.

items.name: Language Models can Self-Improve at State-Value Estimation for Better Search
items.summary: Introduces Self-Taught Lookahead (STL), which trains a value model to predict actions and resulting states for more efficient search, with evaluation on web-agent tasks.

items.name: LiteWebAgent: The Open-Source Suite for VLM-Based Web-Agent Applications
items.summary: Introduces a modular visual web-agent stack with planning and memory components, exposed through a remote-browser application and Chrome extension.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (System Demonstrations)

items.name: SpiritSight Agent: Advanced GUI Agent with One Look
items.summary: Introduces SpiritSight and GUI-Lasagne data, combining multilevel GUI annotations with visual block parsing for high-resolution interface navigation.

items.name: CHOP: Mobile Operating Assistant with Constrained High-frequency Optimized Subtask Planning
items.summary: Uses human-planned subtasks to constrain and refine the intermediate plans connecting user goals with executable mobile operations.

items.name: WinClick: GUI Grounding with Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: Introduces a screenshot-based Windows GUI agent and the WinSpot benchmark for evaluating localization of actionable interface regions.

items.name: SafeArena: Evaluating the Safety of Autonomous Web Agents
items.summary: Pairs benign and harmful web tasks to assess deliberate misuse risks and categorize agent behavior by risk level.

items.name: FedMABench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents on Decentralized Heterogeneous User Data
items.summary: Introduces a benchmark for federated mobile-agent training under heterogeneous user and application distributions, combining datasets, algorithms, and base models.

items.name: Think Twice, Click Once: Enhancing GUI Grounding via Fast and Slow Systems
items.summary: Combines rapid target prediction with deliberate interface analysis, adaptively selecting the grounding process according to task complexity.

items.name: BEARCUBS: A benchmark for computer-using web agents
items.summary: BEARCUBS provides 111 live-web information-seeking questions with short answers and human-validated browsing trajectories. Its tasks require multimodal computer interaction, including video understanding and navigation of interactive 3D content.

items.name: In-Context Defense in Computer Agents: An Empirical Study
items.summary: Studies in-context defenses for computer agents exposed to misleading pop-ups and other environmental instructions. It examines defensive reasoning before action planning and how a small set of examples changes resistance to these attacks.

items.name: COLA: A Scalable Multi-Agent Framework For Windows UI Task Automation
items.summary: Coordinates specialized Windows UI agents with dynamic task scheduling, shared memory, and human-triggered rollback for recovering from errors.

items.name: Plan-and-Act: Improving Planning of Agents for Long-Horizon Tasks
items.summary: Separates planning from execution and creates synthetic plan annotations for training agents on extended web-navigation tasks.

items.name: AgentDAM: Privacy Leakage Evaluation for Autonomous Web Agents
items.summary: Evaluates whether autonomous web agents minimize use of sensitive personal information when completing tasks that expose unnecessary private data.

items.name: MIP against Agent: Malicious Image Patches Hijacking Multimodal OS Agents
items.summary: Studies Malicious Image Patches (MIPs), altered screen regions that can steer screenshot-based OS agents into harmful mouse and keyboard actions.

items.name: API Agents vs. GUI Agents: Divergence and Convergence
items.summary: Compares API-driven and GUI-driven agents across architecture, development, and interaction considerations, discussing when hybrid approaches are useful.

items.name: DeskVision: Large Scale Desktop Region Captioning for Advanced GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces AutoCaptioner, DeskVision, and GUIExplorer for generating desktop region descriptions and training interface-understanding models.

items.name: STEVE: A Step Verification Pipeline for Computer-use Agent Training
items.summary: Labels individual computer-use actions by comparing surrounding screenshots, then trains agents from both successful and unsuccessful steps.

items.name: WebNav: An Intelligent Agent for Voice-Controlled Web Navigation
items.summary: Introduces WebNav, a web navigation agent that turns natural-language commands into GUI actions using screenshot context, DOM labels, and separate LLMs for planning and action parameters.

items.name: MP-GUI: Modality Perception with MLLMs for GUI Understanding
items.summary: Uses specialized graphical, textual, and spatial perception components with a data-collection pipeline to improve GUI understanding.

items.name: Towards Computer-Using Personal Agents
items.summary: Proposes computer-using personal agents connected to user-controlled data repositories, discussing privacy, interoperability, and collaborative tasks.

items.name: UI-Vision: A Desktop-centric GUI Benchmark for Visual Perception and Interaction
items.summary: Provides annotated desktop demonstrations for evaluating element grounding, layout grounding, and action prediction.

items.name: Advancing Mobile GUI Agents: A Verifier-Driven Approach to Practical Deployment
items.summary: Introduces V-Droid, which verifies candidate actions in a discrete action space.

items.name: JARVIS-VLA: Post-Training Large-Scale Vision Language Models to Play Visual Games with Keyboards and Mouse
items.summary: Introduces Act from Visual Language Post-Training, a method for agents that follow instructions in Minecraft through visual input and actions, adjacent to interface operation.

items.name: OS-Kairos: Adaptive Interaction for MLLM-Powered GUI Agents
items.summary: Uses step-level confidence estimates to decide when a GUI agent should act autonomously or request human intervention in complex situations.

items.name: Does Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Help Mobile GUI Agent? An Empirical Study
items.summary: This study compares matched reasoning and non-reasoning vision-language models on static mobile GUI tasks and interactive AndroidWorld navigation. It finds that chain-of-thought effects vary across tasks and model families.

items.name: GUI-Xplore: Empowering Generalizable GUI Agents with One Exploration
items.summary: Introduces GUI-Xplore exploration videos and downstream tasks, with an agent that combines action-aware modeling and graph-based environment reasoning.

items.name: VeriSafe Agent: Safeguarding Mobile GUI Agent via Logic-based Action Verification
items.summary: Translates user instructions into formal specifications and applies runtime logic-based checks to proposed mobile GUI actions.

items.name: Agent-Initiated Interaction in Phone UI Automation
items.summary: Defines when phone agents should request user interaction and introduces AndroidInteraction annotations for deciding whether and how to engage the user.

items.name: Agents in the Sandbox: End-to-End Crash Bug Reproduction for Minecraft
items.summary: Introduces BugCraft, which turns Minecraft crash reports into steps and has a vision-based agent execute them through a macro API; BugCraft-Bench supports evaluation.

items.name: sudo rm -rf agentic_security
items.summary: Evaluates security failures of computer-use agents under adversarial requests and screen-context manipulation. The study examines refusal behavior while agents perform tasks in desktop and web environments.

items.name: ScreenLLM: Stateful Screen Schema for Efficient Action Understanding and Prediction
items.summary: Represents interface interactions with a stateful screen schema to model user behavior and support action understanding and prediction.

items.name: UI-R1: Enhancing Efficient Action Prediction of GUI Agents by Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Uses rule-based action rewards and policy optimization to train GUI action prediction from a compact set of mobile tasks.

items.name: ShieldAgent: Shielding Agents via Verifiable Safety Policy Reasoning
items.summary: Proposes a guardrail agent that reasons over explicit safety policies and checks action trajectories, with a web-agent safety benchmark.

items.name: A Survey of WebAgents: Towards Next-Generation AI Agents for Web Automation with Large Foundation Models
items.summary: Surveys foundation-model web agents through their architectures, training methods and trustworthiness. It organizes research on completing browser tasks from user instructions and identifies directions for further development.

items.name: Towards Trustworthy GUI Agents: A Survey
items.summary: Frames GUI-agent trustworthiness as an execution gap and reviews failures, attacks, and defenses across perception, reasoning, and interaction.

items.name: Navi-plus: Managing Ambiguous GUI Navigation Tasks with Follow-up Questions
items.summary: Navi-plus evaluates GUI agents that ask follow-up questions to complete ambiguous user instructions. It provides GUI clarification question-answer pairs and Dual-Stream Trajectory Evaluation for this interactive setting.

items.name: Agent S2: A Compositional Generalist-Specialist Framework for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Combines generalist and specialist models with hierarchical planning and multiple grounding methods for computer-use tasks.

items.name: An Illusion of Progress? Assessing the Current State of Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces Online-Mind2Web, with 300 tasks across 136 live websites, and examines how benchmark design affects assessments of web agents. It also develops an LLM judge for task completion and compares its judgments with human evaluation.

items.name: Are Autonomous Web Agents Good Testers?
items.summary: Adapts web agents to execute natural-language test steps, verify assertions, and issue test verdicts. The study introduces 113 passing and failing test cases across three offline web applications and compares two agent implementations with qualitative failure analysis.

items.name: ReuseDroid: A VLM-empowered Android UI Test Migrator Boosted by Active Feedback
items.summary: ReuseDroid migrates Android GUI tests between functionally similar apps using VLM agents that separate shared test intent from app-specific interaction flows. It introduces LinPro, a dataset of 578 migration tasks across 39 apps, to evaluate test transfer.

items.name: On the Robustness of GUI Grounding Models Against Image Attacks
items.summary: Evaluates GUI grounding models under natural image noise, untargeted adversarial perturbations, and targeted image attacks. Experiments cover mobile, desktop, and web interfaces and analyze sensitivity to image resolution and adversarial changes.

items.name: Inducing Programmatic Skills for Agentic Tasks
items.summary: Introduces agent skill induction (ASI), which creates, checks, and reuses program-based skills for web tasks by combining primitive actions into higher-level routines.

items.name: SkillWeaver: Web Agents can Self-Improve by Discovering and Honing Skills
items.summary: SkillWeaver explores websites, practices interactions, and converts the resulting experience into a reusable library of callable skill APIs. Its WebArena and live-website experiments examine skill refinement, composition, and transfer from stronger agents to weaker ones.

items.name: Kimi-VL Technical Report
items.summary: Presents Kimi-VL, a general vision-language model evaluated on multi-turn agent tasks including OSWorld and on ScreenSpot-Pro alongside other vision-language tasks.

items.name: ScreenSpot-Pro: GUI Grounding for Professional High-Resolution Computer Use
items.summary: Evaluates GUI target localization in high-resolution professional software and studies cascaded visual search to narrow the target region.

items.name: AgentRewardBench: Evaluating Automatic Evaluations of Web Agent Trajectories
items.summary: AgentRewardBench evaluates automated web-agent judges against expert reviews of 1,302 trajectories from five benchmarks. The annotations cover completion, side effects, and repetition, enabling comparison of LLM judges and rule-based task evaluators.

items.name: Explorer: Robust Collection of Interactable GUI Elements
items.summary: Explorer collects interactable GUI elements from a live target application and records user sessions for application-specific model training. It links repeated interface states into a navigation map that supports path planning and voice-directed interaction.

items.name: AgentA/B: Automated and Scalable Web A/BTesting with Interactive LLM Agents
items.summary: Introduces AgentA/B, which uses persona-based LLM agents to navigate real webpages and perform shopping interactions for simulated web A/B tests.

items.name: Breaking the Data Barrier -- Building GUI Agents Through Task Generalization
items.summary: Studies whether mid-training on GUI perception, multimodal reasoning, and text reasoning transfers to GUI-agent planning. Experiments compare 11 task sources and curated mixtures using WebArena and AndroidWorld to investigate training-data choices when GUI trajectories are scarce.

items.name: RealWebAssist: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Web Assistance with Real-World Users
items.summary: RealWebAssist evaluates web assistance through sequences of instructions collected from real users across multiple websites. It tests intent interpretation, user-specific routines, long-term context, and visual grounding when instructions are ambiguous or evolve during interaction.

items.name: GUI-R1 : A Generalist R1-Style Vision-Language Action Model For GUI Agents
items.summary: Applies reinforcement fine-tuning with unified action rules and curated cross-platform examples to vision-language GUI agents.

items.name: UI-E2I-Synth: Advancing GUI Grounding with Large-Scale Instruction Synthesis
items.summary: UI-E2I-Synth uses GPT-4o to synthesize GUI grounding instructions with varied complexity, addressing small elements, imbalanced element types, and implicit requests. The accompanying UI-I2E-Bench evaluates instruction-to-element localization across these annotation challenges.
items.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025

items.name: The Obvious Invisible Threat: LLM-Powered GUI Agents' Vulnerability to Fine-Print Injections
items.summary: Characterizes six forms of GUI-content injection and studies their effects on GUI agents and human users using adversarial webpages. The analysis examines privacy failures and the limits of human oversight.

items.name: REAL: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Deterministic Simulations of Real Websites
items.summary: Introduces REAL, a benchmark of deterministic website replicas with 112 tasks covering information retrieval and state-changing browser actions.

items.name: VLM-Fuzz: Vision Language Model Assisted Recursive Depth-first Search Exploration for Effective UI Testing of Android Apps
items.summary: VLM-Fuzz combines depth-first UI exploration with Android manifest analysis, runtime widget hierarchies, and on-demand visual reasoning to generate app test inputs. It evaluates coverage on 59 benchmark apps and uses additional Google Play apps to study crash discovery.

items.name: WebRollback: Enhancing Web Agents with Explicit Rollback Mechanisms
items.summary: WebRollback gives a web agent an explicit action for returning to an earlier state in its navigation trajectory. It studies this recovery mechanism on two live web-navigation benchmarks under both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings.

items.name: TongUI: Internet-Scale Trajectories from Multimodal Web Tutorials for Generalized GUI Agents
items.summary: TongUI converts multimodal online tutorials, including videos and articles, into GUI-agent trajectories. Its GUI-Net dataset contains 143,000 trajectories spanning five operating systems and more than 200 applications, and supports fine-tuning for grounding and navigation.

items.name: WebLists: Extracting Structured Information From Complex Interactive Websites Using Executable LLM Agents
items.summary: Introduces WebLists, a benchmark for structured extraction from interactive websites, and BardeenAgent, which turns web-agent runs into replayable CSS-selector programs.

items.name: LearnAct: Few-Shot Mobile GUI Agent with a Unified Demonstration Benchmark
items.summary: LearnAct parses human demonstrations into reusable knowledge, retrieves relevant examples, and uses them during mobile GUI task execution. The accompanying LearnGUI benchmark includes 2,252 offline tasks and 101 online tasks for studying adaptation from demonstrations.

items.name: A Survey on (M)LLM-Based GUI Agents
items.summary: Analyzes LLM-based GUI agents through four components (perception, exploration, planning, and interaction) and the methods used to evaluate them.

items.name: ViMo: A Generative Visual GUI World Model for App Agents
items.summary: ViMo predicts the next mobile-app screenshot after a candidate action by separately modeling graphics and text. A symbolic placeholder representation preserves layout while a second predictor supplies readable text, enabling visual lookahead for GUI-agent planning.

items.name: DoomArena: A framework for Testing AI Agents Against Evolving Security Threats
items.summary: Presents a modular security testing framework that plugs into BrowserGym and tool-use benchmarks to evaluate agents under configurable threat models.

items.name: InfiGUI-R1: Advancing Multimodal GUI Agents from Reactive Actors to Deliberative Reasoners
items.summary: Uses a staged reasoning-focused training framework to move GUI agents from reactive actions toward deliberative planning and recovery.

items.name: UFO2: The Desktop AgentOS
items.summary: Introduces UFO2, a Windows desktop agent architecture combining a coordinating HostAgent, application-specialized agents, and a shared GUI/API action layer. It integrates UI Automation, visual parsing, speculative planning, and an isolated picture-in-picture desktop.

items.name: Guiding VLM Agents with Process Rewards at Inference Time for GUI Navigation
items.summary: Guides visual GUI agents at inference time with a process-reward model that evaluates intermediate actions. It combines stepwise guidance with trajectory reflection and retry mechanisms in static and interactive navigation tasks.

items.name: PixelWeb: The First Web GUI Dataset with Pixel-Wise Labels
items.summary: Introduces PixelWeb, a webpage GUI dataset with element images, contours, and pixel masks. Its annotation pipeline combines bitmap channel information with DOM-based visibility and stacking analysis to address occlusion and overlapping elements.

items.name: Toward a Human-Centered Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy LLM-Powered GUI Agents
items.summary: Presents a position paper on privacy and security evaluation for GUI agents, identifying risk categories and challenges in involving human evaluators. It proposes risk-aware assessment and in-context consent as design directions.

items.name: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
items.summary: Introduces WASP, an end-to-end benchmark for prompt-injection security in web agents. Its evaluation separates partial attack progress from completion of the attacker’s full objective.

items.name: LLM-Powered GUI Agents in Phone Automation: Surveying Progress and Prospects
items.summary: Reviews LLM-driven phone GUI agents with a taxonomy of agent frameworks, prompt- and training-based modeling, datasets, and benchmarks.

items.name: A Survey on GUI Agents with Foundation Models Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Formalizes GUI tasks as Markov decision processes and traces agent training from prompting through supervised fine-tuning to reinforcement learning.

items.name: WebEvolver: Enhancing Web Agent Self-Improvement with Coevolving World Model
items.summary: WebEvolver trains a co-evolving world model to predict web observations and generate additional agent-training trajectories. The same model supports look-ahead action selection at inference, with evaluation on live web-task benchmarks.

items.name: WebThinker: Empowering Large Reasoning Models with Deep Research Capability
items.summary: Combines iterative web search and link-following with interleaved reasoning and report drafting for deep research. Its reported web explorer retrieves page content through a crawler.

items.name: ScaleTrack: Scaling and back-tracking Automated GUI Agents
items.summary: ScaleTrack combines a unified collection of GUI grounding samples with a planning objective that predicts the next action while reconstructing prior actions. This backward prediction links the current screenshot to interaction history during agent training.

items.name: Visual Test-time Scaling for GUI Agent Grounding
items.summary: RegionFocus adds visual test-time scaling by zooming into selected screenshot regions and maintaining an image-based map of landmarks and actions. It evaluates this grounding procedure with UI-TARS and Qwen2.5-VL on ScreenSpot-Pro and WebVoyager.

items.name: OSUniverse: Benchmark for Multimodal GUI-navigation AI Agents
items.summary: Introduces OSUniverse, a desktop GUI benchmark spanning precise clicks through multistep and multiapplication tasks. It provides both manual scoring and an automated validation mechanism.

items.name: WebGen-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Generating Interactive and Functional Websites from Scratch
items.summary: Introduces WebGen-Bench for evaluating agents that generate multi-file websites, using a web-navigation agent to check whether the resulting pages pass interaction tests.

items.name: Do MLLMs Capture How Interfaces Guide User Behavior? A Benchmark for Multimodal UI/UX Design Understanding
items.summary: Introduces WiserUI-Bench, pairing real UI variants from industry A/B tests with observed behavioral winners and expert explanations. It evaluates models’ ability to predict the more effective interface and explain its effect on user behavior.

items.name: EcoAgent: An Efficient Device-Cloud Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework for Mobile Automation
items.summary: EcoAgent splits mobile automation between cloud planning and on-device observation and verification. Compact screen descriptions and feedback reduce communication costs, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.

items.name: AgentVigil: Generic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
items.summary: Introduces AgentVigil, a black-box fuzzing framework for finding indirect prompt injections against LLM agents, including attacks that redirect web navigation.

items.name: Leveraging Vision-Language Models for Visual Grounding and Analysis of Automotive UI
items.summary: Introduces AutomotiveUI-Bench-4K and a fine-tuned vision-language model for locating elements and evaluating automotive infotainment interfaces.

items.name: Seed1.5-VL Technical Report
items.summary: Reports Seed1.5-VL, a general vision-language model evaluated on GUI control and gameplay alongside visual understanding and reasoning tasks.

items.name: Characterizing Unintended Consequences in Human-GUI Agent Collaboration for Web Browsing
items.summary: Studies unintended consequences of collaborative web browsing with GUI agents through social-media analysis and interviews. It organizes observed failures, user impacts, and mitigation practices around planning, interface interaction, feedback, privacy, and trust.

items.name: LLM-Explorer: Towards Efficient and Affordable LLM-based Exploration for Mobile Apps
items.summary: LLM-Explorer uses language models to maintain compact knowledge for mobile app exploration, then generates actions without invoking the model at every step. The study compares exploration coverage and cost across twenty apps.

items.name: Creating General User Models from Computer Use
items.summary: Proposes general user models that turn computer-use observations into confidence-weighted propositions and revise them as new context arrives. Demonstrations use this memory to contextualize assistants, manage notifications, and support proactive actions across apps.

items.name: InfantAgent-Next: A Multimodal Generalist Agent for Automated Computer Interaction
items.summary: Introduces InfantAgent-Next, a modular multimodal computer agent that combines tool-based and vision agents for stepwise tasks, with evaluation on OSWorld and other benchmarks.

items.name: A Survey on the Safety and Security Threats of Computer-Using Agents: JARVIS or Ultron?
items.summary: Systematizes safety and security threats to computer-using agents, with taxonomies of threats and defensive strategies.

items.name: Group-in-Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
items.summary: Introduces Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO), an RL method for assigning step-level credit in multi-turn agents, evaluated on WebShop among other tasks.

items.name: WebInject: Prompt Injection Attack to Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces WebInject, a prompt-injection attack that optimizes rendered webpage pixels to make screenshot-based web agents take attacker-chosen actions.

items.name: Mobile-Bench-v2: A More Realistic and Comprehensive Benchmark for VLM-based Mobile Agents
items.summary: Mobile-Bench-v2 evaluates mobile GUI agents using multiple acceptable offline action paths, noisy interfaces with ads or pop-ups, and ambiguous instructions with scripted clarification exchanges. These splits separate step-level execution, robustness, and proactive interaction.
items.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations

items.name: MobileIPL: Enhancing Mobile Agents Thinking Process via Iterative Preference Learning
items.summary: MobileIPL samples trees of action-planning thoughts, propagates rule-based leaf rewards backward, and forms preference pairs for reasoning-level optimization. It also expands screenshot-based instruction data through staged evolution before evaluation on mobile GUI-agent benchmarks.

items.name: Enhancing Visual Grounding for GUI Agents via Self-Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Proposes GUI grounding training that combines curated seed examples, continuous location-dependent policy feedback, and iterative refinement guided by attention maps. The study evaluates the resulting reinforcement-learning procedure on three grounding benchmarks, including ScreenSpot-Pro.

items.name: GUI-Shift: Enhancing VLM-Based GUI Agents through Self-supervised Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: GUI-Shift trains an inverse-dynamics task that predicts the initial action connecting two GUI states, using trajectories without natural-language instructions. It combines rule-based reinforcement learning with data filtering and evaluates transfer to Android automation and screenshot grounding.

items.name: Scalable Video-to-Dataset Generation for Cross-Platform Mobile Agents
items.summary: Introduces MONDAY and an automated pipeline that extracts mobile-navigation training data from instructional videos across operating-system platforms.

items.name: GEM: Gaussian Embedding Modeling for Out-of-Distribution Detection in GUI Agents
items.summary: GEM detects instructions outside a GUI agent’s capabilities by modeling distances in its input-embedding space with a Gaussian mixture. Experiments across mobile, computer and browser data also examine selective escalation to a cloud model when an input is detected as unfamiliar.

items.name: From Assistants to Adversaries: Exploring the Security Risks of Mobile LLM Agents
items.summary: Analyzes security vulnerabilities across OEM system-level, third-party, and research mobile LLM agents, covering GUI and cross-application attack surfaces.

items.name: The Hidden Dangers of Browsing AI Agents
items.summary: Outlines an end-to-end threat model and empirical security evaluation across architectural layers of autonomous browser agents.

items.name: Scaling Computer-Use Grounding via User Interface Decomposition and Synthesis
items.summary: Introduces OSWorld-G grounding evaluation and the Jedi synthesis pipeline for examples spanning layout reasoning and fine-grained interaction.

items.name: Efficient Agent Training for Computer Use
items.summary: PC Agent-E augments 312 human computer-use trajectories with alternative action decisions synthesized by Claude 3.7 Sonnet. It studies training with this combination and introduces WindowsAgentArena-V2 as an updated evaluation benchmark.

items.name: Building a Stable Planner: An Extended Finite State Machine Based Planning Module for Mobile GUI Agent
items.summary: SPlanner models mobile-app functions and configurations with extended finite-state machines, traverses them to construct execution paths, and converts those paths into natural-language plans. A VLM follows these plans to perform GUI actions, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.

items.name: EVA: Evolving Semantic Adversaries for Red-Teaming GUI Agents Against Environmental Injection Attacks
items.summary: Introduces EVA, a red-teaming framework that evolves semantic payloads for GUI environmental-injection tests. It studies the contribution of semantic versus visual deception and distills discovered patterns into reusable evaluation rules.

items.name: Hidden Ghost Hand: Unveiling Backdoor Vulnerabilities in MLLM-Powered Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: Studies backdoor risks in mobile GUI agents through AgentGhost, which combines goal-level and interaction-history triggers during model training. The paper evaluates multiple mobile agents and a tailored defense.

items.name: MedBrowseComp: Benchmarking Medical Deep Research and Computer Use
items.summary: Introduces MedBrowseComp, a benchmark of human-curated, multi-hop medical questions for agents retrieving and synthesizing facts from live knowledge bases in a computer-use setting.

items.name: ReGUIDE: Data Efficient GUI Grounding via Spatial Reasoning and Search
items.summary: Combines self-generated localization reasoning, spatial consistency checks, and inference-time search to improve data-efficient web grounding.

items.name: Web-Shepherd: Advancing PRMs for Reinforcing Web Agents
items.summary: Web-Shepherd is a process reward model for assessing individual steps of web-navigation trajectories. It introduces a collection of 40,000 step-level preference pairs with checklists and a separate benchmark for comparing reward models, then evaluates verification during WebArena-lite navigation.

items.name: GUI-G1: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
items.summary: Analyzes reasoning templates, reward design, and policy updates in GUI grounding, then proposes targeted adjustments to the training process.

items.name: AutoData: A Multi-Agent System for Open Web Data Collection
items.summary: Introduces AutoData, a multi-agent system that collects web datasets from a natural-language request, and Instruct2DS, a benchmark for live collection across three domains.

items.name: ARPO:End-to-End Policy Optimization for GUI Agents with Experience Replay
items.summary: ARPO extends group-relative policy optimization with a replay buffer that reuses successful GUI trajectories across training iterations. It filters tasks using baseline performance and compares end-to-end reinforcement learning with offline preference optimization on OSWorld.

items.name: WebAgent-R1: Training Web Agents via End-to-End Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Trains web agents through asynchronous multi-turn environment interaction, using task-success rewards to optimize complete trajectories.

items.name: Unlocking Smarter Device Control: Foresighted Planning with a World Model-Driven Code Execution Approach
items.summary: FPWC builds and refines a task-oriented world model before planning mobile-device actions. It executes plans as code and evaluates the approach in simulated environments and on real mobile devices.

items.name: GUI-explorer: Autonomous Exploration and Mining of Transition-aware Knowledge for GUI Agent
items.summary: GUI-explorer generates exploration goals from screenshots and interface structure, then mines observation-action-outcome triples for app-specific transition knowledge. The resulting training-free agent uses this knowledge during mobile task execution, evaluated on SPA-Bench and AndroidWorld.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

items.name: TransBench: Breaking Barriers for Transferable Graphical User Interface Agents in Dynamic Digital Environments
items.summary: Introduces TransBench to evaluate GUI grounding transfer across app versions, iOS, Android, Web, and functionally distinct applications.

items.name: Automated Testing of the GUI of a Real-Life Engineering Software using Large Language Models
items.summary: GERALLT uses LLMs to explore the GUI of engineering software and produce a list of confusing or inconsistent interface areas for developers to inspect.
items.venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation Workshops (ICSTW)

items.name: ProgRM: Build Better GUI Agents with Progress Rewards
items.summary: ProgRM predicts per-step task completion progress to provide intermediate rewards during online GUI-agent training. It derives progress labels by using longest common subsequences to identify key trajectory steps, allowing useful partial progress to contribute even when a trajectory ultimately fails.

items.name: LiteCUA: Computer as MCP Server for Computer-Use Agent on AIOS
items.summary: AIOS 1.0 exposes computer states and actions through an MCP server to provide structured environmental context for agents. LiteCUA is a lightweight agent built on this interface, evaluated on OSWorld to study the effect of computer-environment contextualization.

items.name: ScreenExplorer: Training a Vision-Language Model for Diverse Exploration in Open GUI World
items.summary: Trains ScreenExplorer with reinforcement learning in dynamic GUI environments, using a world-model curiosity reward and experience-stream distillation to support sustained exploration.

items.name: ScienceBoard: Evaluating Multimodal Autonomous Agents in Realistic Scientific Workflows
items.summary: ScienceBoard combines an interactive environment with professional scientific software and 169 human-curated tasks in areas including biochemistry, astronomy, and geoinformatics. It evaluates computer-use agents on visually rich research workflows and analyzes their execution limitations.

items.name: WebCoT: Enhancing Web Agent Reasoning by Reconstructing Chain-of-Thought in Reflection, Branching, and Rollback
items.summary: WebCoT turns reflection, look-ahead, branching and rollback procedures into chain-of-thought training rationales. Fine-tuning on these reconstructed trajectories is evaluated for web-agent self-improvement and transfer across navigation tasks.

items.name: Training LLM-Based Agents with Synthetic Self-Reflected Trajectories and Partial Masking
items.summary: Introduces STeP, which trains agents on synthetic trajectories containing error reflections and corrections while masking poor steps; WebShop is one of three evaluated tasks.

items.name: BacktrackAgent: Enhancing GUI Agent with Error Detection and Backtracking Mechanism
items.summary: BacktrackAgent adds verification, judgment, and reflection modules to detect erroneous GUI actions and guide recovery. It develops backtracking-oriented training data that includes post-action pages and evaluates task completion and step accuracy on Mobile3M and Auto-UI.

items.name: SPA-RL: Reinforcing LLM Agents via Stepwise Progress Attribution
items.summary: Introduces SPA, a reward redistribution method for multi-step LLM agents that estimates each action’s contribution to task completion; Webshop is among its evaluations.

items.name: XBOUND: Exploring Capability Boundaries of Device-Control Agents at the State Level
items.summary: XBOUND evaluates GUI agents at the level of a screen state, considering multiple instructions and possible target actions within it. The study separates action matching from instruction unification and compares effects of grounding and trajectory data.

items.name: UI-Genie: A Self-Improving Approach for Iteratively Boosting MLLM-based Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: UI-Genie jointly improves a mobile GUI agent and a reward model that processes screenshots with interaction history and supplies action- and task-level feedback. Its data pipeline uses rule-based verification, corrupted trajectories, and hard negatives to support reward-guided exploration and iterative training.

items.name: AdInject: Real-World Black-Box Attacks on Web Agents via Advertising Delivery
items.summary: Studies advertising delivery as an indirect-injection channel for web agents under a black-box threat model. AdInject evaluates how static ad content shaped by website context can redirect browser actions.

items.name: RedTeamCUA: Realistic Adversarial Testing of Computer-Use Agents in Hybrid Web-OS Environments
items.summary: RedTeamCUA combines a virtual-machine OS environment with containerized websites for controlled prompt-injection tests spanning both interfaces. Its RTC-Bench contains 864 examples and can initialize agents at injection points to separate attack susceptibility from navigation failures.

items.name: UI-Evol: Automatic Knowledge Evolving for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces UI-Evol, which extracts action sequences from agent interactions and critiques external guidance against those traces. Evaluation on OSWorld examines how revised operational knowledge affects execution and behavioral consistency.

items.name: WorkForceAgent-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLM-based Web Agents via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Uses rule-based rewards for output structure and action correctness to train reasoning for enterprise web navigation.

items.name: Agent-SAMA: State-Aware Mobile Assistant
items.summary: Models mobile application execution as a finite-state machine to support planning, verification, and recovery across interface transitions.

items.name: Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Visual Reasoning
items.summary: Introduces ViGoRL, a visual reasoning model trained to reference image coordinates and zoom during reasoning; its evaluations include GUI element localization.

items.name: ZeroGUI: Automating Online GUI Learning at Zero Human Cost
items.summary: Combines generated tasks, estimated success rewards, and online reinforcement learning to automate GUI-agent interaction training.

items.name: VideoCAD: A Dataset and Model for Learning Long-Horizon 3D CAD UI Interactions from Video
items.summary: Introduces synthetic CAD interaction videos, a model for learning interface actions from video, and evaluation tasks for spatial and long-horizon reasoning.

items.name: Agent-X: Evaluating Deep Multimodal Reasoning in Vision-Centric Agentic Tasks
items.summary: Introduces Agent-X, a benchmark of multi-step visual reasoning and tool use with step-level grading across six settings, including web browsing.

items.name: Open CaptchaWorld: A Comprehensive Web-based Platform for Testing and Benchmarking Multimodal LLM Agents
items.summary: Open CaptchaWorld evaluates multimodal agents on interactive browser-based CAPTCHA puzzles. Its benchmark distinguishes task success from the depth of visual reasoning and interaction needed to complete a puzzle.

items.name: ResTest: Targeted Coverage of Residual Not-Covered Code Using Large Language Models for Web GUI Testing
items.summary: Introduces ResTest, which uses coverage reports and a state transition graph to infer untested web functions, then directs a GUI agent to execute them.

items.name: RiOSWorld: Benchmarking the Risk of Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces RiOSWorld, a computer-use risk benchmark separating user-originated and environmental threats. It evaluates both risky-goal intent and goal completion across web and other computer applications.

items.name: AgentCPM-GUI: Building Mobile-Use Agents with Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Combines grounding pretraining, bilingual interaction trajectories, and reinforcement fine-tuning for mobile GUI actions.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing: System Demonstrations

items.name: FormFactory: An Interactive Benchmarking Suite for Multimodal Form-Filling Agents
items.summary: Introduces FormFactory, an interactive web-based benchmark for agents filling online forms, with varied field formats and evaluation of instruction-to-field alignment.

items.name: MLA-Trust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of Multimodal LLM Agents in GUI Environments
items.summary: Benchmarks truthfulness, controllability, safety, and privacy of multimodal LLM agents across interactive web and mobile GUI tasks.

items.name: WebChoreArena: Evaluating Web Browsing Agents on Realistic Tedious Web Tasks
items.summary: Introduces WebChoreArena, 532 web chores built on WebArena environments to evaluate agents’ retention of page information, calculation, and tracking across pages.

items.name: VPI-Bench: Visual Prompt Injection Attacks for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces VPI-Bench, interactive web-platform variants containing visually embedded malicious instructions. It evaluates computer-use and browser-use agents under these threats and examines system-prompt defenses.

items.name: VerificAgent: Domain-Specific Memory Verification for Scalable Oversight of Aligned Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces VerificAgent, which grows domain-specific memories from task trajectories and subjects them to human fact-checking before deployment. Its OSWorld evaluation treats persistent memory as an auditable constraint on later agent behavior.

items.name: DeepShop: A Benchmark for Deep Research Shopping Agents
items.summary: DeepShop evaluates shopping agents with evolving query complexity across product attributes, filters and sorting preferences. Its evaluation combines checks of these individual requirements with overall task success.

items.name: Surfer-H Meets Holo1: Cost-Efficient Web Agent Powered by Open Weights
items.summary: Describes Surfer-H, a web agent paired with the Holo1 vision-language model family trained on web content, synthetic examples, and agent-generated data. The work introduces WebClick for web-interface localization and evaluates browser task execution on WebVoyager.

items.name: DPO Learning with LLMs-Judge Signal for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Uses an LLM judge to evaluate and filter synthetic GUI interaction trajectories for training a compact vision-language agent. OSWorld experiments assess the policy designed for local execution.

items.name: GUI-Actor: Coordinate-Free Visual Grounding for GUI Agents
items.summary: Uses an attention-based action head and a verifier to select relevant screen regions without generating coordinates as text.

items.name: Go-Browse: Training Web Agents with Structured Exploration
items.summary: Go-Browse frames web-environment exploration as graph search so that information can be reused across data-collection episodes. It collects 10,000 successful trajectories and 40,000 interaction steps on WebArena and uses them to fine-tune a web agent.

items.name: MiMo-VL Technical Report
items.summary: Reports MiMo-VL-7B-SFT and MiMo-VL-7B-RL, general vision-language models trained with staged pre-training and mixed RL, with GUI grounding evaluated on OSWorld-G.

items.name: macOSWorld: A Multilingual Interactive Benchmark for GUI Agents
items.summary: macOSWorld provides 202 interactive tasks across 30 applications, with instructions and operating-system interfaces in five languages. It evaluates GUI agents on macOS workflows and includes a separate subset for deception-attack testing.

items.name: Look Before You Leap: A GUI-Critic-R1 Model for Pre-Operative Error Diagnosis in GUI Automation
items.summary: Uses a pre-execution critic and reinforcement training to evaluate proposed GUI actions and provide corrective suggestions before execution.

items.name: Scenario-Guided LLM-based Mobile App GUI Testing
items.summary: ScenGen organizes mobile GUI testing around business scenarios. Five collaborating agents observe the interface, choose and execute actions, check scenario completion, and record operations and runtime bugs.

items.name: Deep Research Bench: Evaluating AI Web Research Agents
items.summary: Introduces Deep Research Bench, 89 multi-step web research tasks and a frozen collection of scraped pages for evaluating search agents and their traces over time.

items.name: BIMgent: Towards Autonomous Building Modeling via Computer-use Agents
items.summary: BIMgent plans software-specific workflows and executes GUI actions for building-information modeling. It evaluates multimodal building design and reconstruction tasks in professional authoring software.

items.name: GUIPilot: A Consistency-based Mobile GUI Testing Approach for Detecting Application-specific Bugs
items.summary: Introduces GUIPilot, which compares mobile design mock-ups with implemented screens through widget alignment and tests expected transitions by executing inferred UI actions. It evaluates both visual inconsistencies and workflow-specific bugs.

items.name: MCPWorld: A Unified Benchmarking Testbed for API, GUI, and Hybrid Computer Use Agents
items.summary: MCPWorld evaluates API, GUI, and hybrid computer-use agents with 201 tasks in applications whose source can be instrumented and extended with MCP support. It verifies completion from application behavior and packages the testbed in containers with GPU support.

items.name: Thinking vs. Doing: Agents that Reason by Scaling Test-Time Interaction
items.summary: Test-Time Interaction scales the interaction horizon so web agents can explore, backtrack and revise plans within a rollout. Its online reinforcement-learning curriculum adjusts rollout lengths and is evaluated on WebVoyager and WebArena.

items.name: GUI-Reflection: Empowering Multimodal GUI Models with Self-Reflection Behavior
items.summary: GUI-Reflection synthesizes reflection and error-correction examples from successful trajectories and adds dedicated learning stages for these behaviors. It introduces a reflection task suite, a mobile environment for online data collection, and iterative reflection tuning.

items.name: EconWebArena: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Economic Tasks in Realistic Web Environments
items.summary: Introduces EconWebArena, a curated benchmark of economic-data tasks requiring live website navigation, multimodal interpretation, and precise extraction. It evaluates visual grounding, planning, and interaction design within multistep workflows.

items.name: Atomic-to-Compositional Generalization for Mobile Agents with A New Benchmark and Scheduling System
items.summary: UI-NEXUS evaluates compositional mobile tasks in local utility apps and online Chinese and English service apps. AGENT-NEXUS decomposes those long tasks into self-contained atomic subtasks to study generalization beyond isolated screens or short action chains.

items.name: LPO: Towards Accurate GUI Agent Interaction via Location Preference Optimization
items.summary: Location Preference Optimization uses an information-entropy signal to select interaction regions and a distance-based reward to assess click locations. It trains GUI localization through preference optimization and evaluates both offline grounding and online interaction.

items.name: Mirage-1: Augmenting and Updating GUI Agent with Hierarchical Multimodal Skills
items.summary: Mirage-1 organizes interaction trajectories into execution, core, and meta-skills, then uses them to guide Monte Carlo tree search during online GUI tasks. It introduces AndroidLH for long-horizon evaluation and tests the approach on Android and web-navigation benchmarks.

items.name: Build the web for agents, not agents for the web
items.summary: Proposes Agentic Web Interface (AWI), a website interface intended for agent navigation, and sets out six design principles for web-agent use.

items.name: UITron-Speech: Towards Automated GUI Agents Based on Speech Instructions
items.summary: Introduces UITron-Speech, which predicts GUI actions from spoken instructions and screenshots. It combines synthetic speech data and mixed-modality training with a training-free grounding refinement step.

items.name: Poison Once, Control Anywhere: Clean-Text Visual Backdoors in VLM-based Mobile Agents
items.summary: Demonstrates clean-text visual backdoor attacks (VIBMA) that compromise fine-tuned VLM mobile agents through visual triggers while keeping text instructions intact.

items.name: FormGym: Doing Paperwork with Agents
items.summary: Introduces FormGym, a benchmark for filling image-only forms, and FieldFinder, a tool that helps LLMs locate where to place text on those forms.

items.name: AgentSynth: Scalable Task Generation for Generalist Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: AgentSynth composes easily generated subtasks into longer computer-use tasks and trajectories with adjustable difficulty. Its evaluation uses the number of subtasks to probe how agent success changes as task complexity grows.

items.name: GUI-Robust: A Comprehensive Dataset for Testing GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
items.summary: Builds GUI task data with real-world interaction anomalies and evaluates how agent behavior changes under those conditions.

items.name: OS-Harm: A Benchmark for Measuring Safety of Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Extends OSWorld with tasks covering user misuse, prompt injection, and model misbehavior, with assessment of both task success and safety.

items.name: Understanding GUI Agent Localization Biases through Logit Sharpness
items.summary: Introduces a finer-grained taxonomy of GUI localization errors and a logit-based Peak Sharpness Score for analyzing coordinate-prediction uncertainty. A context-aware cropping method refines the visual input without retraining the grounding model.

items.name: Embodied Web Agents: Bridging Physical-Digital Realms for Integrated Agent Intelligence
items.summary: Introduces environments that couple 3D physical-world simulations with functional web interfaces. The accompanying benchmark evaluates tasks requiring agents to coordinate online information and physical actions across cooking, navigation and shopping scenarios.

items.name: OSWorld-Human: Benchmarking the Efficiency of Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: OSWorld-Human adds human-determined trajectories to OSWorld to evaluate the efficiency of desktop computer-use agents. The study compares 16 agents and analyzes model-call latency, changes in step duration during task execution, and excess action steps.

items.name: Context manipulation attacks : Web agents are susceptible to corrupted memory
items.summary: Studies context manipulation in web agents by altering stored task representations. Evaluation on Browser-use and Agent-E examines memory-directed attacks and the implications for secure context handling.

items.name: Learning, Reasoning, Refinement: A Framework for Kahneman's Dual-System Intelligence in GUI Agents
items.summary: CogniGUI combines hierarchical visual parsing of interface elements with a GRPO-based grounding agent that compares alternative interaction paths. Its ScreenSeek benchmark evaluates navigation across applications, changing interface states, and consistency between interfaces.

items.name: Chain-of-Memory: Enhancing GUI Agents for Cross-Application Navigation
items.summary: Chain-of-Memory explicitly records action descriptions and task-relevant screen information in short- and long-term memory for GUI navigation. GUI Odyssey-CoM provides 111,000 screen-action pairs with memory annotations for learning and evaluating information retention across applications.

items.name: Doc2Agent: Scalable Generation of Tool-Using Agents from API Documentation
items.summary: Introduces Doc2Agent, a pipeline that generates and refines Python tools from API documentation for tool-using agents, with WebArena APIs among its evaluations.

items.name: Mobile-R1: Towards Interactive Capability for VLM-Based Mobile Agent via Systematic Training
items.summary: Uses a staged curriculum from response-format alignment through action feedback to interactive task-level training for mobile agents.

items.name: Agent-RewardBench: Towards a Unified Benchmark for Reward Modeling across Perception, Planning, and Safety in Real-World Multimodal Agents
items.summary: Introduces Agent-RewardBench to evaluate step-level reward models for multimodal agents across perception, planning, and safety; web navigation is among its scenarios.

items.name: Mind2Web 2: Evaluating Agentic Search with Agent-as-a-Judge
items.summary: Introduces Mind2Web 2, 130 long-horizon tasks requiring live web browsing and information synthesis, plus an Agent-as-a-Judge framework for grading answers and sources.

items.name: ZonUI-3B: A Lightweight Vision-Language Model for Cross-Resolution GUI Grounding
items.summary: ZonUI-3B trains GUI grounding with a curated 24,000-example collection of mobile, desktop, and web screenshots. Its two-stage procedure first learns across platforms and then specializes on high-resolution images, with ablations on data diversity and redundant examples.

items.name: DiMo-GUI: Advancing Test-time Scaling in GUI Grounding via Modality-Aware Visual Reasoning
items.summary: Separates textual and iconic UI elements and iteratively focuses visual regions to refine grounding without additional model training.

items.name: LineRetriever: Planning-Aware Observation Reduction for Web Agents
items.summary: LineRetriever uses a language model to select observation lines that matter for upcoming web-navigation actions. It reduces DOM or accessibility-tree context by considering the planning horizon.

items.name: SafeMobile: Chain-level Jailbreak Detection and Automated Evaluation for Multimodal Mobile Agents
items.summary: Studies chain-level risk detection for mobile multimodal agents and a language-model-assisted evaluator, assessing safety interventions together with functional preservation.

items.name: WebArxiv: A Reproducible Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Web Agents on arXiv Tasks
items.summary: WebArxiv provides 510 static-snapshot tasks with deterministic answers for scholarly browsing, including constrained paper retrieval, content extraction, and cross-paper comparison. The study also tests dynamic retrieval of interaction history to address repetitive or incomplete agent reasoning.

items.name: GLM-4.5V and GLM-4.1V-Thinking: Towards Versatile Multimodal Reasoning with Scalable Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Reports the GLM-4.1V-Thinking, GLM-4.5V, and GLM-4.6V vision-language model family and curriculum-based RL training, with GUI agents among its evaluated tasks.

items.name: Less is More: Empowering GUI Agent with Context-Aware Simplification
items.summary: SimpAgent prunes distracting interface elements with visual masks and compresses interaction history using consistency-based guidance. The study evaluates these two forms of context reduction during GUI navigation in web and mobile environments.

items.name: How to Train Your LLM Web Agent: A Statistical Diagnosis
items.summary: Studies compute allocation for web-agent post-training with teacher-generated supervised fine-tuning followed by on-policy reinforcement learning. It samples 1,370 training configurations and uses bootstrap analysis to examine hyperparameter sensitivity on WorkArena and MiniWoB++.

items.name: Mobile GUI Agents under Real-world Threats: Are We There Yet?
items.summary: Introduces an app-content instrumentation framework and complementary interactive and static test suites for mobile GUI agents. It studies how untrusted third-party content changes task execution and state understanding.

items.name: WebSynthesis: World-Model-Guided MCTS for Efficient WebUI-Trajectory Synthesis
items.summary: Introduces WebSynthesis, which uses a learned web world model and tree-based planning to synthesize interaction trajectories for training web agents.

items.name: A Systematization of Security Vulnerabilities in Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Analyzes security boundaries in computer-use agents through a risk taxonomy and concrete adversarial case studies. It links observed failures to input provenance, interface-action binding, memory, and delegation, and proposes CUA-specific evaluation principles.

items.name: R-VLM: Region-Aware Vision Language Model for Precise GUI Grounding
items.summary: R-VLM localizes GUI elements through zoomed-in region proposals and an intersection-over-union-aware training objective. It evaluates the grounding model on ScreenSpot and AgentStudio and studies its effect on navigation in AITW and Mind2Web.

items.name: MobileGUI-RL: Advancing Mobile GUI Agent through Reinforcement Learning in Online Environment
items.summary: MobileGUI-RL constructs an online training curriculum through agent exploration and task filtering. It adapts GRPO with trajectory-aware advantages and rewards for task completion and execution efficiency, evaluated on three online mobile-agent benchmarks.

items.name: GTA1: GUI Test-time Scaling Agent
items.summary: GTA1 samples multiple action proposals at each GUI step and uses a judge to select among them. A separate grounding model is trained with reinforcement learning to map selected proposals to visual targets, linking planning-time search with click localization.

items.name: OpenAgentSafety: A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluating Real-World AI Agent Safety
items.summary: Evaluates agent safety across real browser, code, filesystem, shell, and messaging tools using rule-based and model-based assessments.

items.name: VisualTrap: A Stealthy Backdoor Attack on GUI Agents via Visual Grounding Manipulation
items.summary: Studies backdoors that redirect GUI visual grounding even when the task plan is correct. VisualTrap evaluates whether poisoned grounding training transfers to downstream tasks and across web, mobile, and desktop interface settings.

items.name: A Training-Free, Task-Agnostic Framework for Enhancing MLLM Performance on High-Resolution Images
items.summary: Introduces Extract Candidate then Predict (ECP), a training-free two-stage method for high-resolution images, evaluated partly on 4K GUI grounding.

items.name: LaSM: Layer-wise Scaling Mechanism for Defending Pop-up Attack on GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces LaSM, a training-free defense that selectively scales attention and MLP components to improve alignment with task-relevant screen regions. It evaluates the approach against pop-up-based GUI injection attacks.

items.name: Let's Think in Two Steps: Mitigating Agreement Bias in MLLMs with Self-Grounded Verification
items.summary: Studies agreement bias in multimodal agent verifiers across web navigation and computer use, and introduces SGV to assess trajectories using self-generated priors.

items.name: Machine-Readable Ads: Accessibility and Trust Patterns for AI Web Agents interacting with Online Advertisements
items.summary: Compares DOM-based and pixel-based web agents on a cloned news site containing advertisements, consent dialogs and paywalls. The study examines how interface presentation affects ad interaction and consequential subscription choices.

items.name: WebGuard: Building a Generalizable Guardrail for Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces WebGuard, a human-annotated dataset for predicting outcomes and risk levels of state-changing website actions. It provides generalization splits and evaluates specialized guardrail models.

items.name: Manipulating LLM Web Agents with Indirect Prompt Injection Attack via HTML Accessibility Tree
items.summary: Studies indirect prompt injection through HTML content consumed as accessibility trees. The evaluation tests how manipulated page observations redirect browser-agent actions on real websites.

items.name: GUI-G$^2$: Gaussian Reward Modeling for GUI Grounding
items.summary: GUI-G2 replaces binary grounding rewards with Gaussian point rewards and spatial-coverage rewards. An adaptive variance tied to element dimensions supplies continuous training feedback for targets of different sizes, evaluated on the ScreenSpot benchmark family.
