items.name: Screen2AX: Vision-Based Approach for Automatic macOS Accessibility Generation
items.summary: Introduces Screen2AX, which creates hierarchical accessibility metadata from macOS screenshots, plus datasets and Screen2AX-Task for desktop-agent evaluation.

items.name: MobileUse: A GUI Agent with Hierarchical Reflection for Autonomous Mobile Operation
items.summary: MobileUse reflects on errors at action and task timescales, invoking reflection when needed and using proactive exploration to learn unfamiliar apps. It evaluates this mobile execution framework on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab and describes a toolkit for physical-device operation.

items.name: ProactiveVA: Proactive Visual Analytics with LLM-Based UI Agent
items.summary: Studies proactive assistance in visual-analytics interfaces, using interaction logs to detect support needs and provide context-aware suggestions and guidance.

items.name: OS-MAP: How Far Can Computer-Using Agents Go in Breadth and Depth?
items.summary: OS-MAP organizes 416 computer-use tasks across 15 applications by a five-level automation taxonomy and a hierarchy of user demands. The benchmark separates required autonomy from generalization scope to diagnose where agents struggle as task demands increase.

items.name: MMBench-GUI: Hierarchical Multi-Platform Evaluation Framework for GUI Agents
items.summary: MMBench-GUI evaluates interface understanding, element grounding, task automation, and collaboration across six named desktop, mobile, and web platforms. It introduces the Efficiency-Quality Area metric for examining execution efficiency alongside task quality in online GUI automation.

items.name: FingerTip 20K: A Benchmark for Proactive and Personalized Mobile LLM Agents
items.summary: FingerTip 20K gathers 20K human Android demonstrations from users' long-term everyday app use, with user context, to evaluate proactive task suggestion and preference-aware task execution.

items.name: MapAgent: Trajectory-Constructed Memory-Augmented Planning for Mobile Task Automation
items.summary: Builds reusable page memories from past mobile trajectories and retrieves them to support task planning and execution.

items.name: UI-AGILE: Advancing GUI Agents with Effective Reinforcement Learning and Precise Inference-Time Grounding
items.summary: Combines grounding-oriented reward and sampling improvements with inference-time image decomposition and target selection.

items.name: Magentic-UI: Towards Human-in-the-loop Agentic Systems
items.summary: Magentic-UI combines browser interaction, code execution, file operations, and MCP tools in an interface for human-agent collaboration. It studies collaborative planning and task execution, action guards, and persistent memory through benchmark tasks, simulated users, user studies, and safety assessments.

items.name: General Agentic Planning Through Simulative Reasoning with World Models
items.summary: Introduces SiRA, an agent architecture that uses a language-based world model to simulate action outcomes for planning in web-browser tasks.

items.name: Phi-Ground Tech Report: Advancing Perception in GUI Grounding
items.summary: Reports a GUI-grounding model family and empirical design choices covering source data, perception training, and coordinate prediction.

items.name: Measuring Harmfulness of Computer-Using Agents
items.summary: Introduces CUAHarm, 104 computer-use misuse tasks in a sandbox with verifiable rewards, and studies whether language models can monitor unsafe agent actions.

items.name: NaturalGAIA: A Verifiable Benchmark and Hierarchical Framework for Long-Horizon GUI Tasks
items.summary: NaturalGAIA builds verifiable long-horizon GUI tasks from human interaction intents while separating causal task structure from its verbal description. Its LightManus-Jarvis framework divides dynamic planning and context management from execution based on visual and structural interface information.

items.name: Web-CogReasoner: Towards Multimodal Knowledge-Induced Cognitive Reasoning for Web Agents
items.summary: Web-CogReasoner separates factual and conceptual web knowledge from procedural reasoning, using a structured curriculum to train a multimodal agent. Web-CogDataset and Web-CogBench support study of these capabilities alongside web-navigation evaluation.

items.name: NaviMaster: Learning a Unified Policy for GUI and Embodied Navigation Tasks
items.summary: NaviMaster trains a shared policy for GUI and embodied navigation using a common visual-trajectory formulation. It combines trajectory collection, reinforcement learning and distance-aware rewards, with evaluation across both task families.

items.name: MagicGUI: A Foundational Mobile GUI Agent with Scalable Data Pipeline and Reinforcement Fine-tuning
items.summary: Combines a mobile GUI data pipeline, perception and planning capabilities, and reinforcement fine-tuning for interactive task execution.

items.name: CoAct-1: Computer-using Multi-Agent System with Coding Actions
items.summary: CoAct-1 delegates subtasks between a GUI operator and a programmer that executes Python or Bash. Its OSWorld evaluation studies a hybrid action space in which scripts handle suitable file and data operations while visual interaction handles other steps.

items.name: HarmonyGuard: Toward Safety and Utility in Web Agents via Adaptive Policy Enhancement and Dual-Objective Optimization
items.summary: Introduces HarmonyGuard, a multi-agent framework that updates security policies and weighs safety against task completion for agents operating on the open web.

items.name: Uncertainty-Aware GUI Agent: Adaptive Perception through Component Recommendation and Human-in-the-Loop Refinement
items.summary: RecAgent narrows attention to recommended UI components and requests user feedback when task intent or decisions remain uncertain. It introduces ComplexAction to evaluate specified single-step GUI actions in difficult interface scenarios.

items.name: VeriWeb: Verifiable Long-Chain Web Benchmark for Agentic Information-Seeking
items.summary: Introduces VeriWeb, a benchmark of long-chain web information-seeking tasks with verifiable subtasks and a complete human-annotated trajectory for each task.

items.name: Evolving in Tasks: Empowering the Multi-modality Large Language Model as the Computer Use Agent
items.summary: The Self-Evolution Agent combines automatic generation of verifiable computer-use trajectories with step-wise reinforcement learning for long-horizon training. It also describes a model-enhancement procedure that integrates grounding and planning capabilities without an additional training stage.

items.name: GuirlVG: Incentivize GUI Visual Grounding via Empirical Exploration on Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Introduces GuirlVG, an empirical study of reinforcement fine-tuning for GUI visual grounding. It analyzes training components and adds an adaptive KL-based mechanism to limit reward over-optimization.

items.name: Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents
items.summary: D2Snap reduces serialized DOM observations while preserving actionable elements and features that distinguish their uses. The study compares reduced DOM inputs with screenshot-based observations for a web agent on tasks sampled from Online-Mind2Web.

items.name: OS Agents: A Survey on MLLM-based Agents for General Computing Devices Use
items.summary: Surveys agents that operate computers and phones through operating-system interfaces, covering components, capabilities, foundation models, frameworks, and benchmarks.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

items.name: SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent with Autonomous Learning from Experience
items.summary: SEAgent explores unfamiliar software using a world-state assessor and an automatically generated task curriculum. It learns from failed and successful interactions through adversarial imitation and GRPO, then combines specialist experience into a generalist agent evaluated on five OSWorld software environments.

items.name: Cognitive Duality for Adaptive Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces CogniWeb, which switches between fast reactive processing and slower deliberative reasoning according to task complexity. WebArena experiments examine this combination of learned behaviors and online planning.

items.name: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for GUI Grounding via Region Consistency
items.summary: GUI-RC aggregates multiple grounding predictions into spatial voting grids to choose a consensus region. GUI-RCPO then turns agreement with that region into a reward for test-time policy updates on unlabeled GUI screenshots.

items.name: InfiGUI-G1: Advancing GUI Grounding with Adaptive Exploration Policy Optimization
items.summary: Uses multiple candidate answers and adaptive exploration rewards to improve spatial and semantic alignment in GUI grounding.

items.name: MVISU-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents for Real-World Tasks by Multi-App, Vague, Interactive, Single-App and Unethical Instructions
items.summary: MVISU-Bench evaluates bilingual mobile tasks involving cross-app work, vague requests, user interaction and unethical instructions alongside ordinary single-app tasks. Its Aider prompting module is designed to clarify intent and mitigate risky execution within agent workflows.

items.name: OpenCUA: Open Foundations for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Presents demonstration collection infrastructure, the AgentNet dataset, and a training pipeline for open computer-use models.

items.name: OdysseyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Complex Office Application Workflows
items.summary: Introduces OdysseyBench for evaluating long-horizon workflows across office applications, plus HomerAgents to generate tasks from environment exploration and dialogue synthesis.

items.name: FineState-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Fine-Grained State Control in GUI Agents
items.summary: FineState-Bench evaluates fine-grained GUI perception and control across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces. Its Visual Diagnostic Assistant separates perception and localization contributions in controlled interaction experiments.

items.name: UI-Venus Technical Report: Building High-performance UI Agents with RFT
items.summary: Studies screenshot-based GUI grounding and navigation using curated interaction data, reward design, and reinforcement fine-tuning.

items.name: CRAFT-GUI: Curriculum-Reinforced Agent For GUI Tasks
items.summary: CRAFT-GUI organizes GUI trajectories by difficulty for curriculum-based GRPO training. Its reward combines rule-based signals with model judgments, with evaluation on Android Control and an internal online benchmark.

items.name: WebMall -- A Multi-Shop Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents
items.summary: WebMall provides four simulated online shops with heterogeneous product data for comparison shopping, related-product searches, and checkout tasks. It evaluates web agents with different observation formats and memory configurations in a fixed offline environment.

items.name: MM-BrowseComp: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Browsing Agents
items.summary: Introduces MM-BrowseComp, a benchmark for browsing agents that must use evidence from web images and videos to answer multimodal search questions.

items.name: V2P: Visual Attention Calibration for GUI Grounding via Background Suppression and Center Peaking
items.summary: V2P trains GUI grounding by suppressing attention to background regions and emphasizing the center of the target element. It represents target importance with size-dependent Gaussian heatmaps and evaluates the contribution of each component on ScreenSpot-v2 and ScreenSpot-Pro.

items.name: ComputerRL: Scaling End-to-End Online Reinforcement Learning for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Combines API and GUI actions with distributed desktop reinforcement learning and alternating supervised training to address training instability.

items.name: You Don't Know Until You Click:Automated GUI Testing for Production-Ready Software Evaluation
items.summary: RealDevWorld evaluates generated software repositories with 194 development tasks and AppEvalPilot, an agent judge that operates the resulting GUIs. The evaluation examines functional behavior, visual fidelity, and runtime responses to produce task-specific diagnostic feedback.

items.name: Mobile-Agent-v3: Fundamental Agents for GUI Automation
items.summary: Introduces GUI-Owl models and Mobile-Agent-v3 orchestration, using environment-generated trajectories to support GUI capabilities.

items.name: A Functionality-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents in E-commerce Domains
items.summary: Amazon-Bench generates functionality-specific web tasks from page content and interactive controls, covering operations beyond product search. Its evaluator checks task completion and unintended changes to account state, such as address or purchase settings.

items.name: Structuring GUI Elements through Vision Language Models: Towards Action Space Generation
items.summary: Introduces IAML training, which augments coordinate samples to help multimodal models locate GUI elements from screen content and user instructions.

items.name: WebMMU: A Benchmark for Multimodal Multilingual Website Understanding and Code Generation
items.summary: Introduces WebMMU, a multilingual benchmark for website visual question answering, element grounding, code editing, and mockup-to-code generation.

items.name: WebSight: A Vision-First Architecture for Robust Web Agents
items.summary: WebSight uses a vision-language model trained on web-interface examples within a modular agent with planning, action, verification, and episodic memory components. It evaluates element clicking on Showdown Clicks and full browsing tasks on WebVoyager using visual observations.

items.name: DashboardQA: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Question Answering on Interactive Dashboards
items.summary: Introduces DashboardQA to evaluate how vision-language GUI agents answer questions by interacting with dashboards, grounding elements, and planning actions.
items.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EACL 2026

items.name: PerPilot: Personalizing VLM-based Mobile Agents via Memory and Exploration
items.summary: Introduces PerPilot and the PerInstruct dataset for completing user-specific mobile instructions through memory retrieval, app exploration, and clarification when missing context remains unresolved.

items.name: InternVL3.5: Advancing Open-Source Multimodal Models in Versatility, Reasoning, and Efficiency
items.summary: Introduces InternVL3.5, a multimodal model family trained with Cascade RL and designed for more efficient inference; GUI interaction is among its stated capabilities.

items.name: AppAgent-Pro: A Proactive GUI Agent System for Multidomain Information Integration and User Assistance
items.summary: Proposes a proactive GUI assistant that gathers information across domains in response to user requests and anticipated information needs.

items.name: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
items.summary: Introduces CUA-SHADE-Arena and a red-teaming workflow for testing monitors that detect covert misbehavior in computer-use agent trajectories.

items.name: Mind the Third Eye! Benchmarking Privacy Awareness in MLLM-powered Smartphone Agents
items.summary: Introduces SAPA-Bench with 7,138 smartphone scenarios to evaluate whether MLLM-powered mobile agents detect and protect sensitive personal information on screen.

items.name: InquireMobile: Teaching VLM-based Mobile Agent to Request Human Assistance via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
items.summary: InquireMobile trains mobile agents to seek human confirmation at critical decisions using staged reinforcement fine-tuning and pre-action reasoning. InquireBench evaluates safe interaction and proactive inquiry, distinguishing asking for help from completing the underlying task.

items.name: SWIRL: A Staged Workflow for Interleaved Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Control
items.summary: Introduces SWIRL, staged interleaved RL for mobile GUI control, pairing a Navigator that plans from screens and language with an Interactor that produces actions.

items.name: CODA: Coordinating the Cerebrum and Cerebellum for a Dual-Brain Computer Use Agent with Decoupled Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: CODA combines a generalist planner with a specialist GUI executor and trains application-specific planners through decoupled GRPO. Successful specialist trajectories then support supervised training of a consolidated planner, evaluated across four ScienceBoard applications.

items.name: Morae: Proactively Pausing UI Agents for User Choices
items.summary: Introduces Morae, a UI agent that detects decision points and pauses for user choices using interface code and screenshots. A study with blind and low-vision participants evaluates this mixed-initiative approach on real web tasks.

items.name: MMSearch-Plus: Benchmarking Provenance-Aware Search for Multimodal Browsing Agents
items.summary: Introduces MMSearch-Plus, a multimodal browsing benchmark with iterative image-text search, and an agent framework that marks and crops images for targeted retrieval.

items.name: UItron: Foundational GUI Agent with Advanced Perception and Planning
items.summary: UItron combines GUI perception and planning data engineering with supervised training and curriculum reinforcement learning in connected mobile and PC environments. It also collects more than one million operation steps across 100 Chinese apps and builds offline and online evaluation environments.

items.name: KG-RAG: Enhancing GUI Agent Decision-Making via Knowledge Graph-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: KG-RAG converts UI transition graphs into a searchable vector store and uses intent-guided retrieval to construct actionable navigation paths. It introduces KG-Android-Bench and KG-Harmony-Bench and evaluates transfer from mobile apps to web and desktop tasks.

items.name: MobiAgent: A Systematic Framework for Customizable Mobile Agents
items.summary: Presents MobiAgent, combining MobiMind agent models, the AgentRR acceleration framework, and MobiFlow evaluation. It also introduces an AI-assisted data-collection pipeline for mobile GUI tasks.

items.name: FlashAdventure: A Benchmark for GUI Agents Solving Full Story Arcs in Diverse Adventure Games
items.summary: FlashAdventure evaluates GUI agents on completing story arcs in 34 adventure games. It pairs an automated gameplay judge with COAST, a framework that keeps long-term clue memory to plan and complete sequential objectives.

items.name: Throttling Web Agents Using Reasoning Gates
items.summary: Introduces reasoning gates that require agents to solve generated, verifiable puzzles before receiving access to resources. The throttling approach is deployed on a custom website and MCP servers and evaluated with web agents.

items.name: Succeed or Learn Slowly: Sample Efficient Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Mobile App Control
items.summary: Succeed or Learn Slowly applies direct off-policy updates to successful interactions and more conservative regularized updates to negative examples. Successful Transition Replay prioritizes successful experience during policy learning, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.

items.name: OmniActor: A Generalist GUI and Embodied Agent for 2D&3D Worlds
items.summary: Introduces OmniActor, which shares shallow model layers while separating deeper parameters to train jointly on GUI and embodied interactions. A unified action representation and mixed training data support evaluation in both task families.

items.name: AppCopilot: Toward General, Accurate, Long-Horizon, and Efficient Mobile Agent
items.summary: Describes a mobile-agent stack combining region-based coordinate correction, hierarchical task planning, multi-agent voting, and reuse of successful interaction traces.

items.name: UI-TARS-2 Technical Report: Advancing GUI Agent with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: UI-TARS-2 combines scalable trajectory generation, stabilized multi-turn reinforcement learning, and a sandbox that supports GUI, filesystem, and terminal actions. The report evaluates the resulting agent across web, desktop, Android, and game tasks and analyzes training stability.

items.name: PG-Agent: An Agent Powered by Page Graph
items.summary: Introduces PG-Agent, which turns GUI operation episodes into page graphs and retrieves guidance from them to support task decomposition in new scenarios.

items.name: MobileRAG: Enhancing Mobile Agent with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: MobileRAG combines retrieval and memory components to support mobile tasks that need external knowledge or long action sequences. MobileRAG-Eval is introduced to study these requirements on complex real-world app tasks.

items.name: Are LLM Agents the New RPA? A Comparative Study with RPA Across Enterprise Workflows
items.summary: Compares an agent using computer interfaces with UiPath RPA on enterprise data entry, monitoring, and document extraction, measuring speed, reliability, and development effort.

items.name: Learning Active Perception via Self-Evolving Preference Optimization for GUI Grounding
items.summary: LASER builds preference data for multi-step GUI perception by combining Monte Carlo quality estimates with region-overlap evaluation. Its self-evolving training encourages relevant region selection and adapts the amount of reasoning before predicting screen coordinates.

items.name: SparkUI-Parser: Enhancing GUI Perception with Robust Grounding and Parsing
items.summary: Introduces SparkUI-Parser, which adds continuous coordinate decoding and a rejection mechanism for nonexistent targets to a multimodal model. It also presents ScreenParse for evaluating structural interface perception.

items.name: MAS-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Shortcut-Augmented Hybrid Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: MAS-Bench evaluates mobile agents that combine GUI actions with APIs, deep links, and reusable scripts. Its 139 tasks across 11 apps test use of 88 predefined shortcuts as well as the ability to generate new reusable workflows.

items.name: Instruction Agent: Enhancing Agent with Expert Demonstration
items.summary: Introduces Instruction Agent, a GUI agent that follows instructions extracted from one expert demonstration and uses verification and backtracking to handle interruptions.

items.name: VeriOS: Query-Driven Proactive Human-Agent-GUI Interaction for Trustworthy OS Agents
items.summary: Introduces VeriOS-Agent, which learns when to execute GUI actions autonomously and when to query a user under untrustworthy conditions. Its staged training combines supervised learning and group-relative policy optimization.

items.name: AgentSentinel: An End-to-End and Real-Time Security Defense Framework for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces AgentSentinel, which intercepts sensitive computer-agent operations and audits them using task context together with system traces. BadComputerUse evaluates this enforcement approach across attack scenarios involving tool and computer control.

items.name: Dark Patterns Meet GUI Agents: LLM Agent Susceptibility to Manipulative Interfaces and the Role of Human Oversight
items.summary: Studies how GUI agents, people, and human-agent teams respond to manipulative interface designs. The two-phase evaluation examines failure modes and the benefits and costs of human oversight.

items.name: Agentic Lybic: Multi-Agent Execution System with Tiered Reasoning and Orchestration
items.summary: Introduces Agentic Lybic, a desktop automation system that routes tasks among GUI, code, and decision-support workers using a finite-state machine and evaluator.

items.name: Environmental Injection Attacks against GUI Agents in Realistic Dynamic Environments
items.summary: Introduces Chameleon, an environmental-injection evaluation framework that varies webpage content and trigger context. It combines simulated page variation with attention-based optimization and tests GUI agents across realistic websites.

items.name: UI-S1: Advancing GUI Automation via Semi-online Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: UI-S1 simulates multi-turn online learning over offline trajectories, using a patch module to recover divergences while retaining the model’s own outputs in context. It combines discounted future returns with step- and episode-level advantages and introduces a semi-online performance proxy.

items.name: How Auxiliary Reasoning Unleashes GUI Grounding in VLMs
items.summary: Studies the gap between latent visual grounding and explicit coordinate output in general vision-language models. Three zero-shot methods add axes, grids, or labeled intersections to GUI screenshots so models can express spatial locations without fine-tuning.

items.name: PrivWeb: Unobtrusive and Content-aware Privacy Protection For Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces PrivWeb, which uses a local language model to anonymize interface information according to user preferences. Adaptive notifications and selective pauses give users control over sensitive information access during web-agent tasks.

items.name: ReSum: Unlocking Long-Horizon Search Intelligence via Context Summarization
items.summary: Introduces ReSum, which compresses interaction histories during long web searches, and ReSum-GRPO, which trains agents to reason across the resulting segments.

items.name: See, Think, Act: Teaching Multimodal Agents to Effectively Interact with GUI by Identifying Toggles
items.summary: Introduces a benchmark for binary GUI-toggle instructions and State-aware Reasoning, which compares the observed control state with the requested state before choosing an action. It evaluates agents on toggle tasks and broader interactive benchmarks.

items.name: InfraMind: A Novel Exploration-based GUI Agentic Framework for Mission-critical Industrial Management
items.summary: InfraMind explores industrial management GUIs using virtual-machine snapshots and builds memory for planning and hierarchical state recognition. Its framework also studies knowledge distillation and safety checks on open-source and commercial data-center management platforms.

items.name: TGPO: Tree-Guided Preference Optimization for Robust Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: TGPO merges semantically equivalent web states into tree-structured trajectories for offline preference optimization. A process reward model scores subgoal progress, redundant behavior, and action validity, while dynamic weighting emphasizes consequential decisions.

items.name: Detecting Pipeline Failures through Fine-Grained Analysis of Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces a modular framework for identifying errors at intermediate stages of a web-agent pipeline. A SeeAct and Mind2Web case study examines weaknesses that are obscured by final task-success metrics.

items.name: ScaleCUA: Scaling Open-Source Computer Use Agents with Cross-Platform Data
items.summary: Introduces a cross-platform computer-use dataset and agents trained with a collection pipeline combining automated interaction and human input.

items.name: GUI-ARP: Enhancing Grounding with Adaptive Region Perception for GUI Agents
items.summary: GUI-ARP uses visual attention to crop relevant screenshot regions and decides whether a target needs single-stage or multi-stage analysis. Supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO trains this adaptive procedure for high-resolution GUI grounding.

items.name: BTL-UI: Blink-Think-Link Reasoning Model for GUI Agent
items.summary: BTL-UI separates GUI interaction into screen-region attention, planning and executable-command generation. It adds an automated annotation pipeline and rule-based process/outcome rewards for training, with evaluation on both static understanding and dynamic interaction.

items.name: GUI-ReWalk: Massive Data Generation for GUI Agent via Stochastic Exploration and Intent-Aware Reasoning
items.summary: GUI-ReWalk begins with stochastic interface exploration and then infers goals to generate coherent action trajectories. It supports long-horizon workflows across applications and studies training on the resulting data using grounding and navigation benchmarks.

items.name: UIPro: Unleashing Superior Interaction Capability For GUI Agents
items.summary: UIPro pretrains GUI understanding on 20.6 million tasks and then harmonizes interaction datasets through a unified action space. Continued fine-tuning uses the merged multi-platform data to train action prediction for generalist GUI operation.

items.name: Mano Technical Report
items.summary: Introduces Mano, a GUI agent trained with simulated data, supervised fine-tuning, and offline and online RL, with a verification module for error recovery.

items.name: Orcust: Stepwise-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for GUI Agent
items.summary: Orcust combines principle-constrained reward modeling with GUI trajectory collection in instrumented virtual machines. Environment-checkable and model-derived principles guide stepwise feedback for grounding, basic operations, and complete task execution.

items.name: MobileRL: Online Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: MobileRL adapts GRPO to mobile GUI training with difficulty-dependent replay of successes and filtering of failure curricula. A shortest-path reward adjustment accounts for task length, with evaluations on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

items.name: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Implicit Step Rewards
items.summary: Introduces iStar, a general agentic RL method that learns implicit step rewards; WebShop is one of several interactive benchmarks used to evaluate it.

items.name: Robust, Observable, and Evolvable Agentic Systems Engineering: A Principled Framework Validated via the Fairy GUI Agent
items.summary: Presents an agent-engineering framework combining runtime goal clarification, an observable component architecture and evolving execution memory. The Fairy mobile GUI agent evaluates these mechanisms on ambiguous tasks and through controlled and user studies.

items.name: Recon-Act: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Browser-Use System via Web Reconnaissance, Tool Generation, and Task Execution
items.summary: Introduces Recon-Act, a browser-use framework that compares failed and successful web trajectories to create reusable tools for planning and executing long-horizon website tasks.

items.name: Learning GUI Grounding with Spatial Reasoning from Visual Feedback
items.summary: GUI-Cursor treats GUI grounding as a sequence of cursor movements guided by visible feedback and movement history. Online reinforcement learning with trajectory rewards trains the model to refine the target location across multiple steps.

items.name: UISim: An Interactive Image-Based UI Simulator for Dynamic Mobile Environments
items.summary: Introduces UISim, an image-based mobile UI simulator that predicts the next screen layout after an action and renders the resulting screen for testing and data generation.

items.name: Benchmarking MLLM-based Web Understanding: Reasoning, Robustness and Safety
items.summary: Evaluates multimodal LLMs on web interface reasoning, visual perturbation robustness, and safety-critical web understanding tasks.

items.name: D-Artemis: A Deliberative Cognitive Framework for Mobile GUI Multi-Agents
items.summary: Introduces D-Artemis, a mobile GUI agent framework that retrieves app-specific tips, checks actions before execution, and reflects on their outcomes without trajectory training.

items.name: ProRe: A Proactive Reward System for GUI Agents via Reasoner-Actor Collaboration
items.summary: ProRe evaluates GUI task outcomes by having a reasoner assign targeted environment-probing tasks to specialist actors. The additional observations support reward judgments, with separate evaluation of judge accuracy and downstream agent task success.

items.name: RISK: A Framework for GUI Agents in E-commerce Risk Management
items.summary: RISK combines browser-interaction training data, a benchmark, and reinforcement fine-tuning for e-commerce risk-management workflows. Its trajectories and rewards distinguish individual actions from multi-step stateful tasks involving deeply embedded web content.

items.name: Secure and Efficient Access Control for Computer-Use Agents via Context Space
items.summary: Introduces CSAgent, which combines static access policies with user intent and context and enforces them through an operating-system service. A supporting toolchain constructs and refines policies for agents using API, CLI and GUI interfaces.

items.name: WebGen-Agent: Enhancing Interactive Website Generation with Multi-Level Feedback and Step-Level Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Introduces WebGen-Agent for website code generation, using screenshot critiques and GUI-agent tests to refine code and provide step-level training rewards.

items.name: GUI-PRA: Process Reward Agent for GUI Tasks
items.summary: GUI-PRA evaluates GUI progress by generating task-specific criteria and actively inspecting visual evidence with tools. It tests offline judgment on OS-Critic Bench and the effects of this feedback on online mobile policies in AndroidWorld.

items.name: GUI-Shepherd: Reliable Process Reward and Verification for Long-Sequence GUI Tasks
items.summary: Introduces GUI-Shepherd, a process reward model trained on annotated GUI interactions to give step-level feedback for agent training and verification on AndroidWorld and AndroidControl.

items.name: Efficient Multi-turn RL for GUI Agents via Decoupled Training and Adaptive Data Curation
items.summary: DART separates GUI reinforcement learning into asynchronous environment, rollout, data-management, and training services. It curates experience by task difficulty, successful trajectories, and step uncertainty while correcting rollout-policy mismatch, with evaluation on OSWorld.

items.name: Generalist Scanner Meets Specialist Locator: A Synergistic Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Robust GUI Grounding
items.summary: GMS pairs a general vision-language scanner that proposes interface regions with a specialist locator that predicts coordinates within them. Hierarchical coarse-to-fine search coordinates the two components for GUI grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro.

items.name: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
items.summary: RAG-GUI trains a small guidance adapter to filter and summarize retrieved web tutorials while keeping the acting agent fixed. Supervised and rejection-sampling stages prepare the adapter for inference-time assistance, tested on offline web/mobile tasks and interactive Android tasks.

items.name: Scaling Synthetic Task Generation for Agents via Exploration
items.summary: AutoPlay explores application states and functions to generate tasks, then uses a model executor and verifier to construct demonstrations. It produces 20,000 tasks across 20 Android apps and 10,000 tasks across 13 Ubuntu apps for supervised and reinforcement learning of UI agents.

items.name: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
items.summary: Distills generalizable reasoning strategies from both successful and failed agent trajectories into a persistent memory bank for test-time retrieval.

items.name: Flash-Searcher: Fast and Effective Web Agents via DAG-Based Parallel Execution
items.summary: Introduces Flash-Searcher, a parallel agent framework that organizes dependent subtasks as a graph and runs independent paths concurrently; it is evaluated on deep-search benchmarks.

items.name: SCUBA: Salesforce Computer Use Benchmark
items.summary: SCUBA evaluates enterprise UI navigation and CRM workflows with 300 task instances derived from Salesforce user interviews. Salesforce sandbox execution and milestone-based assessment support comparisons between zero-shot agents and agents given demonstrations.

items.name: Ferret-UI Lite: Lessons from Building Small On-Device GUI Agents
items.summary: Ferret-UI Lite develops a 3B GUI agent using mixed real and synthetic data, reasoning with visual tools at inference, and reinforcement learning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across mobile, web, and desktop settings, including AndroidWorld and OSWorld.

items.name: PAL-UI: Planning with Active Look-back for Vision-Based GUI Agents
items.summary: PAL-UI combines observation/action summaries with selective retrieval of historical screenshots during planning. It trains mobile navigation models from step-level supervision and evaluates transfer to web navigation without additional training.

items.name: Graph2Eval: Automatic Multimodal Task Generation for Agents via Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: Introduces Graph2Eval, which generates multimodal agent evaluation tasks from knowledge graphs, including multi-step web interactions in Graph2Eval-Bench.

items.name: GUI-KV: Efficient GUI Agents via KV Cache with Spatio-Temporal Awareness
items.summary: GUI-KV compresses vision-language agents’ attention caches using visual-token saliency and redundancy between screenshot frames. The method requires no retraining and evaluates how cache budgets affect GUI action accuracy and computational cost.

items.name: WAInjectBench: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detections for Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces WAInjectBench with a threat-model taxonomy and malicious and benign text-image datasets for web-agent prompt-injection detection. It compares detector families across explicit and less visible forms of injected content.

items.name: WALT: Web Agents that Learn Tools
items.summary: WALT explores website functionality and converts demonstrated interactions into validated, reusable tools combining DOM actions, URL navigation, and agentic fallbacks. It evaluates this expanded browser action space on WebArena and VisualWebArena.

items.name: Just Do It!? Computer-Use Agents Exhibit Blind Goal-Directedness
items.summary: BLIND-ACT tests whether computer-use agents persist with ambiguous, contradictory, or infeasible goals without adequate contextual reasoning. Its OSWorld-based tasks and judged trajectories examine these behaviors and the effect of mitigation prompts.

items.name: Say One Thing, Do Another? Diagnosing Reasoning-Execution Gaps in VLM-Powered Mobile-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces an evaluation framework for mobile GUI agents that compares actions implied by their reasoning with intended and executed actions to diagnose mismatches.

items.name: Scaling Agents for Computer Use
items.summary: Introduces Behavior Judge, which converts execution trajectories into behavior narratives and compares multiple candidate rollouts. Experiments examine this selection approach on OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena and AndroidWorld.

items.name: BrowserArena: Evaluating LLM Agents on Real-World Web Navigation Tasks
items.summary: Introduces BrowserArena, a live-web platform for head-to-head agent comparisons on user-submitted tasks. Step-level human annotations support targeted analysis of navigation, pop-up handling and CAPTCHA-related failures.

items.name: FocusAgent: Simple Yet Effective Ways of Trimming the Large Context of Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces FocusAgent, which uses a lightweight LLM to select task-relevant lines from web agents' accessibility-tree observations, reducing context size and exposure to prompt injection.

items.name: Improving GUI Grounding with Explicit Position-to-Coordinate Mapping
items.summary: This work addresses GUI localization errors caused by mismatches between visual patch positions and output pixel coordinates. RULER tokens provide explicit coordinate references, while Interleaved MRoPE balances width and height encoding; evaluation uses the ScreenSpot benchmark family.

items.name: WAREX: Web Agent Reliability Evaluation on Existing Benchmarks
items.summary: WAREX augments existing web-agent benchmarks with reliability challenges arising from unstable systems and changing or disruptive website behavior. Evaluation on WebArena, WebVoyager and REAL examines how these disturbances affect task completion.

items.name: Learning Efficient Guardrails for Compliance
items.summary: Introduces PolicyGuardBench for detecting policy violations in full web-agent trajectories and their prefixes, and trains PolicyGuard as an efficient guardrail model.

items.name: Cross-Modal Content Optimization for Steering Web Agent Preferences
items.summary: Introduces Cross-Modal Preference Steering (CPS), a black-box attack that edits a listing's images and text to steer VLM-based web agents' selections.

items.name: \textsc{GUI-Spotlight}: Adaptive Iterative Focus Refinement for Enhanced GUI Visual Grounding
items.summary: GUI-Spotlight trains a grounding model to reason over images and call tools that iteratively narrow its visual focus. The paper evaluates this refinement method on ScreenSpot-Pro after training on 18,500 samples.

items.name: JEF-Hinter: Leveraging Offline Knowledge for Improving Web Agents Adaptation
items.summary: Introduces JEF-Hinter, which distills successful and failed trajectories into compact episodic hints and retrieves them for the current agent state. Web benchmark experiments examine guidance from decisive steps.

items.name: Understanding User Experiences of Computer Use Agents: Design Space and Opportunities for Building Agent UX Prototypes
items.summary: Maps design considerations for computer-use agent experiences and introduces AgentUXlab, a browser-based probe for prototyping and evaluating agent UX on a website.

items.name: 3Dify: a Framework for Procedural 3D-CG Generation Assisted by LLMs Using MCP and RAG
items.summary: Introduces 3Dify, a natural-language 3D graphics framework that operates creation tools through MCP and uses a computer-using agent for GUI operations when MCP is unavailable.

items.name: From Imperative to Declarative: Towards LLM-friendly OS Interfaces for Boosted Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces a Declarative Model Interface that maps existing GUIs to access, state and observation primitives while handling low-level interactions. Evaluation uses Word, PowerPoint and Excel on Windows with a GUI-agent baseline.

items.name: Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos
items.summary: Introduces Watch & Learn (W&L), which converts human computer-use videos into UI action trajectories by predicting actions between consecutive screen states.

items.name: GUISpector: An MLLM Agent Framework for Automated Verification of Natural Language Requirements in GUI Prototypes
items.summary: Introduces GUISpector, an MLLM agent framework that operates GUI prototypes to check natural-language requirements and produces feedback for developers.

items.name: Demystifying deep search: a holistic evaluation with hint-free multi-hop questions and factorised metrics
items.summary: Introduces WebDetective, a deep-search benchmark with a traceable Wikipedia sandbox, and EvidenceLoop, an evidence-tracking workflow for web-agent search and synthesis.

items.name: Agent+P: Guiding UI Agents via Symbolic Planning
items.summary: Guides UI agents with symbolic planning over a UI transition graph initialized from app-code analysis and updated through online exploration, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.

items.name: A Multimodal GUI Architecture for Interfacing with LLM-Based Conversational Assistants
items.summary: Presents an MCP architecture that exposes an application's GUI navigation graph and view-specific tools to speech-enabled LLM assistants for voice interaction.

items.name: Your Harness is Not Secure: Benchmarking Real-world Threat of Command Line Interface Agent
items.summary: Introduces AdvCLI, a sandbox benchmark for evaluating whether command-line agents carry out security-relevant operating-system tasks across multiple hosts.

items.name: Invisible to Humans, Triggered by Agents: Stealthy Jailbreak Attacks on Mobile Vision-Language Agents
items.summary: Uses the near-zero contact-touch signals of automated mobile agents to expose malicious visual content selectively during agent interactions. The paper combines this agent-only perceptual injection with HG-IDA* prompt optimization to study unauthorized cross-app actions.

items.name: ReInAgent: A Context-Aware GUI Agent Enabling Human-in-the-Loop Mobile Task Navigation
items.summary: Introduces ReInAgent, coordinating information management, planning, and reflection around a shared memory for mobile tasks. It proactively asks users for information and checks consistency when instructions are ambiguous or change during execution.

items.name: Auto-scaling Continuous Memory for GUI Agent
items.summary: Encodes GUI trajectories into compact continuous embeddings that can be retrieved directly into an agent’s input. An automated environment-discovery and rollout pipeline expands this memory for long tasks and unfamiliar interfaces.

items.name: WARC-Bench: Web Archive Based Benchmark for GUI Subtask Executions
items.summary: WARC-Bench packages dynamic web pages as replayable archives and evaluates short navigation subtasks involving components such as date pickers and scrollable containers. It also studies supervised training followed by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on these browser interactions.

items.name: ALLOY: Generating Reusable Agent Workflows from User Demonstration
items.summary: Introduces ALLOY, which turns user demonstrations into editable, reusable workflows for LLM-based web agents carrying out preference-dependent tasks.

items.name: SecureWebArena: A Holistic Security Evaluation Benchmark for LVLM-based Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces SecureWebArena with simulated interactive websites, an attack-vector taxonomy and labeled agent trajectories. Its evaluation separates failures in reasoning, behavioral traces and task outcomes across vision-language agent families.

items.name: BrowserAgent: Building Web Agents with Human-Inspired Web Browsing Actions
items.summary: Trains BrowserAgent to use Playwright-based scrolling, clicking and typing directly on webpages for information-seeking tasks. Supervised and rejection fine-tuning are paired with explicit memory for conclusions carried across steps.

items.name: SusBench: An Online Benchmark for Evaluating Dark Pattern Susceptibility of Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces SusBench, an online benchmark that inserts dark-pattern designs into consumer websites for agent evaluation. A human study checks the realism of the interventions, and agent trials compare susceptibility across pattern types.

items.name: WebRouter: Query-specific Router via Variational Information Bottleneck for Cost-sensitive Web Agent
items.summary: Introduces WebRouter, a cost-aware router that compresses web-agent prompts to choose among LLMs, with cost and accuracy measured on WebVoyager websites.

items.name: R-WoM: Retrieval-augmented World Model For Computer-use Agents
items.summary: R-WoM evaluates how well world models predict nearby GUI states, align complete procedures, and recognize milestone transitions. It retrieves external tutorials to guide simulated future interactions, with experiments on subsets of OSWorld and WebArena.

items.name: HackWorld: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Exploiting Web Application Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Introduces HackWorld for evaluating visual computer-use agents in a capture-the-flag collection of web applications. The benchmark examines interface navigation and multistep planning during vulnerability discovery and exploitation tasks.

items.name: Detect Anything via Next Point Prediction
items.summary: Introduces Rex-Omni, a general visual perception model trained for coordinate prediction; GUI grounding is one capability evaluated alongside detection and OCR.

items.name: In-Browser LLM-Guided Fuzzing for Real-Time Prompt Injection Testing in Agentic AI Browsers
items.summary: Proposes an in-browser fuzzing framework that uses language-model guidance to test indirect prompt-injection vulnerabilities in agentic browsers. The work focuses on unwanted actions triggered by webpage instructions under the browser agent's user privileges.

items.name: ReUseIt: Synthesizing Reusable AI Agent Workflows for Web Automation
items.summary: Introduces ReUseIt, which synthesizes reusable web-agent workflows from successful and failed attempts and adds guards to detect and fix execution errors.

items.name: Hi-Agent: Hierarchical Vision-Language Agents for Mobile Device Control
items.summary: Introduces Hi-Agent, jointly training a high-level reasoning model and a low-level mobile action model. Execution feedback supplies a foresight advantage for optimizing subgoal decisions, with evaluations on Android control benchmarks.

items.name: WebAggregator: Enhancing Compositional Reasoning Capabilities of Deep Research Agent Foundation Models
items.summary: Introduces WebAggregator, a pipeline for synthesizing compositional questions from websites to train deep-research agents, plus the WebAggregatorQA testbed.

items.name: State Your Intention to Steer Your Attention: An AI Assistant for Intentional Digital Living
items.summary: Introduces an assistant that reads screenshots, application titles, and URLs to compare computer activity with a user's stated intention and send notifications when it diverges.

items.name: Agentic Entropy-Balanced Policy Optimization
items.summary: Introduces Agentic Entropy-Balanced Policy Optimization (AEPO), an RL method that adjusts rollout sampling and policy updates for tool-using web agents.

items.name: ColorBench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents with Graph-Structured Framework for Complex Long-Horizon Tasks
items.summary: ColorBench represents mobile tasks as graphs of states collected from real devices, providing a quasi-dynamic environment with multiple valid paths and error paths. It evaluates single-app and cross-app tasks using completion, subtask progress, and atomic diagnostics.

items.name: LLMs as Scalable, General-Purpose Simulators For Evolving Digital Agent Training
items.summary: Introduces UI-Simulator, which generates UI states and transitions for agent-training trajectories, and UI-Simulator-Grow, which prioritizes tasks and trajectory variants.

items.name: CORE: Reducing UI Exposure in Mobile Agents via Collaboration Between Cloud and Local LLMs
items.summary: Introduces CORE, which divides mobile UI hierarchies into semantic blocks and shares planning between local and cloud language models. Local ranking limits the screen information sent for cloud-side element selection, with a multi-round mechanism for correcting inadequate context.

items.name: PolySkill: Learning Generalizable Skills Through Polymorphic Abstraction
items.summary: Introduces PolySkill, which separates a web-agent skill's goal from its execution so agents can learn and reuse skills across websites.

items.name: GUIrilla: A Scalable Framework for Automated Desktop UI Exploration
items.summary: GUIrilla systematically explores macOS interfaces to collect interaction traces and accessibility metadata for downstream GUI research. It organizes these observations into hierarchical MacApp Trees and describes an accessibility-driven collection library.

items.name: WEBSERV: A Full-Stack and RL-Ready Web Environment for Training Web Agents at Scale
items.summary: WebServ combines copy-on-write container environments with a compact DOM-derived browser interface for training web agents. Network-aware waiting supports action execution in single-page applications, with evaluations and reinforcement-learning experiments on WebArena-Lite.

items.name: Beyond Pipelines: A Survey of the Paradigm Shift toward Model-Native Agentic AI
items.summary: Surveys model-native agentic AI and the role of RL in learned planning, tool use and memory, covering GUI agents as one application alongside deep-research agents.

items.name: UltraCUA: A Foundation Model for Computer Use Agents with Hybrid Action
items.summary: UltraCUA trains a shared policy for primitive GUI actions and high-level tool calls using synthesized tasks and hybrid trajectories. Supervised fine-tuning followed by online reinforcement learning is evaluated on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.

items.name: Investigating the Impact of Dark Patterns on LLM-Based Web Agents
items.summary: Presents LiteAgent for recording web-agent interactions and TrickyArena for enabling or disabling dark patterns in controlled websites. Experiments compare how individual patterns, combined patterns and visual or HTML changes affect agent decisions.

items.name: Genesis: Evolving Attack Strategies for LLM Web Agent Red-Teaming
items.summary: Introduces Genesis, a red-teaming framework that generates adversarial injections for web agents and revises attack strategies using responses and interaction logs.

items.name: AndroidControl-Curated: Revealing the True Potential of GUI Agents through Benchmark Purification
items.summary: AndroidControl-Curated audits ambiguities and factual errors in AndroidControl and produces a refined evaluation dataset. The paper also studies post-training a small Magma-R1 model on a curated subset to examine the effect of data quality on GUI action assessment.

items.name: CUARewardBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Reward Models on Computer-using Agent
items.summary: Introduces CUARewardBench for evaluating outcome and process reward models on annotated computer-use trajectories, plus Unanimous Prompt Ensemble (UPE) for reward judgments.

items.name: WebGraphEval: Multi-Turn Trajectory Evaluation for Web Agents using Graph Representation
items.summary: Introduces WebGraphEval, which merges multiple agents' trajectories into a weighted graph of canonical actions. Structural analyses examine recurring behavior, inefficient paths and important decision points beyond a final success score.

items.name: See, Think, Act: Online Shopper Behavior Simulation with VLM Agents
items.summary: Studies online shopper action prediction with VLM agents using webpage screenshots, HTML, and action history from OPeRA, trained with SFT and hierarchical RL rewards.

items.name: SheetBrain: A Neuro-Symbolic Agent for Accurate Reasoning over Complex and Large Spreadsheets
items.summary: Introduces SheetBrain, a spreadsheet question-answering and manipulation agent that uses a Python sandbox and Excel tools, plus the SheetBench benchmark.

items.name: ColorAgent: Building A Robust, Personalized, and Interactive OS Agent
items.summary: Presents ColorAgent, an operating system agent for long-horizon user instructions, trained with step-wise RL and self-evolving training and evaluated on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

items.name: VideoAgentTrek: Computer Use Pretraining from Unlabeled Videos
items.summary: Extracts structured GUI actions from screen-recorded tutorials using inverse dynamics, then uses the inferred trajectories for computer-use training.

items.name: Branch-and-Browse: Efficient and Controllable Web Exploration with Tree-Structured Reasoning and Action Memory
items.summary: Branch-and-Browse is a web agent framework that uses tree-structured subtasks, web state replay, and page action memory to explore and complete tasks.

items.name: Surfer 2: The Next Generation of Cross-Platform Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Surfer2 combines hierarchical context management with separate planning and execution, self-verification, and recovery for visual computer use. It evaluates the framework across web, desktop, and Android tasks without task-specific fine-tuning.

items.name: UI-Ins: Enhancing GUI Grounding with Multi-Perspective Instruction-as-Reasoning
items.summary: Treats alternative instruction formulations as reasoning paths and trains GUI-grounding models to select and combine useful perspectives.

items.name: GhostEI-Bench: Do Mobile Agents Resilience to Environmental Injection in Dynamic On-Device Environments?
items.summary: Introduces GhostEI-Bench, a benchmark that injects deceptive UI events into Android emulator workflows to assess mobile agents and analyze failures from actions and screenshots.

items.name: Mixing Importance with Diversity: Joint Optimization for KV Cache Compression in Large Vision-Language Models
items.summary: MixKV compresses vision-language model KV caches by balancing importance and diversity; its evaluations include GUI grounding alongside broader multimodal tasks.

items.name: OpenPhone: Mobile Agentic Foundation Models
items.summary: OpenPhone trains a compact mobile policy with supervised learning followed by GRPO on synthetic GUI data, incorporating reasoning and memory management. Its device-cloud design handles routine work locally and delegates complex subtasks, with online evaluation on AndroidLab.

items.name: Mitigating Coordinate Prediction Bias from Positional Encoding Failures
items.summary: Introduces Vision-PE Shuffle Guidance (VPSG), a training-free correction for coordinate drift in visual models, evaluated for localization on ScreenSpot-Pro.

items.name: WebATLAS: An LLM Agent with Experience-Driven Memory and Action Simulation
items.summary: WebATLAS is a web agent that stores interaction outcomes and simulates candidate actions before acting, using past experience to plan navigation on unseen websites.

items.name: MGA: Memory-Driven GUI Agent for Observation-Centric Interaction
items.summary: Introduces MGA, which separates task-agnostic screen-state reading from decision making and connects steps through structured state memory. Validated state deltas replace full trajectory replay, evaluated on OSWorld and application tasks.

items.name: OS-Sentinel: Towards Safety-Enhanced Mobile GUI Agents via Hybrid Validation in Realistic Workflows
items.summary: Introduces MobileRisk-Live and OS-Sentinel, combining a formal verifier for system-level violations with a multimodal judge for contextual risks in mobile GUI workflows.

items.name: OSWorld-MCP: Benchmarking MCP Tool Invocation In Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: OSWorld-MCP evaluates how agents choose between GUI operations and MCP tool calls in computer tasks. It combines generated and curated tools, with 158 manually validated tools across seven applications, to examine tool use alongside task completion.

items.name: Agent Data Protocol: Unifying Datasets for Diverse, Effective Fine-tuning of LLM Agents
items.summary: The agent data protocol (ADP) provides a shared format for agent training data across browsing, tool use, coding, and other tasks, including web agent workflows.

items.name: GUI Knowledge Bench: Revealing the Knowledge Gap of VLMs in GUI Tasks
items.summary: GUI Knowledge Bench tests knowledge of widgets, interactions, and procedures across six named platforms and 292 applications to assess VLMs used for GUI tasks.

items.name: Measuring the Security of Mobile LLM Agents under Adversarial Prompts from Untrusted Third-Party Channels
items.summary: Measures how untrusted third-party notifications, messages, and app content can hijack mobile LLM agents into executing unauthorized cross-app actions.

items.name: GUI-Rise: Structured Reasoning and History Summarization for GUI Navigation
items.summary: Combines structured progress-and-decision reasoning with history summarization to improve cross-domain generalization in GUI navigation agents.

items.name: Enhancing Trustworthy GUI Grounding via Self-Critiqued Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: HyperClick trains GUI grounders to produce a click and an accompanying confidence estimate using rewards for correctness and confidence alignment. Its evaluation examines localization, calibration, and abstention behavior.

items.name: GUI-AIMA: Aligning Intrinsic Multimodal Attention with a Context Anchor for GUI Grounding
items.summary: Introduces GUI-AIMA, which supervises instruction-relevant attention over visual patches. Patch-level grounding can be combined with an optional zoom stage and is evaluated across GUI localization benchmarks.

items.name: Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis
items.summary: DreamGym synthesizes agent experiences with a reasoning-based environment model for online RL; its evaluations include the web task setting WebArena.

items.name: Learning from Online Videos at Inference Time for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: This work retrieves online video tutorials and converts them into structured GUI action demonstrations with short objectives. A two-stage selection process supplies a relevant local trajectory as in-context guidance at each execution step.

items.name: GUI-360$^\circ$: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for Computer-Using Agents
items.summary: Collects Windows application trajectories with screenshots and action traces for grounding, screen parsing, and action prediction.

items.name: SynthAgent: Adapting Web Agents with Synthetic Supervision
items.summary: Introduces SynthAgent, which generates tasks by exploring website elements and refines them when observations reveal conflicts. A later trajectory-refinement stage removes misaligned behavior before fine-tuning agents for the target websites.

items.name: WebVIA: A Web-based Vision-Language Agentic Framework for Interactive and Verifiable UI-to-Code Generation
items.summary: WebVIA combines a web UI exploration agent, interactive UI-to-Code generation, and validation of generated code's interactivity.

items.name: AUTO-Explorer: Automated Data Collection for GUI Agent
items.summary: Introduces Auto-Explorer, an automated GUI exploration method that records software states for training-data collection. UIXplore evaluates exploration coverage, and collected data is used to fine-tune and test GUI element grounding.

items.name: Grounding Computer Use Agents on Human Demonstrations
items.summary: GroundCUA turns expert desktop demonstrations into densely annotated screenshots and grounding instructions. The GroundNext model family uses this supervision and subsequent reinforcement learning, with both grounding benchmarks and an OSWorld agent configuration used for evaluation.

items.name: An Efficient Training Pipeline for Reasoning Graphical User Interface Agents
items.summary: A GUI grounding pipeline filters 4.8M synthetic examples to 12K training instances and adapts a 3B vision-language model, evaluated on ScreenSpot, Multimodal-Mind2Web, and AndroidControl.

items.name: AgentPRM: Process Reward Models for LLM Agents via Step-Wise Promise and Progress
items.summary: AgentPRM scores sequential agent decisions by their promise and progress toward a goal, with web shopping and browser navigation among the motivating tasks.

items.name: History-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents
items.summary: HAR-GUI combines episodic reasoning and short-term memory to use earlier interactions when selecting GUI actions. Its training constructs reflective scenarios and correction guidance and applies a hybrid reinforcement-learning reward to the 3B policy.

items.name: ProBench: Benchmarking GUI Agents with Accurate Process Information
items.summary: ProBench extends mobile GUI evaluation with tasks whose correctness depends on the interaction process as well as the final state. Its ProcessProvider supplies process information for assessing agent behavior and analyzing failure modes.

items.name: TaskSense: Cognitive Chain Modeling and Difficulty Estimation for GUI Tasks
items.summary: Cognitive Chain estimates GUI task difficulty by extracting sequences of cognitive steps from execution traces, then uses those estimates to assess GUI agents.

items.name: Co-EPG: A Framework for Co-Evolution of Planning and Grounding in Autonomous GUI Agents
items.summary: Co-EPG alternates reinforcement learning for a planner with updates to a grounding model using generated training examples. The evolving grounder provides feedback to the planner, and evaluation uses Multimodal Mind2Web and AndroidControl.

items.name: OSGym: Scalable OS Infra for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: OSGym supplies full operating-system sandboxes with GUIs for parallel computer-use data collection and training. It combines per-replica state management, hardware-aware orchestration, copy-on-write virtual-machine disks, and layered failure recovery.

items.name: Mobile-Agent-RAG: Driving Smart Multi-Agent Coordination with Contextual Knowledge Empowerment for Long-Horizon Mobile Automation
items.summary: Uses separate retrieval systems for high-level mobile-task planning and precise interface operations, with a benchmark for extended cross-app tasks.

items.name: WebCoach: Self-Evolving Web Agents with Cross-Session Memory Guidance
items.summary: Introduces WebCoach, which condenses navigation logs into persistent episodic memory and retrieves experiences by similarity and recency. Runtime hooks selectively supply advice to browser agents, evaluated on WebVoyager without retraining the underlying models.

items.name: MEGA-GUI: Multi-stage Enhanced Grounding Agents for GUI Elements
items.summary: Introduces MEGA-GUI, which separates coarse region selection from fine-grained interface-element grounding. Bidirectional zooming and context-aware instruction rewriting coordinate specialized vision-language agents across visual scales.

items.name: STEP: Success-Rate-Aware Trajectory-Efficient Policy Optimization
items.summary: STEP allocates RL sampling by task success rate and trains on individual steps from interaction trajectories, with evaluations on OSWorld and AndroidWorld.

items.name: DualTAP: A Dual-Task Adversarial Protector for Mobile MLLM Agents
items.summary: Applies dual-task adversarial perturbations to mobile screenshots to conceal personally identifiable information from untrusted MLLM routers while preserving agent task utility.

items.name: Can We Stop Malicious AI? KILLBENCH: A Benchmark for External AI Kill Switch Feasibility
items.summary: KillBench evaluates external prompt-style signals intended to halt maliciously operating web agents, across harmful scenarios and agent configurations.

items.name: Computer-Use Agents as Judges for Generative User Interface
items.summary: AUI-Gym evaluates generated websites by having computer-use agents attempt tasks whose executability is checked programmatically. A feedback dashboard condenses navigation histories into visual summaries that a coding agent can use to revise an interface.

items.name: D-GARA: A Dynamic Benchmarking Framework for GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
items.summary: D-GARA evaluates Android GUI agents under runtime anomalies such as permission dialogs, battery warnings, and update prompts. Its modular environment embeds these interruptions in Android applications to study recovery and robustness.

items.name: UI-CUBE: Enterprise-Grade Computer Use Agent Benchmarking Beyond Task Accuracy to Operational Reliability
items.summary: UI-CUBE evaluates 226 tasks ranging from individual controls to copy-paste and enterprise workflows. Interface variations, multiple resolutions, and application-state validation support diagnosis of operational reliability beyond task accuracy alone.

items.name: Building Browser Agents: Architecture, Security, and Practical Solutions
items.summary: Reports architectural and security lessons from building a browser agent, including hybrid accessibility-tree and visual context, browser tooling and programmatic constraints. A WebGames evaluation accompanies the discussion of reliability and specialization.

items.name: Fara-7B: An Efficient Agentic Model for Computer Use
items.summary: Introduces FaraGen synthetic web trajectories, a compact screenshot-based action model, and WebTailBench for underrepresented browser tasks.

items.name: AppSelectBench: Application-Level Tool Selection Benchmark
items.summary: AppSelectBench evaluates whether computer-using agents choose the right desktop application for a task, using generated user intents and multiple evaluation protocols.

items.name: "Are We Done Yet?": A Vision-Based Judge for Autonomous Task Completion of Computer Use Agents
items.summary: This study tests vision-language models as task-completion judges using screenshots and instructions from 42 built-in macOS applications. It evaluates judgment accuracy on human-labeled tasks and separately studies how judge feedback affects agent task success.

items.name: BrowseSafe: Understanding and Preventing Prompt Injection Within AI Browser Agents
items.summary: BrowseSafe builds a benchmark of prompt injections in realistic HTML for browser agents and evaluates defenses against attacks that can affect agent actions.

items.name: OpenApps: Simulating Environment Variations to Measure UI-Agent Reliability
items.summary: Introduces OpenApps, a configurable app ecosystem for measuring UI-agent reliability under changes in appearance and content. Its evaluation compares task success and failure behavior across many versions of the same apps.

items.name: Prune4Web: DOM Tree Pruning Programming for Web Agent
items.summary: Introduces Prune4Web, where generated scoring programs filter DOM elements according to decomposed subtasks before grounding. An annotation pipeline and two-turn training procedure coordinate the planner, programmatic filter and grounder.

items.name: Qwen3-VL Technical Report
items.summary: Describes the Qwen3-VL dense and MoE vision-language models, with 256K-token interleaved context, interleaved-MRoPE, DeepStack and textual video timestamps; a general foundation model aimed partly at agentic use.

items.name: Real-Time Procedural Learning From Experience for AI Agents
items.summary: PRAXIS stores action outcomes and retrieves past state-action-result examples to guide agent decisions, with evaluation on the REAL web browsing benchmark.

items.name: Training High-Level Schedulers with Execution-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon GUI Automation
items.summary: This work trains high-level schedulers with staged reinforcement learning driven by execution feedback. Its CES framework separates a Coordinator for planning and decomposition, a StateTracker for compressed context, and a low-level Executor.

items.name: MCP vs RAG vs NLWeb vs HTML: A Comparison of the Effectiveness and Efficiency of Different Agent Interfaces to the Web (Technical Report)
items.summary: Compares HTML browsing, RAG, MCP, and NLWeb interfaces for web agents performing product search, comparison, and checkout tasks in four simulated e-shops.

items.name: MPR-GUI: Benchmarking and Enhancing Multilingual Perception and Reasoning in GUI Agents
items.summary: MPR-GUI evaluates GUI perception and reasoning through strictly aligned tasks in six languages. GUI-XLI adjusts non-English hidden representations toward English representations at language-sensitive layers during inference to address the measured cross-language gaps.

items.name: AFRAgent : An Adaptive Feature Renormalization Based High Resolution Aware GUI agent
items.summary: Introduces AFRAgent, which uses adaptive feature renormalization to combine low-resolution visual embeddings with high-resolution details. The architecture is evaluated for smartphone GUI automation on Meta-GUI and AITW.

items.name: DrawingBench: Evaluating Spatial Reasoning and UI Interaction Capabilities of Large Language Models through Mouse-Based Drawing Tasks
items.summary: DrawingBench evaluates sequences of low-level mouse-based GUI actions through 250 drawing prompts and rule-based criteria. Action inspection and multi-turn external feedback support analysis of spatial reasoning, tool-state management, and refinement.

items.name: HiconAgent: History Context-aware Policy Optimization for GUI Agents
items.summary: HiconAgent trains GUI policies to use history through variable-length context sampling and paired policy updates with compressed and complete histories. Its compression retains past actions while removing historical observations, and an alignment loss couples the two branches.

items.name: Chain-of-Ground: Improving GUI Grounding via Iterative Reasoning and Reference Feedback
items.summary: Chain-of-Ground uses iterative visual reasoning and reference feedback to refine GUI localization without additional training. It evaluates on ScreenSpot-Pro and introduces TPanel-UI to probe grounding on industrial control panels with visual distortions.

items.name: GUI Exploration Lab: Enhancing Screen Navigation in Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Introduces GUI Exploration Lab, a simulation engine for composing screens, interface elements, and navigation graphs. It studies how supervised learning, single-turn RL, and multiturn RL affect GUI navigation and exploration.

items.name: LegalWebAgent: Empowering Access to Justice via LLM-Based Web Agents
items.summary: LegalWebAgent separates user-needs clarification, webpage browsing, and actions such as form completion or scheduling. A 15-task evaluation studies legal-service workflows relevant to Québec civil-law users, using HTML and screenshot observations.

items.name: Zoom in, Click out: Unlocking and Evaluating the Potential of Zooming for GUI Grounding
items.summary: ZoomClick uses repeated zooming and context adjustment to improve GUI grounding without training. The paper studies zoom depth, crop sizes, and related choices and introduces GUIZoom-Bench to evaluate how grounding models respond to zoomed views.

items.name: Privacy Practices of Browser Agents
items.summary: Presents a privacy evaluation framework for browser agents covering component weaknesses, website defenses, tracking, privacy-related prompts and personal-data leakage. The framework is applied to deployed browser-agent tools.

items.name: MVP: Multiple View Prediction Improves GUI Grounding
items.summary: MVP addresses unstable GUI coordinates by predicting across several attention-guided cropped views. It clusters the resulting coordinates and selects the densest cluster centroid, evaluating this training-free inference method across grounding models.

items.name: GAIR: GUI Automation via Information-Joint Reasoning and Group Reflection
items.summary: Introduces GAIR, which combines information from specialized GUI models through a general-purpose coordinating model. When the available information is insufficient, group reflection sends targeted requests back to the specialists before selecting an operation.

items.name: AgentProg: Empowering Long-Horizon GUI Agents with Program-Guided Context Management
items.summary: Introduces AgentProg, organizing mobile-agent interaction history as a program with variables and control flow to decide what context to retain. A global belief state handles partial observability, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and extended long-horizon tasks.

items.name: WebSTAR: Scalable Data Synthesis for Computer Use Agents with Step-Level Filtering
items.summary: Introduces a pipeline that filters individual steps from noisy computer-agent rollouts and augments them with reasoning for training. WebSTAR and WebSCORE support GUI-policy supervision and a distilled process reward model, StepRM.

items.name: Using GUI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
items.summary: GUI-EDA collects more than 2,000 screenshot-answer-action pairs from engineers working across five CAD tools and five physical domains. The accompanying benchmark evaluates more than 30 GUI agents on specialized electronic-design workflows.

items.name: ceLLMate: Sandboxing Browser AI Agents
items.summary: ceLLMate constrains browser-agent authority through an extension that applies policies at the HTTP layer. It evaluates this sandbox against prompt-injection attacks in WASP, avoiding dependence on brittle low-level click and keystroke policies.

items.name: MobiBench: Multi-Branch, Modular Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: MobiBench evaluates mobile GUI agents offline while allowing multiple valid action paths. It decomposes agent pipelines into modules to study component contributions, configurations, and performance bottlenecks.

items.name: WebOperator: Action-Aware Tree Search for Autonomous Agents in Web Environment
items.summary: WebOperator uses tree search, action filtering, and path checks before replay to explore web tasks and backtrack while accounting for irreversible actions.

items.name: MobileWorldBench: Towards Semantic World Modeling For Mobile Agents
items.summary: Evaluates semantic world models for mobile interfaces and studies natural-language state transitions as a tool for agent planning.

items.name: Step-GUI Technical Report
items.summary: Step-GUI uses calibrated trajectory rewards to turn generated GUI interaction data into training signals for compact agent models. The report also introduces GUI-MCP for hierarchical GUI operations and local task delegation, and AndroidDaily for static-action and end-to-end mobile evaluation.

items.name: OS-Oracle: A Comprehensive Framework for Cross-Platform GUI Critic Models
items.summary: OS-Oracle synthesizes GUI critic examples and trains a pre-action critic with supervised learning followed by consistency-preserving GRPO. It introduces OS-Critic Bench across mobile, web, and desktop settings and tests critic-assisted agents in OSWorld and AndroidWorld.

items.name: VenusBench-GD: A Comprehensive Multi-Platform GUI Benchmark for Diverse Grounding Tasks
items.summary: VenusBench-GD is a bilingual, cross-platform GUI grounding benchmark organized into basic and advanced tasks. Its annotation pipeline and six-subtask taxonomy support comparisons of general multimodal models and GUI-specialized models across different grounding demands.

items.name: DAVE: A VLM Vision Encoder for Document Understanding and Web Agents
items.summary: DAVE trains a vision encoder for document images and web agents using self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised parsing and localization. It combines decoder-specific encoder merging with feature fusion and evaluates web localization and agent benchmarks alongside document tasks.

items.name: EchoTrail-GUI: Building Actionable Memory for GUI Agents via Critic-Guided Self-Exploration
items.summary: EchoTrail-GUI builds a memory of successful GUI trajectories through autonomous exploration filtered by a reward model. It retrieves relevant trajectories as in-context guidance for new tasks and evaluates the approach on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

items.name: MobileWorld: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents in Agent-User Interactive and MCP-Augmented Environments
items.summary: Introduces long mobile workflows that combine agent-user interaction, cross-application tasks, and MCP-based tool access.

items.name: AndroidLens: Long-latency Evaluation with Nested Sub-targets for Android GUI Agents
items.summary: AndroidLens provides 571 extended mobile tasks in Chinese and English, with multiple valid paths and preserved environmental anomalies. Its dynamic evaluation uses nested milestones and Average Task Progress to measure partial completion of long workflows.

items.name: iSHIFT: Lightweight Slow-Fast GUI Agent with Adaptive Perception
items.summary: Introduces iSHIFT, which combines latent reasoning with perception-control tokens to adapt GUI inference. The agent switches between detailed regional grounding and faster use of global visual cues.

items.name: MAI-UI Technical Report: Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
items.summary: MAI-UI combines GUI navigation, native user interaction, and MCP tool calls in a family of policies trained through generated data and online reinforcement learning.
