The report also studies device-cloud routing and scaling of parallel environments and interaction budgets, with grounding and Android navigation evaluation.

items.name: SmartSnap: Proactive Evidence Seeking for Self-Verifying Agents
items.summary: SmartSnap trains GUI agents to collect concise screenshot evidence of task completion for an LLM judge, with experiments on mobile tasks.

items.name: DECEPTICON: How Dark Patterns Manipulate Web Agents
items.summary: DECEPTICON is an environment of 700 web navigation tasks that isolates dark patterns to measure how deceptive interface designs steer agent actions.
items.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations

items.name: It's a TRAP! Task-Redirecting Agent Persuasion Benchmark for Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces TRAP, which evaluates task-redirection attacks embedded in realistic web interfaces. Controlled website clones and a modular injection framework support comparisons of persuasion techniques and contextual changes across agents.

items.name: Nested Browser-Use Learning for Agentic Information Seeking
items.summary: NestBrowse organizes browser actions in a nested framework that separates interaction control from page exploration. It evaluates this design for deep information seeking beyond snippet retrieval and direct URL fetching.

items.name: ShowUI-$π$: Flow-based Generative Models as GUI Dexterous Hands
items.summary: Models discrete clicks and continuous drags with flow-based action generation, and introduces drag trajectories and the ScreenDrag benchmark.

items.name: Permission Manifests for Web Agents
items.summary: Proposes agent-permissions.json, a website manifest for declaring which interactions web agents may perform, with optional references to APIs.

items.name: ProSoftArena: Benchmarking Hierarchical Capabilities of Multimodal Agents in Professional Software Environments
items.summary: ProSoftArena evaluates 436 professional-software tasks across six disciplines and 13 applications in a Windows 11 virtual-machine environment. Its capability hierarchy, execution-based checks, and human-in-the-loop evaluation cover precise GUI operations and multi-software workflows.

items.name: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
items.summary: WebGym supplies realistic web tasks with rubric-based evaluation and an asynchronous rollout system for reinforcement learning. It studies how training on an agent’s own interaction traces scales with task coverage and transfers to unseen websites.

items.name: Agent-Dice: Disentangling Knowledge Updates via Geometric Consensus for Agent Continual Learning
items.summary: Agent-Dice fuses parameter updates to support continual learning in LLM agents, with GUI agent tasks evaluated alongside tool-use domains.

items.name: FocusUI: Efficient UI Grounding via Position-Preserving Visual Token Selection
items.summary: FocusUI selects instruction-relevant screenshot patches while preserving their positional structure for GUI grounding. Its PosPad scheme replaces runs of dropped tokens with positional markers and is evaluated under reduced token budgets.

items.name: MobileDreamer: Generative Sketch World Model for GUI Agent
items.summary: MobileDreamer predicts post-action GUI states as task-relevant textual sketches with an order-invariant learning objective. Agents use these predictions for lookahead action selection, evaluated on AndroidWorld.

items.name: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
items.summary: InfiniteWeb generates functional, interconnected websites and task evaluators using shared specifications and task-driven development. It evaluates website construction and the transfer of GUI policies trained in these synthetic web environments to OSWorld and Online-Mind2Web.

items.name: FronTalk: Benchmarking Front-End Development as Conversational Code Generation with Multi-Modal Feedback
items.summary: FronTalk benchmarks multi-turn front-end code generation from text and visual feedback; a web agent explores generated sites for evaluation and in AceCoder.

items.name: GUITester: Enabling GUI Agents for Exploratory Defect Discovery
items.summary: Introduces GUITestBench for interactive defect discovery and GUITester, which separates task navigation from anomaly verification. Testing-oriented plans and history-based reflection help distinguish software defects from agent execution mistakes.

items.name: From Off-Policy to On-Policy: Enhancing GUI Agents via Bi-level Expert-to-Policy Assimilation
items.summary: BEPA adapts a small set of expert GUI traces into policy-aligned guidance through trajectories reachable by the learner and a dynamically updated task cache. It evaluates this two-level approach to reinforcement learning on desktop and web benchmarks.

items.name: Beyond Clicking:A Step Towards Generalist GUI Grounding via Text Dragging
items.summary: GUI-Drag provides synthesized text-dragging examples, while ScreenDrag benchmarks selecting text by dragging across varied GUI contexts.

items.name: ShowUI-Aloha: Human-Taught GUI Agent
items.summary: Transforms human screen recordings and input events into annotated demonstrations used by planning and execution components for GUI tasks.

items.name: ColorBrowserAgent: Complex Long-Horizon Browser Agent with Adaptive Knowledge Evolution
items.summary: ColorBrowserAgent converts human feedback into reusable website knowledge and uses that knowledge to guide progressive context summaries. It evaluates the resulting memory and adaptation mechanisms on long browser workflows.

items.name: When Bots Take the Bait: Exposing and Mitigating the Emerging Social Engineering Attack in Web Automation Agent
items.summary: Studies deceptive social-engineering web patterns targeting browser automation agents and proposes defenses against bait-based manipulation.

items.name: OS-Symphony: A Holistic Framework for Robust and Generalist Computer-Using Agent
items.summary: OS-Symphony coordinates milestone-based reflection and memory with tools that build visually aligned tutorials through browser interaction. The framework evaluates trajectory correction and adaptation on online computer-use benchmarks including OSWorld.

items.name: WebTrap Park: An Automated Platform for Systematic Security Evaluation of Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces WebTrap Park, a platform that turns web-agent security risks into executable tasks and assesses concrete interactions with live pages. It compares agent frameworks without requiring modifications to their implementations.

items.name: ExpSeek: Self-Triggered Experience Seeking for Web Agents
items.summary: ExpSeek uses step-level entropy signals to decide when a web agent should request experience-based guidance. It supplies guidance tailored to the current step and evaluates the intervention across web-agent benchmarks.

items.name: PersonalAlign: Hierarchical Implicit Intent Alignment for Personalized GUI Agent with Long-Term User-Centric Records
items.summary: Introduces AndroidIntent to evaluate how GUI agents infer omitted preferences and recurring routines from long-term user records. Its HIM-Agent maintains hierarchical memory of preferences and routines for personalized execution and proactive suggestions.

items.name: GUI-Eyes: Tool-Augmented Perception for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
items.summary: GUI-Eyes trains GUI grounders to decide when and how to use visual tools such as crops and zooms. Its coarse-to-fine policy uses dense spatial rewards based on location proximity and region overlap, with evaluation on ScreenSpot-Pro.

items.name: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: System-level Security for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: NOVA separates trusted task planning from screen-derived observations by producing a branching plan before execution and resolving runtime values through perception. Its OSWorld study examines security and utility while identifying remaining risks from perception-driven branch steering.

items.name: Compress to Focus: Efficient Coordinate Compression for Policy Optimization in Multi-Turn GUI Agents
items.summary: CCPO couples GUI policy optimization with coordinate-guided compression of past visual observations. It aggregates targets across rollouts to focus retained context and uses distance-based advantages to train grounding and compression together.

items.name: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
items.summary: Terminal-Bench 2.0 benchmarks agents on 89 workflow-inspired tasks in computer terminal environments, with a distinct environment, human solution and verification tests for each task.

items.name: Mind the Gap: Action Rebinding Attacks against Android GUI Agents
items.summary: Studies action-rebinding attacks in which an Android GUI agent’s planned input is redirected to a different application during the observation–action delay. The evaluation examines cross-application execution and the consequences of treating an earlier screen as the current action target.

items.name: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI): Architectures, Taxonomies, and Evaluation of Large Language Model Agents
items.summary: Surveys LLM agent architectures, operating environments and evaluation, covering web navigation and native computer use alongside other agent domains.

items.name: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction
items.summary: MirrorGuard trains a reasoning-correction defense using GUI risk trajectories generated in a text-based neural-symbolic simulator. It evaluates whether corrections transfer to computer-use agents operating real interfaces, keeping simulated training separate from deployment tests.

items.name: MagicGUI-RMS: A Multi-Agent Reward Model System for Self-Evolving GUI Agents via Automated Feedback Reflux
items.summary: MagicGUI-RMS combines domain-specific and general reward models to assess GUI actions and propose corrections. A structured data pipeline and feedback-recycling process support repeated reward-model and agent improvement.

items.name: EvoCUA: Evolving Computer Use Agents via Learning from Scalable Synthetic Experience
items.summary: EvoCUA combines task synthesis with executable validators, asynchronous sandbox rollouts and iterative policy updates. It turns successful routines and analyzed failures into supervision and evaluates the evolving agent on OSWorld.

items.name: Computer Environments Elicit General Agentic Intelligence in LLMs
items.summary: LLM-in-Sandbox gives agents a minimal computer environment for resource access, file management and code execution; LLM-in-Sandbox-RL trains models to use it.

items.name: The Behavioral Fabric of LLM-Powered GUI Agents: Human Values and Interaction Outcomes
items.summary: Introduces a controlled web-task testbed for studying how stated preferences and human values influence GUI-agent decisions. It analyzes how personas alter navigation and how prominent interface cues can override the intended preference guidance.

items.name: GraphPilot: GUI Task Automation with One-Step LLM Reasoning Powered by Knowledge Graph
items.summary: GraphPilot builds app-specific knowledge graphs from explored pages, elements and transitions, then uses them to plan action sequences. It requests additional interface observations when uncertain and checks plans against graph transition rules before correction and execution.

items.name: EntWorld: A Holistic Environment and Benchmark for Verifiable Enterprise GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces EntWorld, an enterprise GUI benchmark built by deriving task logic from database schemas. Long workflows across enterprise domains are assessed with deterministic SQL-based state checks.

items.name: From Struggle to Success: Context-Aware Guidance for Screen Reader Users in Computer Use
items.summary: Introduces AskEase, an on-demand assistant that combines contextual information to provide screen-reader-friendly computer-use guidance. A study with screen-reader users evaluates task completion and perceived workload while preserving human control of the interaction.

items.name: MalURLBench: A Benchmark Evaluating Agents' Vulnerabilities When Processing Web URLs
items.summary: MalURLBench evaluates how LLM-based web agents handle disguised malicious URLs across attack scenarios; the paper also analyzes attack factors and proposes URLGuard.

items.name: GAIA: A Data Flywheel System for Training GUI Test-Time Scaling Critic Models
items.summary: GAIA trains a GUI action critic on positive and negative examples, then uses that critic to collect improved examples for another training round. It studies how recycling these data affects the test-time action choices of different GUI agents.

items.name: SwipeGen: Bridging the Execution Gap in GUI Agents via Human-like Swipe Synthesis
items.summary: Introduces SwipeGen for synthesizing varied swipe trajectories and SwipeBench for assessing their execution quality. The study examines how richer control of trajectory, speed, and timing changes GUI agents’ interaction performance.

items.name: GUIGuard-Bench: Toward a General Evaluation for Privacy-Preserving GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces GUIGuard-Bench, which annotates private regions in GUI trajectories with categories, risk levels, and relevance to the user’s task. It evaluates privacy recognition and the effect of screenshot protection on offline planning and task utility.

items.name: MAGNET: Towards Adaptive GUI Agents with Memory-Driven Knowledge Evolution
items.summary: MAGNET maintains separate memories for stable interface functions and task procedures across changing layouts and workflows. It updates frequently used knowledge and evaluates adaptation in AndroidWorld and offline distribution-shift settings.

items.name: Curiosity Driven Knowledge Retrieval for Mobile Agents
items.summary: Uses execution uncertainty to trigger retrieval from application documentation, code, and past trajectories, organizing the results into structured AppCards for Android agent planning.

items.name: Me-Agent: A Personalized Mobile Agent with Two-Level User Habit Learning for Enhanced Interaction
items.summary: Me-Agent personalizes mobile agent behavior through a preference reward model and hierarchical memory for long-term and app-specific habits, and introduces User FingerTip.

items.name: MobileBench-OL: A Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Evaluating Mobile GUI Agents in Real-World Environment
items.summary: Introduces MobileBench-OL, an online benchmark of Chinese-app tasks spanning execution, reasoning, exploration, and noisy conditions. Its automatic evaluation and reset framework supports repeated testing of mobile GUI agents in real environments.

items.name: OmegaUse: Building a General-Purpose GUI Agent for Autonomous Task Execution
items.summary: OmegaUse combines exploratory and taxonomy-guided data synthesis with supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO for GUI control. The report introduces OS-Nav for offline Android and Ubuntu evaluation alongside established grounding and action-prediction benchmarks.

items.name: OS-Marathon: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents on Vast-Horizon, Repetitive Tasks
items.summary: Introduces OS-Marathon to evaluate long repetitive computer-use workflows whose execution grows with the amount of input data. It studies failure accumulation under task decomposition and GraphDemo, which adapts agents using a demonstration of the recurring workflow.

items.name: Continual GUI Agents
items.summary: Continual GUI Agents defines grounding under changing application domains and screen resolutions. Its GUI-AiF training framework uses separate point- and region-alignment rewards to adapt grounding as these distributions shift.

items.name: CUA-Skill: Develop Skills for Computer Using Agent
items.summary: CUA-Skill encodes Windows application knowledge in parameterized skills and execution/composition graphs. Its agent retrieves and instantiates these skills and uses memory for failure recovery, with end-to-end evaluation on WindowsAgentArena.

items.name: CovAgent: Overcoming the 30% Curse of Mobile Application Coverage with Agentic AI and Dynamic Instrumentation
items.summary: CovAgent augments Android GUI fuzzers by analyzing decompiled app code and component transitions to identify unsatisfied activation conditions. A second agent generates instrumentation that enables otherwise difficult-to-reach activities, with coverage-based evaluation.

items.name: BEAP-Agent: Backtrackable Execution and Adaptive Planning for GUI Agents
items.summary: BEAP-Agent treats GUI execution as depth-first search with coordinated planning, execution and task-state tracking. It supports backtracking across multiple levels of earlier states and evaluates recovery on OSWorld.

items.name: WebArbiter: A Principle-Guided Reasoning Process Reward Model for Web Agents
items.summary: WebArbiter generates reasoned action-preference verdicts for web navigation, using reasoning distillation followed by reinforcement learning. It introduces WebPRMBench and evaluates both preference judgments and reward-guided trajectory search.
items.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations

items.name: How do Visual Attributes Influence Web Agents? A Comprehensive Evaluation of User Interface Design Factors
items.summary: Introduces VAF, a controlled pipeline that varies webpage appearance while retaining item semantics. It measures both agent clicks and reasoning references to study which visual design factors change browsing decisions.

items.name: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
items.summary: DynaWeb learns a world model that predicts web-page representations after actions and uses it to generate policy-training rollouts. It interleaves these rollouts with expert trajectories and evaluates the trained web agents on WebArena and WebVoyager.

items.name: SSL: Sweet Spot Learning for Differentiated Guidance in Agentic Optimization
items.summary: SSL uses progressively tiered rewards for agent training, including distance-based guidance on GUI perception tasks alongside planning and reasoning tasks.

items.name: Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution
items.summary: Darwinian Memory splits GUI trajectories into reusable units and updates the memory by retaining useful paths and pruning poor ones. It evaluates this training-free memory mechanism on long multi-application tasks.

items.name: Okara: Detection and Attribution of TLS Man-in-the-Middle Vulnerabilities in Android Apps with Foundation Models
items.summary: Okara uses foundation-model-driven GUI agents to explore Android apps for TLS vulnerability detection, then applies instrumentation and classification to attribute vulnerable code.

items.name: Learning with Challenges: Adaptive Difficulty-Aware Data Generation for Mobile GUI Agent Training
items.summary: MobileGen estimates a mobile agent’s strengths across structural and semantic task difficulty, then samples new training targets around that profile. A controllable multi-agent generator creates the corresponding instructions and GUI trajectories.

items.name: Agentic Reward Modeling: Verifying GUI Agent via Progressive Trajectory-Grounded Interaction
items.summary: VAGEN verifies GUI trajectories by first extracting readily available evidence and escalating to tool-based environment probes when needed. Evaluation on OSWorld-Verified and AndroidWorld studies verification accuracy and its cost.

items.name: SimGym: Traffic-Grounded Browser Agents for Offline A/B Testing in E-Commerce
items.summary: SimGym runs traffic-grounded synthetic buyers as browser agents to compare e-commerce storefront variants offline, using buyer profiles derived from production interactions.

items.name: Generative Visual Code Mobile World Models
items.summary: gWorld predicts future mobile GUI states as renderable web code and supplies an automated pipeline for code-based training data. The study evaluates visual state prediction and how stronger world models affect downstream mobile policies.

items.name: SafePred: A Predictive Guardrail for Computer-Using Agents via World Models
items.summary: SafePred uses world-model risk forecasts to guide action filtering and task replanning. Its desktop and web safety evaluations distinguish policy compliance, task success and success under the specified policy.

items.name: SafeGround: Know When to Trust GUI Grounding Models via Uncertainty Calibration
items.summary: Introduces SafeGround, which estimates GUI-grounding uncertainty from the spatial dispersion of sampled predictions and calibrates a decision threshold before testing. It studies risk-aware selection on ScreenSpot-Pro, with statistical control scoped to the threshold’s false-discovery rate.

items.name: Avenir-Web: Human-Experience-Imitating Multimodal Web Agents with Mixture of Grounding Experts
items.summary: Avenir-Web combines multiple grounding specialists with procedural experience, a task checklist and adaptive memory. It evaluates this planning and execution framework on live Online-Mind2Web tasks.

items.name: ToolTok: Tool Tokenization for Efficient and Generalizable GUI Agents
items.summary: ToolTok represents GUI operations with learned tool tokens and frames interaction as progressive tool selection. Semantic anchoring and an easy-to-hard curriculum teach tool meanings before visual pathfinding, with evaluation across grounding scenarios.

items.name: Agent Alpha: Tree Search Unifying Generation, Exploration and Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Agent Alpha uses step-level Monte Carlo tree search to reuse successful prefixes and recover from early GUI mistakes. Comparison-based evaluation and diversity-constrained expansion guide the search, with experiments on OSWorld.

items.name: WebSentinel: Detecting and Localizing Prompt Injection Attacks for Web Agents
items.summary: WebSentinel identifies suspicious webpage segments and checks each against its surrounding page context to detect and locate prompt injections. Its evaluation uses both contaminated and clean webpage datasets.

items.name: Do Web Agents Investigate Before They Decide?
items.summary: Introduces MIRAGE, a web decision benchmark where agents must actively uncover evidence that can contradict the visible context. Separate investigation, reasoning, decision, and hallucination measures diagnose failures beyond reaching the right page.

items.name: M$^2$-Miner: Multi-Agent Enhanced MCTS for Mobile GUI Agent Data Mining
items.summary: M2-Miner uses multi-agent-guided Monte Carlo tree search to collect mobile GUI intent–trajectory pairs. Intent recycling and progressive collector training aim to increase the diversity and usefulness of the mined interaction data.

items.name: UI-Mem: Self-Evolving Experience Memory for Online Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: UI-Mem stores workflows, skills and failure patterns as reusable templates to guide online GUI reinforcement learning. It varies guidance within rollout groups and continually updates the memory so an unguided policy can learn from guided experiences.

items.name: MemGUI-Bench: Benchmarking Memory of Mobile GUI Agents in Dynamic Environments
items.summary: MemGUI-Bench evaluates short-term retention and cross-session experience reuse in mobile GUI agents using paired tasks and repeated-attempt protocols. Its staged evaluator measures memory fidelity, learning and execution efficiency.

items.name: Trifuse: Enhancing Attention-Based GUI Grounding via Multimodal Fusion
items.summary: Trifuse combines attention-based localization with OCR text cues and icon captions to ground GUI instructions. Its fusion procedure favors cross-modal agreement and sharp location peaks, and is evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning.

items.name: POINTS-GUI-G: GUI-Grounding Journey
items.summary: Studies GUI-grounding development from a weakly grounded base model through data preparation, visual training, and verifiable rewards.

items.name: Where Not to Learn: Prior-Aligned Training with Subset-based Attribution Constraints
items.summary: Proposes training with subset-based attribution constraints so models attend to intended evidence, evaluated on image classification and GUI-agent click decisions.

items.name: ANCHOR: Branch-Point Data Generation for GUI Agents
items.summary: ANCHOR expands verified desktop demonstrations by generating new tasks at meaningful branch points and executing their instructions. State-aware verification and action filtering refine the resulting trajectories, which are evaluated through fine-tuned agents on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.

items.name: Mapping the Design Space of User Experience for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Develops a taxonomy of computer-use-agent interaction design through system review and practitioner interviews. A Wizard-of-Oz study then examines how users respond to normal, erroneous, and risky web-based execution, focusing on control, explanation, prompts, and mental models.

items.name: Do Multi-Agents Dream of Electric Screens? Achieving Perfect Accuracy on AndroidWorld Through Task Decomposition
items.summary: Minitap coordinates six specialized agents for AndroidWorld tasks, checking text input against device state and detecting action loops to revise its strategy.

items.name: When Benign Inputs Lead to Severe Harms: Eliciting Unsafe Unintended Behaviors of Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: AutoElicit iteratively revises benign instructions using execution feedback to surface harmful unintended actions by computer-use agents in OS workflows.

items.name: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: MisActBench provides action-level labels for task alignment, while DeAction checks proposed computer-use actions and requests revisions through structured feedback. The paper separately evaluates offline detection and interactive operation in OSWorld and RedTeamCUA.

items.name: GUI-GenBench: Evaluating Image Generation Models as Interactive GUI Environments
items.summary: GUI-GenBench tests image-generation models as action-conditioned GUI environments across five suites, including transitions, trajectories and grounding. Its VLM-based GUI-Score separates goal completion, interaction logic, consistency and visual properties.

items.name: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs: Leveraging the Cognitive Gap for Scalable and Diverse GUI-Agent Defense
items.summary: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs introduces generated interactive challenges intended to distinguish human users from GUI agents. The benchmark targets perception, memory, decisions and actions, with backend-supported challenge types designed for scalable instance generation.

items.name: UI-Venus-1.5 Technical Report
items.summary: Describes a GUI-agent family combining broad intermediate training, full-trajectory online reinforcement learning, and merging of specialized models.

items.name: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
items.summary: MUZZLE evaluates web-agent exposure to indirect prompt injection by finding attack surfaces in agent trajectories and refining injected instructions from execution feedback.

items.name: A11y-CUA Dataset: Characterizing the Accessibility Gap in Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces A11y-CUA, a dataset comparing how blind or low-vision users and sighted users perform everyday computer tasks. It contrasts those traces with agent behavior under default, keyboard-only, and magnifier conditions to identify barriers to shared control.

items.name: TreeCUA: Efficiently Scaling GUI Automation with Tree-Structured Verifiable Evolution
items.summary: TreeCUA organizes GUI exploration trajectories as reusable trees and balances deeper tasks against broader coverage. Its data pipeline combines action verification, memory-backed recovery and a DPO variant that uses information from adjacent branches.

items.name: Code2World: A GUI World Model via Renderable Code Generation
items.summary: Code2World predicts future GUI screens through renderable code, trained on AndroidCode trajectories with supervised learning and render-aware reinforcement learning. It evaluates visual prediction and downstream AndroidWorld navigation with the learned world model.

items.name: Anonymization-Enhanced Privacy Protection for Mobile GUI Agents: Available but Invisible
items.summary: An anonymization framework replaces sensitive screen content and instructions with consistent, type-preserving placeholders while mediating actions through a local interaction proxy. Experiments on AndroidLab and PrivScreen examine the privacy–utility trade-off when mobile GUI agents operate over these transformed interfaces.

items.name: Autonomous Continual Learning for Environment Adaptation of Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: ACuRL uses autonomous interface exploration and an adaptive task curriculum to continually train computer-use policies with reinforcement learning. CUAJudge supplies outcome feedback, and experiments study adaptation across desktop applications and environment changes.

items.name: LHAW: Controllable Underspecification for Long-Horizon Tasks
items.summary: LHAW generates underspecified variants of long-horizon workflow tasks and uses agent trials to evaluate when missing information requires clarification.

items.name: See, Plan, Snap: Evaluating Multimodal GUI Agents in Scratch
items.summary: ScratchWorld evaluates program construction through the Scratch interface using fine-grained drag-and-drop actions and a complementary semantic-API mode. Runtime tests assess the resulting programs, allowing analysis of the gap between program reasoning and GUI manipulation.

items.name: ICA: Information-Aware Credit Assignment for Visually Grounded Long-Horizon Information-Seeking Agents
items.summary: Information-Aware Credit Assignment scores intermediate information gathered by web agents, using rendered webpage snapshots to compare evidence across trajectories.

items.name: Blind Gods and Broken Screens: Architecting a Secure, Intent-Centric Mobile Agent Operating System
items.summary: Analyzes security risks in screen-based mobile agents and proposes Aura, an agent runtime with structured interactions, app-agent isolation and mediated communication.

items.name: How Smart Is Your GUI Agent? A Framework for the Future of Software Interaction
items.summary: Proposes GUI Agent Autonomy Levels (GAL), a six-level framework for describing autonomy and benchmarking GUI agents that navigate web, desktop, and mobile software.

items.name: Adaptive Milestone Reward for GUI Agents
items.summary: ADMIRE extracts milestones from successful GUI explorations to provide adaptive intermediate rewards. It assigns credit differently to successful and failed trajectories and evaluates training on AndroidWorld, with additional transfer studies in web and embodied settings.

items.name: WebTestPilot: Agentic End-to-End Web Testing against Natural Language Specification by Inferring Oracles with Symbolized GUI Elements
items.summary: WebTestPilot turns natural-language requirements into web test steps with inferred preconditions and postconditions over symbolized GUI elements. A benchmark of bug-injected web applications tests whether these context-aware oracles distinguish application defects from agent mistakes.

items.name: AmbiBench: Benchmarking Mobile GUI Agents Beyond One-Shot Instructions in the Wild
items.summary: AmbiBench evaluates mobile GUI agents under four levels of instruction clarity, including tasks requiring active clarification. Its MUSE evaluator separately audits outcomes, execution quality and interaction quality to study alignment with user intent.

items.name: Agentic Test-Time Scaling for WebAgents
items.summary: CATTS allocates additional inference computation when an agent’s action votes show uncertainty. The paper compares voting and arbiter strategies and evaluates this selective scaling on WebArena-Lite, Online-Mind2Web and GoBrowse.

items.name: Agent Skills for Large Language Models: Architecture, Acquisition, Security, and the Path Forward
items.summary: This survey organizes agent skills by architecture, acquisition, deployment and security, including their role in computer-use systems and GUI grounding. It also proposes a permission and lifecycle governance framework for skill deployment.

items.name: Scaling Web Agent Training through Automatic Data Generation and Fine-grained Evaluation
items.summary: This work uses constraint-based progress evaluation to retain partially successful web trajectories for training. It introduces BookingArena for structured booking tasks and studies a distilled agent trained with the resulting data.

items.name: SPILLage: Agentic Oversharing on the Web
items.summary: Formalizes and measures natural agentic oversharing when browser agents handle private user emails and calendars across live websites.

items.name: OpAgent: Operator Agent for Web Navigation
items.summary: OpAgent combines multi-task GUI fine-tuning with online web reinforcement learning using outcome judgments and rule-based progress rewards. A modular planner, grounder, reflector and summarizer support navigation and recovery, evaluated separately from the underlying trained policy.

items.name: Building Autonomous GUI Navigation via Agentic-Q Estimation and Step-Wise Policy Optimization
items.summary: This framework learns an agentic-Q model to estimate individual actions’ contributions to GUI task completion. It then optimizes a policy with step-level samples from its own trajectories, decoupling policy updates from environment interaction.

items.name: GUI-GENESIS: Automated Synthesis of Efficient Environments with Verifiable Rewards for GUI Agent Post-Training
items.summary: GUI-GENESIS reconstructs applications as lightweight web environments with executable assertions for reward computation. It evaluates the cost of these training environments and transfer from synthetic interaction training to held-out real tasks.

items.name: ScreenParse: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
items.summary: ScreenParse supplies dense annotations of UI elements, types and text in web screenshots through an automated rendering and filtering pipeline. ScreenVLM learns to output structured screen markup, and the study evaluates dense parsing and transfer to GUI grounding.

items.name: AutoWebWorld: Synthesizing Infinite Verifiable Web Environments via Finite State Machines
items.summary: AutoWebWorld turns finite-state task models into interactive websites whose actions and goal states can be checked programmatically. It generates verified trajectories for training and evaluates transfer to WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web.

items.name: A Trajectory-Based Safety Audit of Clawdbot (OpenClaw)
items.summary: Audits Clawdbot safety through logged action and tool-call trajectories across local execution and web-mediated workflows, using automated and human review.

items.name: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training
items.summary: Introduces WebWorld, an open-web simulator trained on interaction trajectories for generating agent training data and testing candidate actions. WebWorld-Bench evaluates simulated transitions, alongside downstream web-agent training experiments.

items.name: EmbeWebAgent: Embedding Web Agents into Any Customized UI
items.summary: EmbeWebAgent embeds agent access into existing web applications through frontend observations and a page-specific function registry. Its workflow combines GUI primitives, composite actions and MCP tools, demonstrated in a live interface.

items.name: World-Model-Augmented Web Agents with Action Correction
items.summary: WAC has a web-agent action model consult a world model, simulate action outcomes and use judge feedback to correct actions before execution.

items.name: HiPER: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Explicit Credit Assignment for Large Language Model Agents
items.summary: HiPER trains interactive LLM agents with separate subgoal planning and multi-step execution, assigning reinforcement-learning credit at both levels.

items.name: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
items.summary: MemoryArena links tasks across sessions so that agents must distill earlier interaction experience and use it in later decisions. Its evaluation includes web navigation alongside planning, search and formal reasoning, testing memory through subsequent actions.

items.name: Mobile-Agent-v3.5: Multi-platform Fundamental GUI Agents
items.summary: Presents GUI-Owl-1.5 variants and a hybrid data pipeline for multimodal GUI interaction, tool use, memory, and multi-platform tasks.

items.name: Persona2Web: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents for Contextual Reasoning with User History
items.summary: Persona2Web tests whether web agents can resolve ambiguous requests using preferences implicit in a user’s history. Its reasoning-aware evaluation compares agent architectures and history-access strategies on personalized tasks on the open web.

items.name: IntentCUA: Learning Intent-level Representations for Skill Abstraction and Multi-Agent Planning in Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: IntentCUA coordinates planner and critic agents through shared intent-aligned memory, retrieving reusable skills for long-horizon automation across desktop applications.

items.name: Web Agents Should Use Typed Actions Instead of Click-Based Browsing
items.summary: Proposes web verbs as typed actions for web agents, exposing operations with structured inputs, outputs and conditions so agents can compose auditable workflows.

items.name: Computer-Using World Model
items.summary: Presents a desktop world model that predicts textual UI changes before synthesizing the next screenshot. It learns from Microsoft Office transitions and is evaluated by letting a frozen agent compare simulated actions before execution.

items.name: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents
items.summary: CowCorpus records interleaved human and agent actions during web navigation and identifies distinct patterns of user intervention. Models trained to anticipate these interventions are integrated into live web agents and assessed in a user study.

items.name: ActionEngine: From Reactive to Programmatic Web Agents via State Machine Memory
items.summary: ActionEngine explores web applications to build an updateable state-machine memory of GUI states, operations and transitions. It generates complete task programs from that memory, using reactive repair to handle changed interfaces or missing knowledge.

items.name: ProactiveMobile: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Boosting Proactive Intelligence on Mobile Devices
items.summary: ProactiveMobile benchmarks mobile agents on inferring latent user intent from device context and generating executable sequences from a pool of 63 APIs.

items.name: GUI-Libra: Training Native GUI Agents to Reason and Act with Action-aware Supervision and Partially Verifiable RL
items.summary: GUI-Libra trains GUI agents with action-aware supervision, a curated reasoning dataset and reinforcement learning adapted to partially verifiable actions across web and mobile tasks.

items.name: Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Efficient High-Resolution GUI Agents
items.summary: GUIPruner compresses high-resolution screenshots and interaction history for GUI navigation through training-free resizing and layout-aware token pruning.

items.name: CoME: Empowering Channel-of-Mobile-Experts with Informative Hybrid-Capabilities Reasoning
items.summary: Introduces Channel-of-Mobile-Experts (CoME), a mobile agent with experts for screen summary, subtask planning, action decisions and action functions, trained in stages with InfoGain-Driven DPO (Info-DPO).

items.name: ST-Lite: Training-Free KV Cache Compression with Spatio-Trajectory Guidance for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces ST-Lite, a training-free KV cache compression scheme for vision-language GUI agents that filters redundant frames and preserves small UI elements in interaction traces.

items.name: Atomicity for Agents: Exposing, Exploiting, and Mitigating TOCTOU Vulnerabilities in Browser-Use Agents
items.summary: Identifies time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race vulnerabilities when web pages mutate between agent planning and action execution.

items.name: M$^2$: Dual-Memory Augmentation for Long-Horizon Web Agents via Trajectory Summarization and Insight Retrieval
items.summary: Introduces M², a training-free memory framework for long-horizon web agents that summarizes interaction history and retrieves task guidance from an offline insight bank.

items.name: K^2-Agent: Co-Evolving Know-What and Know-How for Hierarchical Mobile Device Control
items.summary: Introduces K2-Agent, a hierarchical mobile-control framework that refines task knowledge through a reasoning loop and trains an executor with curriculum-guided reinforcement learning.

items.name: CGL: Advancing Continual GUI Learning via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Combines supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning for continual GUI learning, using policy entropy to adjust their proportions and gradient projection to limit conflicting updates. AndroidControl-CL groups applications into sequential tasks to evaluate adaptation and retention.

items.name: PlugMem: A Task-Agnostic Plugin Memory Module for LLM Agents
items.summary: Introduces PlugMem, a knowledge-graph memory module for general LLM agents, evaluated on web-agent tasks alongside conversational question answering and knowledge retrieval.

items.name: Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks
items.summary: Studies webpage injections that affect both screenshots and accessibility trees, then trains web agents through teacher imitation, supervised adversarial examples, and adversarial reinforcement learning. The evaluation tests defenses on MiniWoB++ and held-out tasks.

items.name: TimeWarp: Evaluating Web Agents by Revisiting the Past
items.summary: TimeWarp tests web agents across multiple versions of the same sites, varying visual design, frontend code and workflows. TimeTraj transfers plans across versions to collect training trajectories and study robustness to interface change.

items.name: WebFactory: Automated Compression of Foundational Language Intelligence into Grounded Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces WebFactory, a GUI-agent training pipeline that synthesizes websites, generates tasks and trajectories, and trains with decomposed rewards. Offline and online transfer evaluations examine agents trained on the generated environments.

items.name: STRUCTUREDAGENT: Planning with AND/OR Trees for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
items.summary: Introduces STRUCTUREDAGENT, a web-agent planning framework that interleaves execution with dynamic AND/OR trees, supporting node repair and exploration of alternative plans.

items.name: WebChain: A Large-Scale Human-Annotated Dataset of Real-World Web Interaction Traces
items.summary: WebChain aligns human web-interaction trajectories with visual, structural and action data for agent training. It also introduces WebChainBench and a mid-training approach that separates spatial grounding from planning.

items.name: Enhancing Web Agents with a Hierarchical Memory Tree
items.summary: Introduces Hierarchical Memory Tree (HMT), which organizes web-agent trajectories by intent, stage and action, then uses the hierarchy to plan and act on websites.

items.name: Generalization in Online Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Agents
items.summary: Introduces AndroidWorld-Generalization with separate tests for unseen task instances, templates, and applications. A GRPO training system combines containerized environments with asynchronous trajectory collection to study these generalization regimes.

items.name: Ares: Adaptive Reasoning Effort Selection for Efficient LLM Agents
items.summary: Introduces Ares, a router that selects a reasoning level for each step of a general LLM agent from its interaction history, with web agents among the evaluation settings.

items.name: OSExpert: Computer-Use Agents Learning Professional Skills via Exploration
items.summary: Uses GUI-based depth-first exploration to verify elementary software functions, assemble action primitives, and construct curricula of composed skills. OSExpert-Eval examines how the resulting procedural knowledge supports complex computer-use tasks.

items.name: PIRA-Bench: A Transition from Reactive GUI Agents to GUI-based Proactive Intent Recommendation Agents
items.summary: PIRA-Bench evaluates proactive intent recommendations from noisy GUI screenshot sequences containing interleaved tasks and user context. Its PIRF baseline combines memory and state tracking to maintain multiple task threads and identify opportunities to assist.

items.name: SlowBA: An efficiency backdoor attack towards VLM-based GUI agents
items.summary: Introduces SlowBA, a backdoor attack on vision-language GUI agents that uses pop-up triggers to induce longer reasoning chains and increase response latency.

items.name: SecAgent: Efficient Mobile GUI Agent with Semantic Context
items.summary: Presents a Chinese mobile GUI dataset and navigation benchmark together with SecAgent, which compresses previous screenshots and actions into semantic summaries. The agent is trained with supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning to use this compact interaction context.

items.name: Agentic Critical Training
items.summary: Introduces Agentic Critical Training (ACT), a reinforcement-learning warm-up that teaches general agents to choose expert actions over alternatives, with WebShop among its evaluations.

items.name: AgentOS: From Application Silos to a Natural Language-Driven Data Ecosystem
items.summary: Proposes Personal Agent Operating System (AgentOS), with a natural language or voice portal and an Agent Kernel that coordinates agents and tasks in place of a GUI desktop.

items.name: Video-Based Reward Modeling for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Builds ExeVR-53k from execution-video, instruction and reward triplets, including negative instructions with step annotations. A reward model uses spatiotemporal token pruning to judge task completion from the instruction and execution keyframes.

items.name: SpecOps: A Fully Automated AI Agent Testing Framework in Real-World GUI Environments
items.summary: SpecOps divides testing of GUI-based agents into test generation, environment setup, execution and validation handled by specialist agents. Its evaluation spans five real-world agents, including web applications and browser extensions, and measures execution reliability and bug discovery.

items.name: Hybrid Self-evolving Structured Memory for GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces HyMEM, a graph-based memory for GUI agents that links symbolic task knowledge with trajectory embeddings and refreshes working memory during computer-use tasks.

items.name: Safe and Scalable Web Agent Learning via Recreated Websites
items.summary: Introduces VeriEnv, which recreates websites as executable training environments and exposes internal state through a Python SDK for task generation and deterministic reward checks. Experiments examine web-agent learning across new and expanded site environments.

items.name: CUAAudit: Meta-Evaluation of Vision-Language Models as Auditors of Autonomous Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: CUAAudit examines vision-language models that judge computer-use task completion from an instruction and final environment state. Across macOS, Windows and Linux benchmarks, it measures accuracy, confidence calibration and disagreement between auditors.

items.name: Terminal Is All You Need: Design Properties for Human-AI Agent Collaboration
items.summary: This position paper derives interface design principles from terminal-based human-agent collaboration: representational compatibility, transparent actions and low participation barriers. It argues that graphical and other agent-facing modalities should provide these properties explicitly.

items.name: You Told Me to Do It: Measuring Instructional Text-induced Private Data Leakage in LLM Agents
items.summary: Introduces ReadSecBench, a README-based benchmark for measuring whether high-privilege agents follow injected instructions that leak private data; a computer-use agent is evaluated.

items.name: HATS: Hardness-Aware Trajectory Synthesis for GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces HATS, which directs GUI trajectory exploration toward semantically ambiguous actions and iteratively checks instruction-execution alignment. Feedback from trajectory refinement updates the exploration signal used to collect subsequent training examples.

items.name: AI Planning Framework for LLM-Based Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces a planning taxonomy and trajectory-quality metrics for web agents, supported by 794 human-labeled WebArena trajectories and a comparison of two planning styles.

items.name: Adaptive Vision-Language Model Routing for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Adaptive VLM Routing estimates GUI-action difficulty and small-model confidence to select a model under a predicted reliability threshold. Grounding and agent-routing benchmarks assess the cost–accuracy trade-off, with prior interaction context used for warm agents.

items.name: Why Do LLM-based Web Agents Fail? A Hierarchical Planning Perspective
items.summary: Presents a hierarchical planning framework for evaluating web agents at planning, execution and replanning stages, and reports low-level execution as the main failure source.

items.name: Zoom to Essence: Trainless GUI Grounding by Inferring upon Interface Elements
items.summary: Presents ZoomUI, a training-free grounding method that expresses instructions as visual element descriptions and uses model attention to zoom progressively into relevant interface regions. Evaluation examines instruction-to-element localization on GUI benchmarks.

items.name: Visual Confused Deputy: Exploiting and Defending Perception Failures in Computer-Using Agents
items.summary: Formalizes a visual confused-deputy failure in which a computer agent acts on a misperceived UI object. A separate guardrail checks both the visual target and the agent's action reasoning against deployment-specific knowledge before permitting execution.

items.name: GUI-CEval: A Hierarchical and Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: GUI-CEval evaluates Chinese mobile GUI agents through a hierarchy of atomic abilities and application-level tasks collected on physical devices. Its diagnostics cover perception, planning, reflection, execution and post-action evaluation across a broad set of apps.

items.name: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
items.summary: This public red-teaming study evaluates indirect prompt injection that both changes agent behavior and hides the compromise from the final response. Its scenarios include computer use alongside tool calling and coding, with analyses of transfer and model-dependent vulnerability.

items.name: WebPII: Benchmarking Visual PII Detection for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: WebPII provides synthetic e-commerce screenshots with fine-grained annotations for sensitive information, including partially filled forms and transaction identifiers. It also trains WebRedact to detect visual PII as a privacy component for computer-use agents.

items.name: AdaZoom-GUI: Adaptive Zoom-based GUI Grounding with Instruction Refinement
items.summary: Combines instruction rewriting with conditional second-stage zooming for small GUI targets. A grounding dataset and GRPO training support joint prediction of click coordinates and element bounding boxes.

items.name: AndroTMem: From Interaction Trajectories to Anchored Memory in Long-Horizon GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces AndroTMem-Bench for Android tasks whose later actions depend on earlier UI states. Anchored State Memory retains causally linked intermediate states for subgoal-specific retrieval and evaluates them against full-history and summary-based memory.

items.name: ClawTrap: A MITM-Based Red-Teaming Framework for Real-World OpenClaw Security Evaluation
items.summary: Presents a man-in-the-middle network red-teaming framework for evaluating autonomous OpenClaw agents under live traffic manipulation.

items.name: OS-Themis: A Scalable Critic Framework for Generalist GUI Rewards
items.summary: Presents OS-Themis, a multi-agent critic that divides GUI trajectories into verifiable milestones and reviews their evidence before assigning an outcome. OGRBench evaluates GUI rewards across platforms, with AndroidWorld experiments examining training and trajectory filtering.

items.name: A Subgoal-driven Framework for Improving Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: The framework separates inference-time subgoal planning from MiRA, a reinforcement-learning method that supplies milestone rewards. WebArena-Lite experiments evaluate these mechanisms for long-horizon web navigation.

items.name: MedSPOT: A Workflow-Aware Sequential Grounding Benchmark for Clinical GUI
items.summary: Benchmarks sequential target localization in clinical software workflows, emphasizing how early mistakes affect subsequent interaction steps.

items.name: ContractSkill: Repairable Contract-Based Skills for Multimodal Web Agents
items.summary: Turns draft web-agent skills into structured executable artifacts that support deterministic checks, fault localization and local repair. VisualWebArena and MiniWoB experiments examine execution and reuse within the same benchmark family.

items.name: MANA: Towards Efficient Mobile Ad Detection via Multimodal Agentic UI Navigation
items.summary: MANA combines visual, temporal and exploration signals to guide navigation toward mobile advertisements. It evaluates ad detection and interaction cost on commercial smartphones, including obfuscated-ad cases.

items.name: Ego2Web: A Web Agent Benchmark Grounded in Egocentric Videos
items.summary: Ego2Web pairs first-person videos with online tasks that require agents to connect the user’s physical context to web actions. It also evaluates an automatic task judge against human judgments and analyzes failures in video understanding and web execution.

items.name: The Evolution of Tool Use in LLM Agents: From Single-Tool Call to Multi-Tool Orchestration
items.summary: Surveys multi-tool LLM agents across planning, training, safety, efficiency, and evaluation, including GUI and mobile systems among its application areas.

items.name: IntentWeave: A Progressive Entry Ladder for Multi-Surface Browser Agents in Cloud Portals
items.summary: Introduces IntentWeave, a design space and browser-extension prototype for placing web-agent assistance across browser surfaces, evaluated through a study of three entry strategies.

items.name: AgentRAE: Remote Action Execution through Notification-based Visual Backdoors against Screenshots-based Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: AgentRAE studies notification-based visual backdoors that redirect mobile GUI-agent actions. Its training separates sensitivity to icon differences from trigger/action association, with evaluations of clean behavior and targeted redirection.

items.name: CAPTCHA Solving for Native GUI Agents: Automated Reasoning-Action Data Generation and Self-Corrective Training
items.summary: Introduces ReCAP, a native GUI agent for interactive CAPTCHA challenges, trained with generated interaction trajectories, reasoning traces and self-correction data.

items.name: The Cognitive Firewall:Securing Browser Based AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Via Hybrid Edge Cloud Defense
items.summary: Proposes a split-compute browser defense pairing a local visual sentinel, a cloud planner, and deterministic policy enforcement against indirect prompt injection.

items.name: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
items.summary: CareFlow benchmarks long healthcare-software workflows, while CarePilot coordinates action proposals, execution checks and corrective feedback using short- and long-term memory. Its actor consumes visual interfaces and system state to select semantic actions.

items.name: Towards Automated Crowdsourced Testing via Personified-LLM
items.summary: Introduces PersonaTester, a framework that gives LLM agents tester personas to vary their exploration and interaction habits during automated crowdsourced GUI testing.

items.name: CUA-Suite: Massive Human-annotated Video Demonstrations for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: CUA-Suite combines continuous expert desktop demonstrations in VideoCUA with the UI-Vision evaluation benchmark and GroundCUA grounding data. Screen recordings, cursor traces and layered annotations support study of temporal behavior and professional software workflows.

items.name: UI-Voyager: A Self-Evolving GUI Agent Learning via Failed Experience
items.summary: Introduces a two-stage mobile GUI learner that first co-evolves trajectories and policies through rejection fine-tuning. Group Relative Self-Distillation then uses successful rollout branches to provide step-level supervision for failed trajectories, evaluated on AndroidWorld.

items.name: WebTestBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents towards End-to-End Automated Web Testing
items.summary: Introduces WebTestBench for end-to-end website testing, separating checklist generation from defect detection. Its WebTester baseline evaluates test coverage, detection and sustained interaction across web application categories.

items.name: GUIDE: A Benchmark for Understanding and Assisting Users in Open-Ended GUI Tasks
items.summary: GUIDE evaluates whether models can recognize a user’s behavior, infer intent and decide when to offer help during open-ended software tasks. It uses narrated screen recordings of novice users and studies the effect of additional user context on these assistance decisions.

items.name: Where and How to Prune: An Empirical Study of Visual Token Pruning for GUI Agent Navigation
items.summary: Studies visual token pruning for GUI navigation, separating reusable screenshot encoder embeddings from later language-model computation. The analysis examines foreground-background token allocation and spatial coverage when pruning historical screenshots.

items.name: Towards GUI Agents: Vision-Language Diffusion Models for GUI Grounding
items.summary: Adapts a discrete vision-language diffusion model to single-turn GUI action and bounding-box prediction, using a hybrid masking schedule for coordinate geometry. Experiments across web, desktop and mobile datasets examine grounding accuracy and inference tradeoffs.

items.name: GUIDE: Resolving Domain Bias in GUI Agents through Real-Time Web Video Retrieval and Plug-and-Play Annotation
items.summary: GUIDE retrieves relevant software tutorials through subtitle-based video search, then infers planning and grounding knowledge from consecutive annotated keyframes. It inserts that knowledge into existing GUI-agent modules without parameter updates and evaluates the plug-in on OSWorld.

items.name: Vision2Web: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Visual Website Development with Agent Verification
items.summary: Introduces Vision2Web, a benchmark for website development from images, spanning UI-to-code, multi-page frontend and full-stack tasks, with a GUI agent verifier and VLM-based judge.

items.name: MolmoPoint: Better Pointing for VLMs with Grounding Tokens
items.summary: MolmoPoint replaces textual coordinate generation with pointing tokens that select visual regions and refine them through subpatches. The general image/video method includes GUI-pointing evaluation on ScreenSpotPro alongside other visual grounding tasks.

items.name: "What Did It Actually Do?": Understanding Risk Awareness and Traceability for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Presents an interview study of computer-use agent risks and AgentTrace, a prototype interface showing agent actions, resource access, permission history, and lasting changes.

items.name: Emergence WebVoyager: Toward Consistent and Transparent Evaluation of (Web) Agents in The Wild
items.summary: Audits sources of ambiguity and operational variation in WebVoyager evaluation and introduces standardized guidance for task setup, failure handling, annotation and reporting. Emergence WebVoyager applies this protocol to a web-agent evaluation.

items.name: PSPA-Bench: A Personalized Benchmark for Smartphone GUI Agent
items.summary: PSPA-Bench evaluates personalized smartphone GUI behavior using user-specific instructions and a process-aware assessment of interaction traces. Its comparison of GUI agents diagnoses weaknesses in adapting workflows and preferences.

items.name: Terminal Agents Suffice for Enterprise Automation
items.summary: Studies enterprise automation by terminal agents that call platform APIs, comparing their task results and cost with other agent approaches, including web agents using graphical interfaces.

items.name: PixelPrune: Pixel-Level Adaptive Visual Token Reduction via Predictive Coding
items.summary: PixelPrune removes pixel-redundant patches before the vision encoder, reducing both encoding and downstream language-model work. The training-free method evaluates lossless and controlled-lossy compression on document and GUI tasks.

items.name: When Users Change Their Mind: Evaluating Interruptible Agents in Long-Horizon Web Navigation
items.summary: Introduces InterruptBench, a WebArena-Lite-derived benchmark that tests how long-horizon web-navigation agents handle mid-task user additions, revisions, and retractions.

items.name: Do Phone-Use Agents Respect Your Privacy?
items.summary: Introduces MyPhoneBench to verify whether phone-use agents minimize personal data disclosure when filling forms during benign mobile tasks.

items.name: Read More, Think More: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents
items.summary: Studies HTML and accessibility-tree observations for web agents, relating their usefulness to model capability and thinking budget, and proposes diff-based observation history to save tokens.

items.name: GPA: Learning GUI Process Automation from Demonstrations
items.summary: Presents demonstration-based GUI process replay with Sequential Monte Carlo localization and readiness checks. GPA executes the learned workflow locally and can serve as the GUI execution component of an agent using MCP or CLI tools.

items.name: UI-Oceanus: Scaling GUI Agents with Synthetic Environmental Dynamics
items.summary: UI-Oceanus converts autonomous GUI exploration and execution feedback into supervision for predicting future interface states. It compares forward and inverse objectives during continual pretraining and examines downstream offline and online navigation as synthetic data scales.

items.name: Poison Once, Exploit Forever: Environment-Injected Memory Poisoning Attacks on Web Agents
items.summary: Studies persistent web-agent memory contamination introduced through environmental observations. Experiments on WebArena and VisualWebArena examine cross-session effects and how interaction failures alter susceptibility.

items.name: AgentHazard: A Benchmark for Evaluating Harmful Behavior in Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces AgentHazard, a benchmark of harmful multi-step behavior by computer-use agents acting through tools, files, and execution environments.

items.name: The Tool Illusion: Rethinking Tool Use in Web Agents
items.summary: Presents a controlled study of higher-level tool use in web agents across tool sources, backbone models, frameworks, and evaluation benchmarks.

items.name: GUIDE: Interpretable GUI Agent Evaluation via Hierarchical Diagnosis
items.summary: GUIDE evaluates GUI trajectories by segmenting them into subtasks, diagnosing each segment, and aggregating structured findings into a task verdict. It tests diagnostic judgments on e-commerce, web-agent and Android-control traces.

items.name: Your Agent, Their Asset: A Real-World Safety Analysis of OpenClaw
items.summary: Introduces a safety evaluation of OpenClaw and the CIK taxonomy for analyzing how changes to a personal agent's persistent state affect attacks on its local and service access.

items.name: Comparing Human Oversight Strategies for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Compares four human oversight strategies during live web-agent sessions, examining exposure to problematic actions and opportunities to intervene. The analysis identifies timing and attention problems in control handoffs and upfront plan approval.

items.name: IntentScore: Intent-Conditioned Action Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Trains IntentScore on offline desktop GUI interactions to assess candidate actions using both their state relevance and planning intent. The reward model is evaluated as an action reranker for Agent S3 on OSWorld.

items.name: Don't Act Blindly: Robust GUI Automation via Action-Effect Verification and Self-Correction
items.summary: Introduces VeriGUI, which checks expected action effects and reasons about recovery before subsequent GUI actions. Training combines synthetic failure trajectories with verification-weighted GRPO, evaluated on an AndroidControl-based robustness benchmark.

items.name: Gym-Anything: Turn any Software into an Agent Environment
items.summary: Introduces Gym-Anything, where a setup agent configures software environments and an independent auditor checks the resulting evidence. CUA-World supplies long-horizon tasks across professional applications, with experiments on trajectory distillation and test-time auditing.

items.name: MAESTRO: Adapting GUIs and Guiding Navigation with User Preferences in Conversational Agents with GUIs
items.summary: Introduces MAESTRO, a conversational GUI system that remembers user preferences, adapts interface options, and guides backtracking in multistep booking decisions.

items.name: VenusBench-Mobile: A Challenging and User-Centric Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents with Capability Diagnostics
items.summary: Introduces VenusBench-Mobile, an online benchmark for mobile GUI agents with user-intent-driven tasks and capability annotations for analyzing agent behavior and failures.

items.name: The Art of Building Verifiers for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Describes a web-trajectory verifier built around structured rubrics, separate process and outcome judgments, and explicit treatment of uncontrollable failures. CUAVerifierBench supplies human labels for evaluating these choices and screenshot-based context management.

items.name: WebSP-Eval: Evaluating Web Agents on Website Security and Privacy Tasks
items.summary: WebSP-Eval evaluates agents carrying out website security and privacy tasks such as preference changes and session management. A browser extension controls account and initial state across runs, enabling analysis of failures on stateful UI controls.

items.name: What's Missing in Screen-to-Action? Towards a UI-in-the-Loop Paradigm for Multimodal GUI Reasoning
items.summary: Introduces UILoop, which inserts explicit UI-element localization, function and usage reasoning between screen observation and action. UI Comprehension-Bench evaluates these element-level capabilities with three metrics.

items.name: Android Coach: Improve Online Agentic Training Efficiency with Single State Multiple Actions
items.summary: Introduces Android Coach, which uses a learned critic to evaluate multiple candidate actions at each observed emulator state. Process rewards and a group-wise advantage estimator support online training, evaluated on AndroidLab and AndroidWorld.

items.name: GameWorld: Towards Standardized and Verifiable Evaluation of Multimodal Game Agents
items.summary: Introduces GameWorld, a browser-game benchmark that evaluates multimodal agents through keyboard and mouse controls or semantic actions using outcome checks.

items.name: Structured Distillation of Web Agent Capabilities Enables Generalization
items.summary: Introduces Agent-as-Annotators, which uses modular LLM roles to synthesize and filter web-agent trajectories for supervised training of a smaller web agent.

items.name: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection
items.summary: This study tests black-box GUI-grounding failures caused by strategically added, innocuous-looking UI elements. Its iterative overlay search is compared with random injection and repeated independent grounding trials to distinguish persistent misdirection from incidental clutter.

items.name: Same Outcomes, Different Journeys: A Trace-Level Framework for Comparing Human and GUI-Agent Behavior in Production Search Systems
items.summary: Presents a trace-level framework for comparing GUI agents with people on task outcomes, queries, and interface navigation in a production audio-search application.

items.name: Preference Redirection via Attention Concentration: An Attack on Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces PRAC, an adversarial-patch attack that redirects a computer-use agent's visual attention to steer product selection on an online shopping platform.

items.name: KnowU-Bench: Towards Interactive, Proactive, and Personalized Mobile Agent Evaluation
items.summary: Introduces KnowU-Bench, an Android emulator benchmark for mobile agents that evaluates preference elicitation, proactive decisions, consent and GUI task execution.

items.name: MolmoWeb: Open Visual Web Agent and Open Data for the Open Web
items.summary: Presents MolmoWebMix, combining synthetic browser trajectories, human demonstrations and GUI perception data, and MolmoWeb screenshot-to-action policies trained from it. Browser benchmarks also test parallel rollouts with best-of-N selection.

items.name: ClawBench: Can AI Agents Complete Everyday Online Tasks?
items.summary: Introduces ClawBench, 153 everyday tasks on production websites in 15 categories; an interception layer blocks each final submission so bookings, purchases and job applications are scored without side effects.

items.name: CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation
items.summary: Introduces CORA, which calibrates a risk model to choose between executing and abstaining from mobile GUI actions, then diagnoses rejected actions to suggest interventions. Phone-Harm provides step-level safety labels for evaluating this safeguarding process.

items.name: Turing Test on Screen: A Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agent Humanization
items.summary: Introduces the Agent Humanization Benchmark (AHB) and mobile touch-dynamics data to assess whether GUI agents' interactions resemble human touch behavior.

items.name: Avenir-UX: Automated UX Evaluation via Simulated Human Web Interaction with GUI Grounding
items.summary: Avenir-UX combines grounded web interaction with simulated user profiles and structured usability measures to produce evaluations of website journeys. The paper describes its architecture and use of SUS, step-wise ease questions and think-aloud traces for automated UX reporting.

items.name: MobiFlow: Real-World Mobile Agent Benchmarking through Trajectory Fusion
items.summary: Introduces MobiFlow, a mobile-agent evaluation framework that fuses task trajectories into a state graph for dynamic interaction with third-party apps and measures task outcomes.

items.name: Agentic Compilation: Mitigating the LLM Rerun Crisis for Minimized-Inference-Cost Web Automation
items.summary: Proposes Compile-and-Execute, which turns a sanitized DOM into a reusable JSON workflow so repetitive browser tasks can run without further model queries.

items.name: EE-MCP: Self-Evolving MCP-GUI Agents via Automated Environment Generation and Experience Learning
items.summary: EE-MCP studies application-dependent mixtures of GUI actions and MCP calls using generated environments, trajectory collection and filtered training. An experience bank extracts rules from trajectory comparisons for inference-time improvement, distinct from model distillation.

items.name: HealthAdminBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Healthcare Administration Tasks
items.summary: Introduces HealthAdminBench with GUI environments for an electronic health record, payer portals and fax handling. Expert-defined administrative tasks are decomposed into verifiable subtasks to compare local progress with end-to-end workflow completion.

items.name: The Blind Spot of Agent Safety: How Benign User Instructions Expose Critical Vulnerabilities in Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces OS-BLIND, a computer-use agent safety benchmark for harmful outcomes arising from benign instructions and threats in task environments.

items.name: WebForge: Breaking the Realism-Reproducibility-Scalability Trilemma in Browser Agent Benchmark
items.summary: Presents WebForge, a pipeline that plans, generates, refines and validates self-contained interactive websites. WebForge-Bench uses these environments to evaluate browser agents across domains and controlled difficulty levels.

items.name: CocoaBench: Evaluating Unified Digital Agents in the Wild
items.summary: Introduces CocoaBench, a benchmark for unified digital agents on long-horizon tasks combining vision, search, and coding, including capabilities related to GUI automation.

items.name: Mobile GUI Agent Privacy Personalization with Trajectory Induced Preference Optimization
items.summary: Proposes Trajectory Induced Preference Optimization (TIPO) to train mobile GUI agents for differing user privacy preferences across structurally different task trajectories.

items.name: ClawGUI: A Unified Framework for Training, Evaluating, and Deploying GUI Agents
items.summary: Presents ClawGUI, a shared harness for GUI-agent reinforcement learning, benchmark evaluation and deployment on mobile devices. It combines parallel virtual and physical environments, process rewards, and hybrid CLI-GUI execution with persistent memory.

items.name: WebAgentGuard: A Reasoning-Driven Guard Model for Detecting Prompt Injection Attacks in Web Agents
items.summary: WebAgentGuard separates prompt-injection detection from the operating web agent through a parallel multimodal guard. The guard is trained on synthetic visual/textual examples using reasoning-focused supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning.

items.name: From Imitation to Discrimination: Progressive Curriculum Learning for Robust Web Navigation
items.summary: Introduces the Triton dataset and a staged training curriculum for text-based web navigation agents, using hard-negative HTML examples to train element discrimination and longer task execution.

items.name: PrecisionCUA: Iterative Visual Refinement for Pixel-Precise Cursor Grounding in Code Editors
items.summary: Studies iterative cursor grounding in dense code-editor interfaces, using visual feedback from earlier attempts to correct displacement. PrecisionCUA evaluates this closed-loop process across multiple model families on coding-interface tasks.

items.name: WebXSkill: Skill Learning for Autonomous Web Agents
items.summary: WebXSkill pairs parameterized action programs with step-level language guidance, mining reusable skills from synthetic browser-agent traces. A URL-based graph supports retrieval, and deployment alternates between direct program execution and guided native planning.

items.name: Towards Scalable Lightweight GUI Agents via Multi-role Orchestration
items.summary: Introduces LAMO, a training framework for a lightweight GUI agent that can execute tasks alone or serve as an action executor alongside planners in multi-agent workflows.

items.name: RiskWebWorld: A Realistic Interactive Benchmark for GUI Agents in E-commerce Risk Management
items.summary: Introduces RiskWebWorld, an interactive benchmark of e-commerce risk-management tasks for GUI agents on websites, with Gymnasium infrastructure for evaluation and agentic RL.

items.name: UI-Copilot: Advancing Long-Horizon GUI Automation via Tool-Integrated Policy Optimization
items.summary: UI-Copilot separates GUI execution from on-demand memory retrieval and numerical assistance. Its training procedure treats tool selection and multi-turn task execution as distinct optimization targets while keeping persistent observations outside transient context.

items.name: UI-Zoomer: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Zoom-In for GUI Grounding
items.summary: Introduces UI-Zoomer, a training-free grounding method that uses candidate agreement and token confidence to decide when to crop and retry. Prediction variance determines a separate crop radius for each uncertain interface target.

items.name: GUI-Perturbed: Domain Randomization Reveals Systematic Brittleness in GUI Grounding Models
items.summary: Introduces GUI-Perturbed, which varies screenshot appearance and instruction wording independently to diagnose grounding failures. Experiments on three related model architectures examine relational instructions, browser zoom and augmentation-based fine-tuning.

items.name: Beyond Chat and Clicks: GUI Agents for In-Situ Assistance via Live Interface Transformation
items.summary: DOMSteer translates help requests and live page context into reversible DOM changes such as control highlighting, contextual tooltips and layout reorganization. The work evaluates in-place GUI assistance with interface tests, use cases and a comparative user study.

items.name: SkillDroid: Compile Once, Reuse Forever
items.summary: Introduces SkillDroid, which compiles successful mobile GUI trajectories into reusable action templates and replays them without model calls, recompiling when they degrade.

items.name: FedGUI: Benchmarking Federated GUI Agents across Heterogeneous Platforms, Devices, and Operating Systems
items.summary: Introduces FedGUI, a federated GUI-learning benchmark built from six datasets spanning mobile, web and desktop interfaces. Its experiments separate platform, device, operating-system and data-source heterogeneity when evaluating collaborative training.

items.name: OpenMobile: Building Open Mobile Agents with Task and Trajectory Synthesis
items.summary: Presents OpenMobile, which builds exploration-based environment memory to synthesize task instructions and switches between learner and expert policies during trajectory collection. The resulting data includes recovery behavior and is tested through mobile-agent training and benchmark-overlap analysis.

items.name: Zoom Consistency: A Free Confidence Signal in Multi-Step Visual Grounding Pipelines
items.summary: Proposes zoom consistency as a confidence signal for multistep GUI grounding and uses it to route between specialist and generalist visual grounding models.

items.name: StressWeb: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Web Agent Robustness under Realistic Interaction Variability
items.summary: Introduces a web-agent stress-testing benchmark with controlled changes to layouts, interaction semantics, and execution for diagnosing behavior under varied conditions.

items.name: Penny Wise, Pixel Foolish: Bypassing Price Constraints in Multimodal Agents via Visual Adversarial Perturbations
items.summary: Introduces PriceBlind, a visual perturbation method for controlled screenshot-based evaluation of price-constrained multimodal agents. The reported transfer experiments use a simplified single-turn coordinate-selection protocol.
