items.name: AgentClick: A Skill-Based Human-in-the-Loop Review Layer for Terminal AI Agents
items.summary: AgentClick gives terminal-based agents a browser review interface for plans, drafts, execution traces and editable memory. A local server and skill plugin let users inspect proposed actions and provide structured feedback.

items.name: A Survey on Long-Term Memory Security in LLM Agents: Attacks, Defenses, and Governance Across the Memory Lifecycle
items.summary: Organizes security risks and defenses for persistent agent memory into six lifecycle phases and proposes five verifiable governance primitives.

items.name: HalluClear: Diagnosing, Evaluating and Mitigating Hallucinations in GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces HalluClear with a GUI hallucination taxonomy, expert-calibrated evaluation workflow and structured-reasoning post-training scheme. It evaluates how these components affect hallucinations, grounding and action fidelity across GUI agents.

items.name: Do LLMs Need to See Everything? A Benchmark and Study of Failures in LLM-driven Smartphone Automation using Screentext vs. Screenshots
items.summary: DailyDroid compares text-only and text-plus-screenshot agents on everyday Android tasks across multiple apps and difficulty levels. Its failure analysis examines accessibility, observation modality and agent/application behavior.

items.name: WebUncertainty: Dual-Level Uncertainty Driven Planning and Reasoning For Autonomous Web Agent
items.summary: WebUncertainty adapts planning mode to task uncertainty and guides action-level tree search with confidence-derived uncertainty estimates. Its evaluations examine autonomous execution of dynamic, long-horizon web tasks on WebArena and WebVoyager.

items.name: On the Reliability of Computer Use Agents
items.summary: This study examines repeated OSWorld executions to separate execution stochasticity, task-specification ambiguity and behavioral variation. Paired task-level tests show why one successful run is insufficient evidence of reliable computer use.

items.name: AJ-Bench: Benchmarking Agent-as-a-Judge for Environment-Aware Evaluation
items.summary: AJ-Bench evaluates judge agents that actively gather evidence from search, data systems and graphical interfaces. Its annotated tasks and trajectories test information acquisition, state verification and process verification.

items.name: Mango: Multi-Agent Web Navigation via Global-View Optimization
items.summary: Proposes Mango, a multi-agent web-navigation method that selects starting URLs using Thompson Sampling and stores navigation history to inform later attempts.

items.name: Human-Guided Harm Recovery for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces a preference-trained reward model for guiding computer-use agents out of harmful states and BackBench, a benchmark of recovery tasks.

items.name: Temporal UI State Inconsistency in Desktop GUI Agents: Formalizing and Defending Against TOCTOU Attacks on Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: This study examines UI changes between a desktop agent’s screenshot observation and action dispatch. Its pre-execution state checks address overlay and focus manipulation, while the reported DOM-injection blind spot limits the defense’s coverage.

items.name: AutomationBench
items.summary: Introduces AutomationBench, a benchmark for agents coordinating business workflows across applications through REST APIs, including endpoint discovery and policy adherence.

items.name: PlayCoder: Making LLM-Generated GUI Code Playable
items.summary: PlayEval measures whether generated GUI applications remain logically playable, using PlayTester to execute task-oriented GUI playthroughs. PlayCoder closes the loop between repository-aware generation, interactive testing and targeted code repair.

items.name: AgentLens: Adaptive Visual Modalities for Human-Agent Interaction in Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces AgentLens, a mobile GUI agent that shows full, partial, or generated interface views during background task execution to support user interaction.

items.name: Measure Twice, Click Once: Co-evolving Proposer and Visual Critic via Reinforcement Learning for GUI Grounding
items.summary: Trains a GUI grounding proposer together with a visual critic that evaluates candidate locations rendered on screenshots. An adaptive reinforcement-learning schedule balances their development, using proposal diversity and critic feedback during training.

items.name: VLAA-GUI: Knowing When to Stop, Recover, and Search, A Modular Framework for GUI Automation
items.summary: VLAA-GUI combines mandatory checks for visually supported completion, multi-tier loop recovery and on-demand workflow search. Optional coding and grounding agents support execution, with component ablations on Linux and Windows GUI tasks.

items.name: SOLAR-RL: Semi-Online Long-horizon Assignment Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: SOLAR-RL trains GUI navigation agents by reconstructing rollout candidates from static data and assigning step rewards that reflect trajectory quality.

items.name: Agentic World Modeling: Foundations, Capabilities, Laws, and Beyond
items.summary: Survey of agentic world models that classifies predictive capabilities and governing laws, including the digital setting of web and GUI agents.

items.name: PageGuide: Browser extension to assist users in navigating a webpage and locating information
items.summary: PageGuide is a browser extension that highlights evidence for answers on a page and guides users through web pages with evidence captured at each step.

items.name: GoClick: Lightweight Element Grounding Model for Autonomous GUI Interaction
items.summary: Studies a compact encoder-decoder grounding model and progressive training-data refinement for resource-constrained GUI interaction.

items.name: OS-SPEAR: A Toolkit for the Safety, Performance,Efficiency, and Robustness Analysis of OS Agents
items.summary: Provides an evaluation toolkit for joint safety, efficiency, and multimodal robustness analysis of operating-system GUI agents.

items.name: AutoGUI-v2: A Comprehensive Multi-Modal GUI Functionality Understanding Benchmark
items.summary: AutoGUI-v2 evaluates interface functionality, grounding and predicted interaction outcomes using hierarchical regions derived through VLM-human annotation. Its tasks span multiple operating systems and expose differences between functional localization, captioning and transition-logic understanding.

items.name: Odysseys: Benchmarking Web Agents on Realistic Long Horizon Tasks
items.summary: Introduces Odysseys, a live-web benchmark of long, multi-site tasks derived from browsing sessions. Graded task rubrics and a rubric-score-per-step measure evaluate both partial progress and trajectory efficiency.

items.name: Benchmarking and Improving GUI Agents in High-Dynamic Environments
items.summary: Introduces DynamicGUIBench for applications whose interfaces change between actions, together with DynamicUI, an agent that processes screen recordings. The agent selects informative frames, filters inconsistent action reasoning and uses trajectory reflection for subsequent decisions.

items.name: SnapGuard: Lightweight Prompt Injection Detection for Screenshot-Based Web Agents
items.summary: SnapGuard detects screenshot-based prompt injection through complementary visual-stability and recovered textual cues. Its evaluation compares detection quality and inference cost across attack and benign-page settings.

items.name: Training Computer Use Agents to Assess the Usability of Graphical User Interfaces
items.summary: uxCUA learns to assess interface usability by choosing interaction flows, executing them and predicting a numerical usability score. Training uses interactive UIs with usability labels and human preferences, with evaluations on synthetic and real interfaces.

items.name: Beyond Screenshots: Evaluating VLMs' Understanding of UI Animations
items.summary: AniMINT evaluates how VLMs perceive, explain and interpret UI animations using densely annotated videos. The study distinguishes basic motion recognition from higher-level animation meaning and probes motion, context and perceptual cues.

items.name: Step-level Optimization for Efficient Computer-use Agents
items.summary: Proposes a step-level model cascade that runs a smaller computer-use policy until learned monitors flag stalled progress or semantic drift. Separate history-based stuck detection and milestone checks determine when to escalate for recovery or verification without retraining the larger model.

items.name: AutoSurfer -- Teaching Web Agents through Comprehensive Surfing, Learning, and Modeling
items.summary: AutoSurfer explores website actions breadth-first, retaining page and trajectory knowledge to guide task synthesis and trajectory refinement. It evaluates the resulting training data by fine-tuning a web agent on WebArena and examining synthesized-task diversity.

items.name: WindowsWorld: A Process-Centric Benchmark of Autonomous GUI Agents in Professional Cross-Application Environments
items.summary: Introduces WindowsWorld for professional workflows spanning multiple desktop applications, with generated tasks refined through human review. Intermediate subgoals support process-oriented evaluation of cross-application reasoning and execution efficiency.

items.name: FineState-Bench: Benchmarking State-Conditioned Grounding for Fine-grained GUI State Setting
items.summary: FineState-Bench tests whether GUI agents locate the intended control and set its exact state across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces, with stage-wise diagnostic metrics.

items.name: Exploring LLM Agent Designs and Interaction Modalities for Scientific Visualization
items.summary: This study compares specialized, computer-use and coding agents on scientific visualization workflows. It examines GUI, CLI, code and tool-call interaction modes, including how persistent memory changes performance across repeated trials.

items.name: A11y-Compressor: A Framework for Enhancing the Efficiency of GUI Agent Observations through Visual Context Reconstruction and Redundancy Reduction
items.summary: A11y-Compressor transforms linearized accessibility trees through modal detection, redundancy reduction and semantic structuring. Its OSWorld evaluation measures both observation-token reduction and task success.

items.name: Learn where to Click from Yourself: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
items.summary: Introduces GUI-SD, an on-policy self-distillation method for locating GUI elements from instructions, using a visually enriched teacher context and entropy-guided token weighting.

items.name: Faithful Mobile GUI Agents with Guided Advantage Estimator
items.summary: Introduces Faithful-Agent, which first teaches abstention under perturbed evidence and then refines GUI policies with an anchor-based, variance-adaptive advantage estimator. A thought-action consistency reward encourages decisions grounded in displayed evidence and instructions.

items.name: Planner Matters! An Efficient and Unbalanced Multi-agent Collaboration Framework for Long-horizon Planning
items.summary: A planner-centric RL framework divides agent automation among a planner, actor, and memory manager, with evaluations that include web navigation and OS control.

items.name: AutoFocus: Uncertainty-Aware Active Visual Search for GUI Grounding
items.summary: Presents AutoFocus, a training-free grounding method that turns sampled coordinates and token uncertainty into spatial region proposals. Shape-aware crops and visual comparison select a target while retaining surrounding interface context.

items.name: AcademiClaw: When Students Set Challenges for AI Agents
items.summary: AcademiClaw benchmarks OpenClaw agents on long academic workflows, scoring task completion in isolated Docker sandboxes with rubrics and a safety audit.

items.name: Augmenting Interface Usability Heuristics for Reliable Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: A study adapts interface usability heuristics for computer-use agents and evaluates augmented designs in UI-Verse, a suite of controlled interface environments.

items.name: cotomi Act: Learning to Automate Work by Watching You
items.summary: cotomi Act is a browser agent that executes multi-step tasks and turns observed user browsing into persistent knowledge shared with users.

items.name: WAAA! Web Adversaries Against Agentic Browsers
items.summary: Evaluates agentic browsers against classical web attacks and visual social-engineering lures beyond indirect prompt injection.

items.name: X-OmniClaw Technical Report: A Unified Mobile Agent for Multimodal Understanding and Interaction
items.summary: Describes an Android agent architecture combining multimodal perception, working and personal memory, hybrid XML/visual grounding, and reusable skills captured from user interactions.

items.name: Constraining Host-Level Abuse in Self-Hosted Computer-Use Agents via TEE-Backed Isolation
items.summary: A TEE-backed design confines host operations by self-hosted computer-use agents, classifying and authorizing actions before constrained local execution.

items.name: BAMI: Training-Free Bias Mitigation in GUI Grounding
items.summary: BAMI uses coarse-to-fine focus and candidate selection at inference time to address precision and ambiguity errors in GUI grounding.

items.name: Weblica: Scalable and Reproducible Training Environments for Visual Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces Weblica, which combines HTTP-level capture and replay with website-grounded environment synthesis. The resulting interactive web environments support reinforcement learning and tests of navigation transfer and inference-time scaling.

items.name: Securing Computer-Use Agents: A Unified Architecture-Lifecycle Framework for Deployment-Grounded Reliability
items.summary: Survey of computer-use agent reliability and security across browsers, desktops, and mobile apps, using architecture and lifecycle views to map failures and controls.

items.name: Region4Web: Rethinking Observation Space Granularity for Web Agents
items.summary: Reorganizes webpage accessibility trees into functional regions through hierarchical decomposition and semantic abstraction. PageDigest supplies a persistent region-level observation to web agents, evaluated on WebArena.

items.name: LiteGUI: Lightweight GUI Agents via Multi-Solution Guided Distillation and Dual-Level Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: LiteGUI trains lightweight GUI agents on logged states with guided on-policy distillation and dual-level RL, supported by its multi-solution Lite-Dataset.

items.name: Computer Use at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
items.summary: DigiWorld is a sandboxed mobile-app benchmark for computer-use agents, paired with PRISM environment principles and a confidence-interval aggregation method.

items.name: WebTrap: Stealthy Mid-Task Hijacking of Browser Agents During Navigation
items.summary: WebTrap injects mid-task instructions into browser-agent navigation to steer an agent toward an attacker goal before it resumes the user's task.

items.name: OTora: A Unified Red Teaming Framework for Reasoning-Level Denial-of-Service in LLM Agents
items.summary: OTora generates attacks that increase reasoning and tool use in multi-step LLM agents while preserving task outcomes; evaluations include WebShop agents.

items.name: Mem-W: Latent Memory-Native GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces Mem-W, which compresses previous trajectories and current-session segments into latent memory tokens used directly by the GUI policy. Self-distillation and outcome supervision train this memory representation for web and mobile navigation.

items.name: Don't Click That: Teaching Web Agents to Resist Deceptive Interfaces
items.summary: DUDE combines asymmetric hybrid-reward learning with summaries of deceptive-interface failures to guide safer web actions. Its RUC benchmark evaluates deception susceptibility alongside ordinary task performance across interface scenarios.

items.name: How Mobile World Model Guides GUI Agents?
items.summary: Compares mobile world models that predict state changes as delta text, full text, images or renderable code. Downstream Android benchmarks examine synthetic training trajectories and test-time guidance, including limits of post-action reflection.

items.name: WildClawBench: A Benchmark for Real-World, Long-Horizon Agent Evaluation
items.summary: WildClawBench evaluates CLI agents on long, multimodal tasks in Docker containers with real tools, using task checks, side-effect audits, and a semantic judge.

items.name: MMTB: Evaluating Terminal Agents on Multimedia-File Tasks
items.summary: MultiMedia-TerminalBench evaluates agents that use terminal tools to work with audio and video files. The Terminus-MM harness adds multimedia perception to study how accessible evidence changes executable workflows and task outcomes.

items.name: ReVision: Scaling Computer-Use Agents via Temporal Visual Redundancy Reduction
items.summary: Trains GUI agents with a learned selector that removes repeated visual patches across consecutive screenshots while preserving spatial structure. ReVision evaluates this history representation on OSWorld, WebTailBench and AgentNetBench.

items.name: Executable Agentic Memory for GUI Agent
items.summary: Executable Agentic Memory stores GUI routines in a knowledge graph built through state-aware exploration and action-group mining. A learned value model guides tree search over this executable memory for retrieval-based planning, with AndroidWorld and efficiency evaluation.

items.name: ToolCUA: Towards Optimal GUI-Tool Path Orchestration for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: ToolCUA synthesizes interleaved GUI/tool trajectories and trains agents to choose between graphical actions and higher-level tools. Staged supervised and reinforcement learning culminate in online hybrid-environment training with a reward for efficient execution paths.

items.name: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
items.summary: LongMemEval-V2 asks memory systems to recover environment knowledge from long web-agent histories for question answering. Its AgentRunbook variants contrast indexed knowledge pools with coding-agent retrieval from stored trajectory files.

items.name: Covering Human Action Space for Computer Use: Data Synthesis and Benchmark
items.summary: Introduces CUActSpot to evaluate clicks, drags, drawing and other screen interactions across GUI, text, tables, canvases and natural images. A renderer-based pipeline records geometry and screenshots, then generates matching instructions and action traces for training a grounding model.

items.name: What Happens Before Decoding? Prefill Determines GUI Grounding in VLMs
items.summary: Re-Prefill adds an attention-guided second prefill pass that revisits candidate screen regions before coordinate generation. The study evaluates this training-free intervention across GUI-grounding models and benchmarks.

items.name: SimPersona: Learning Discrete Buyer Personas from Raw Clickstreams for Grounded E-Commerce Agents
items.summary: SimPersona learns buyer types from clickstreams and uses persona tokens to condition web agents trained on browsing traces for live storefront tasks.

items.name: Web Agents Should Adopt the Plan-Then-Execute Paradigm
items.summary: Argues for compiling web tasks into predefined execution graphs before exposing an agent to untrusted runtime content. Its WebArena task analysis identifies typed, semantically complete website tools as a prerequisite and distinguishes this interface proposal from reactive click-level control.

items.name: Beyond Binary: Reframing GUI Critique as Continuous Semantic Alignment
items.summary: BBCritic ranks candidate GUI-agent actions through instruction–action alignment, while BBBench evaluates fine-grained ranking with a hierarchical action taxonomy.

items.name: Video2GUI: Synthesizing Large-Scale Interaction Trajectories for Generalized GUI Agent Pretraining
items.summary: Video2GUI extracts GUI interaction trajectories from tutorial videos to build WildGUI, a pretraining dataset spanning applications and websites.
items.venue: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning

items.name: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
items.summary: A study shows that websites can infer the model behind a browser agent from passively recorded UI actions and timing traces across web tasks.

items.name: WARD: Adversarially Robust Defense of Web Agents Against Prompt Injections
items.summary: WARD guards web agents against prompt injections in HTML and visual interfaces, using web data and adaptive attacker–guard training.

items.name: Orchard: An Open-Source Agentic Modeling Framework
items.summary: Orchard provides an environment service and training recipes for several agent domains, including Orchard-GUI, a vision-language computer-use agent.

items.name: DRS-GUI: Dynamic Region Search for Training-Free GUI Grounding
items.summary: DRS-GUI searches screenshot regions through focus, shift and scatter operations selected by a tree-search planner. A region-quality reward guides this training-free perceptual search before final GUI grounding.

items.name: SaaS-Bench: Can Computer-Use Agents Leverage Real-World SaaS to Solve Professional Workflows?
items.summary: SaaS-Bench evaluates browser agents on professional workflows across self-hosted applications. Weighted checkpoints measure task completion and partial progress, with application-state checks and configured content judges documented in the official harness.

items.name: PersonaFingerprint: Measuring Persona Inference on Modern Websites with LLM-Driven Browsing
items.summary: PersonaFingerprint studies persona inference from encrypted web traffic, using a persona-constrained computer-use agent to browse real websites and collect traces.

items.name: PAGER: Bridging the Semantic-Execution Gap in Point-Precise Geometric GUI Control
items.summary: Introduces PAGE Bench for point-precise geometric GUI construction and PAGER, an agent that plans around primitive dependencies and executes pixel-level actions.

items.name: ScreenSearch: Uncertainty-Aware OS Exploration
items.summary: ScreenSearch explores desktop GUI states by indexing and deduplicating UIA-tree screens, then using outcome ambiguity and frontier rewards to guide graph search.

items.name: ShopGym: An Integrated Framework for Realistic Simulation and Scalable Benchmarking of E-Commerce Web Agents
items.summary: ShopGym builds sandbox e-commerce storefronts from live shops and generates catalog-grounded tasks for evaluating web shopping agents in resettable environments.

items.name: WinDeskGround: A Benchmark for Robust GUI Grounding in Complex Multi-Window Desktop Environments
items.summary: WinDeskGround synthesizes multi-window desktop layouts with controlled occlusion, density and semantic similarity to test GUI grounding robustness. Its instruction-target benchmark measures how localization changes when interfaces depart from simple single-layer scenes.

items.name: Skim: Speculative Execution for Fast and Efficient Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces Skim, a speculative execution framework for web agents that learns site URL and answer patterns offline, then uses them to answer matching queries with a small model.

items.name: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents
items.summary: SE-GA retrieves hierarchical memories during inference and uses the collected experience in a separate policy-improvement pipeline. Its evaluation includes offline grounding/action tasks and online Android interaction, which measure different capabilities.

items.name: TriAxialKV: Toward Extreme Low-Precision KV-Cache Quantization for Agentic Inference Tasks
items.summary: TriAxialKV assigns KV-cache precision by token recency, modality, and role for agentic inference, with a computer-use agent on OSWorld among its evaluations.

items.name: TClone: Low-Latency Forking of Live GUI Environments for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: TClone versions live GUI workspaces through snapshots, isolated forks, rollback and selective commit or merge. It separates fast branch creation from durable checkpoints using copy-on-write sharing, filesystem versioning and asynchronous checkpointing, with end-to-end agent-loop latency measurements.

items.name: DiagEval: Trajectory-Conditioned Diagnosis for Reliable Software Evaluation with GUI Agents
items.summary: DiagEval diagnoses failed GUI-agent evaluations of interactive software by reusing failed trajectories for targeted probes that distinguish execution errors from defects.

items.name: MUIAnno: An Expert-Annotated Dataset and Evaluation Benchmark for Mobile UI Understanding
items.summary: MUIAnno provides expert labels for elements in manually explored mobile-app screens, with a web annotation tool that emits structured JSON. It also supplies UI-element detection baselines for the dataset.

items.name: DocOS: Towards Proactive Document-Guided Actions in GUI Agents
items.summary: DocOS benchmarks agents that search online documentation and translate procedural instructions into GUI actions in interactive web environments. It separates failures to retrieve useful procedures from failures to ground retrieved instructions into executable actions.

items.name: MementoGUI: Learning Agentic Multimodal Memory Control for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
items.summary: MementoGUI learns a controller for selecting, compressing and retrieving textual and region-level visual memories while leaving the GUI-agent backbone fixed. It also converts computer-use traces into controller training data and evaluates semantic actions, progress and memory consistency on long-horizon tasks.

items.name: OmniGUI: Benchmarking GUI Agents in Omni-Modal Smartphone Environments
items.summary: OmniGUI evaluates step-level action prediction from interleaved smartphone screenshots, synchronous audio and video. Expert demonstrations carry multimodal-dependency annotations, and initial baselines use native multimodal models as agent proxies to study temporal and audio-related failures.

items.name: AQuaUI: Visual Token Reduction for GUI Agents with Adaptive Quadtrees
items.summary: AQuaUI reduces screenshot tokens for GUI agents at inference time with adaptive quadtrees that retain spatial positions and reuse prior tree structure across steps.

items.name: What and When to Distill: Selective Hindsight Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents
items.summary: SERL trains multi-turn agents by using task rewards and selective step feedback to weight updates, with WebShop among its evaluation settings.

items.name: CutVerse: A Compositional GUI Agents Benchmark for Media Post-Production Editing
items.summary: Cutverse benchmarks GUI agents on long editing workflows across professional media applications and parses recordings and input logs into grounded action trajectories.

items.name: OpenComputer: Verifiable Software Worlds for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces OpenComputer, which builds desktop tasks around application-state verifiers and refines those verifiers using execution feedback. An evaluation harness records trajectories and assigns auditable partial credit across professional software workflows.

items.name: Weasel: Out-of-Domain Generalization for Web Agents via Importance-Diversity Data Selection
items.summary: Weasel selects web-agent training steps by balancing importance and diversity across states, sites and interaction patterns. It also prunes training accessibility trees around known action targets and regenerates rationales to match the model’s reasoning style.

items.name: MemGym: a Long-Horizon Memory Environment for LLM Agents
items.summary: MemGym benchmarks agent memory across several task regimes, including computer use on WebArena-Infinity, with scores designed to isolate memory performance.

items.name: Agent JIT Compilation for Latency-Optimizing Web Agent Planning and Scheduling
items.summary: Agent JIT compilation turns browser task descriptions into validated executable plans containing model calls, tools and parallel work. A cost-based scheduler and pre/postcondition protocol target latency and incorrect tool use in web-agent execution.

items.name: Spreadsheet-RL: Advancing Large Language Model Agents on Realistic Spreadsheet Tasks via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Spreadsheet-RL trains spreadsheet agents with RL in a Microsoft Excel environment exposed through a Python sandbox and supplies the Domain-Spreadsheet benchmark.

items.name: DRIVE: Modeling Skills at the Reasoning and Interaction Levels for Web Agents under Continual Learning
items.summary: DRIVE separates reusable reasoning skills from page-specific interaction skills for web agents, retrieving both to plan tasks and execute actions on websites.

items.name: PANDO: Efficient Multimodal AI Agents via Online Skill Distillation
items.summary: Analyzes inefficiency in VisualWebArena trajectories and distills reusable online skills to reduce repeated actions and token overhead in multimodal web agents.

items.name: ScaleWoB: Guiding GUI Agents with Coding Agents via Large-Scale Environmental Synthesis
items.summary: Introduces ScaleWoB, which synthesizes interactive GUI environments as backend-free webpages with verifiable rewards. Its mobile-oriented benchmark evaluates agent execution and compares selected synthetic tasks with real-app behavior.

items.name: CUA-Gym: Scaling Verifiable Training Environments and Tasks for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Presents CUA-Gym, which co-generates instructions, initial and target states, and executable reward checks through generator-discriminator iterations. Mock web applications expand training environments, with learned agents evaluated on OSWorld-Verified and WebArena.

items.name: AgentHijack: Benchmarking Computer Use Agent Robustness to Common Environment Corruptions
items.summary: Introduces AgentHijack, a benchmark for desktop computer-use agents facing pop-ups, resolution changes and other common corruptions, alongside an agent that checks its environment.

items.name: Claw-Anything: Benchmarking Always-On Personal Assistants with Broader Access to User's Digital World
items.summary: Claw-Anything benchmarks persistent personal assistance across activity histories, backend services and integrated GUI/CLI interaction. Its simulated event histories introduce irrelevant or conflicting context, and a separate generation pipeline supplies training environments.

items.name: MobileGym: A Verifiable and Highly Parallel Simulation Platform for Mobile GUI Agent Research
items.summary: Introduces MobileGym, a browser-hosted simulation of mobile app interactions whose configurable JSON state supports deterministic judging and parallel rollouts. MobileGym-Bench adds parameterized tasks, with experiments examining online training and transfer to real devices.

items.name: VISTA: An End-to-End Benchmark for Visual Spec-to-Web-App Coding Agents
items.summary: VISTA evaluates coding agents that turn design handoffs into working web and Android applications. Its evaluator locates annotated interactive components and probes their behavior, keeping visual localization distinct from functional correctness.

items.name: Anchor: Preventing Artifact Drift for Reliable Agent Verification
items.summary: Anchor builds ERP-Bench by generating procurement and manufacturing tasks with shared state verifiers for evaluating browser and computer-use agents.

items.name: MobileExplorer: Accelerating On-Device Inference for Mobile GUI Agents via Online Exploration
items.summary: MobileExplorer probes relevant UI elements while an on-device model is reasoning, then supplies the exploration trace as compact context. A two-level rollback mechanism restores the working state when simple backtracking fails.

items.name: ChartAct: A Benchmark for Dynamic Chart Understanding
items.summary: ChartAct benchmarks multimodal models and GUI agents on interactive charts from websites, requiring actions such as hovering or zooming to answer questions.

items.name: Scaling, Benchmarking, and Reasoning of Vision-Language Agents for Mobile GUI Navigation
items.summary: HyperTrack provides mobile GUI navigation tasks across Chinese apps, while GUIEvalKit benchmarks VLM agents offline and supports analysis of training scale and history.

items.name: AndroidDaily: A Verifiable Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents on Real-World Closed-Source Applications
items.summary: AndroidDaily evaluates mobile GUI agents on daily workflows in closed-source Android apps. Its GRADE evaluator follows visual trajectories against operational obligations, output-quality requirements and negative constraints, producing process-level diagnostics without hidden app state.

items.name: MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content
items.summary: MIRAGE constructs mobile screenshot injections in ordinary user-content regions through localization, contextual payload generation and realism curation. Its evaluation separates visual realism from attack effectiveness against pixel-observing GUI agents.

items.name: GUI Agents for Continual Game Generation
items.summary: PlaytestArena evaluates generated browser games using expected in-play behaviors adjudicated by GUI agents. Play2Code pairs a coding agent with a rubric-blind GUI playtester whose interaction traces and feedback guide iterative refinement, with a separate final judge.

items.name: GUI-CIDER: Mid-training GUI Agents via Causal Internalization and Density-aware Exemplar Reselection
items.summary: GUI-CIDER turns GUI trajectories into textual planning and causal interface knowledge, reselects exemplars for causal structure and low redundancy, then mid-trains GUI agents on that corpus.

items.name: Mobile-Aptus: Confidence-Driven Proactive and Robust Interaction in MLLM-based Mobile-Using Agents
items.summary: Mobile-Aptus trains mobile agents to output actions and confidence scores, then corrects confidence bias to guide when they request human help.

items.name: MaskClaw: Edge-Side Personalized Privacy Arbitration for GUI Agents with Behavior-Driven Skill Evolution
items.summary: MaskClaw makes local Allow, Mask or Ask decisions before GUI screenshots leave a trusted environment, using visual evidence and personalized policy memory. Its benchmark and designed evolution scenarios test how corrections and edits can become privacy skills checked by a sandbox gate.

items.name: Learn from Weaknesses: Automated Domain Specialization for Small Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: LearnWeak specializes small computer-use agents by finding domain-specific weaknesses, generating targeted tasks, and training separately for planning and execution errors.

items.name: PRO-CUA: Process-Reward Optimization for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: PRO-CUA trains computer-use agents with step-level RL, scoring candidate actions from live rollouts with a process reward model and evaluating on live web benchmarks.

items.name: GTA: Generating Long-Horizon Tasks for Web Agents at Scale
items.summary: GTA generates multi-hop web-agent tasks and executable trajectories through crawling, retrieval, and validation, releasing a benchmark built from over 50 websites.

items.name: STAMP: Training Explicit Memory for Mobile GUI Agents in Controllable and Scalable Virtual Environments
items.summary: STAMP trains explicit memory for mobile GUI agents in virtual environments by injecting facts into generated tasks and using supervised data and online RL.

items.name: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents: Comprehensive Evaluation with a Lightweight Framework
items.summary: Introduces a lightweight framework for evaluating HTML reduction in web agents, using Minimal Failure Set coverage to assess pruning and optimize latency.

items.name: Recovering Policy-Induced Errors: Benchmarking and Trajectory Synthesis for Robust GUI Agents
items.summary: GUI-RobustEval measures how GUI agents recover from their own errors, while RoTS synthesizes recovery trajectories for training on varied failure modes.

items.name: PhoneWorld: From Real-App Trajectories to Dynamic and Verifiable Environments for Phone-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces PhoneWorld, which converts observed app pages, transitions and state changes into executable Android environments through a build-inspect-repair process. Generated tasks and programmatic verifiers support benchmarking, trajectory collection and online training.

items.name: UI-KOBE: Knowledge-Oriented Behavior Exploration for Lightweight Graph-Guided GUI Agents
items.summary: UI-KOBE explores mobile applications to build graphs of UI states and executable transitions. A lightweight agent then matches its current screenshot to the graph and chooses a transition, local action, completion signal or fallback action.

items.name: DiffSpot: Can VLMs Spot Fine-Grained Visual Differences in Web Interfaces?
items.summary: DiffSpot benchmarks detection of fine visual changes in rendered web interfaces using image pairs created by single-property CSS mutations.

items.name: GUI-C$^2$: Coarse-to-Fine GUI Grounding via Difficulty-Aware Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Introduces GUI-D to score training samples by difficulty and GUI-C² to refine screen-element locations through area-gated cropping and reinforcement learning.

items.name: BlueFin: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Financial Spreadsheets
items.summary: Introduces BlueFin, a benchmark and evaluation framework for agents handling professional finance spreadsheet workbooks through synthesis, manipulation, and comprehension tasks.

items.name: Learning to Adapt: Self-Improving Web Agent via Cognitive-Aware Exploration
items.summary: Introduces SCALE, which uses exploration roles and graph planning to train web agents, and SCALE-20k, a dataset of tasks and demonstrations from real websites.

items.name: Masking Stale Observations Helps Search Agents -- Until It Doesn't: A Regime Map and Its Mechanism
items.summary: Studies when masking older retrieved pages helps long-horizon search agents manage context, using offline and live-web search benchmarks and analysis of reopened pages.

items.name: BraveGuard: From Open-World Threats to Safer Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces BraveGuard, a framework that turns emerging threats and computer-use agent trajectories into training supervision for guards that monitor multi-step safety risks.

items.name: Multi-Agent Computer Use
items.summary: MACU represents computer-use objectives as a dependency graph whose manager dispatches parallel subagents and revises tasks as new information arrives. Desktop and web experiments examine coordination, information handoff and task-completion time.

items.name: STaR-KV: Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Re-weighting for KV Cache Compression in GUI Vision-Language Models
items.summary: STaR-KV compresses GUI-agent KV caches by calibrating visual-token importance across attention subspaces and interaction time. Its training-free scoring combines spatial specialization, temporal redundancy and an adaptive temperature, evaluated at matched cache budgets.

items.name: OpenWebRL: Demystifying Online Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning for Visual Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces OpenWebRL, a framework for training visual web agents with online multi-turn reinforcement learning on live websites, including browser infrastructure and success judging.

items.name: Context-Aware Workflow Decomposition for Automated Mobile UI Annotation Using Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: Studies staged prompting for automated mobile UI element annotation, comparing workflow depths and element groupings on expert-annotated MUIAnno screens.

items.name: DeskCraft: Benchmarking Desktop Agents on Professional Workflows and Human-in-the-Loop Collaboration
items.summary: DeskCraft evaluates professional desktop workflows and human-agent collaboration through mid-execution clarification, interruption and post-completion feedback. Its tasks cover creative applications and expose difficulties in long-horizon execution and proactive clarification.

items.name: MedCUA-Bench: A Screenshot-Only Benchmark for Clinical Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: MedCUA-Bench evaluates screenshot-only clinical interface workflows using paired intent- and step-level goals. It combines reconstructed medical interfaces with completion and clinical-safety checks, and separately reports results on a real OpenEMR system.

items.name: Perceive Before Reasoning: A Pre-Reasoning Perception Framework for Efficient and Reliable Proactive Mobile Agents
items.summary: Introduces PRPF, a two-stage framework for proactive mobile agents that gates intervention with MPP and invokes PAR only when assistance is warranted.

items.name: CLI-Anything: Towards Agent-Native Computer Use
items.summary: CLI-Anything argues for application interfaces built around structured commands, explicit state and execution feedback. It describes transforming existing software into command-line harnesses and organizing that approach through CLI-Hub.

items.name: Demo2Tutorial: From Human Experience to Multimodal Software Tutorials
items.summary: Introduces Demo2Tutorial, which turns recorded software interactions into multimodal tutorials with task graphs and reports benefits for GUI-agent planning.

items.name: Online Skill Learning for Web Agents via State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval
items.summary: State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval extracts reusable sub-procedures from completed web trajectories and represents them as paired text and code. Skills are retrieved against both the current webpage state and the task goal at intermediate execution steps.

items.name: MIRAGE: Mobile Agents with Implicit Reasoning and Generative World Models
items.summary: Introduces MIRAGE, which trains mobile app agents to reason in compact latent states and anticipate future screenshots, reducing generated tokens during action selection.

items.name: Benchmarking Living-Screen-Native GUI Agents on Short-Video Platforms
items.summary: LivingScreen evaluates agents in a browser-based short-video environment where observing content consumes time and affects subsequent actions. Its task suite scores accuracy together with information efficiency to diagnose over- and under-observation on continuously changing screens.

items.name: AppAgent-Claw: CLI Is All You Need for GUI Automation
items.summary: Introduces AppAgent-Claw, which records demonstrated GUI workflows as reusable OpenClaw skills, locates visual targets during replay and checks intended on-screen effects.

items.name: Domain-Conditioned Safety in Frontier Computer-Using Agents: A 793-Episode Browser Benchmark, a Coding-Domain Cross-Reference, and a Reproducibility Audit of Recent Red-Teaming
items.summary: Introduces CUA-HandCrafted, a browser-agent red-teaming benchmark that varies attack templates, tasks and system prompts. Its domain comparison and reproducibility audit caution against transferring browser-surface safety conclusions to coding agents or unreleased optimized injections.

items.name: AsyncWebRL: Efficient Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Step Visual Web Agents
items.summary: AsyncWebRL overlaps web-agent rollouts, updates and policy refresh while managing screenshot handling and a persistent rollout pool. It also replaces trajectory-length normalization in multi-step GRPO to reduce verbose failed trajectories, with throughput and out-of-distribution evaluation.

items.name: PerceptUI: LLM Agents as Human-Aligned Synthetic Users for UI/UX Evaluation
items.summary: Introduces PerceptUI, a persona-conditioned model for predicting how particular users answer questions about interfaces, supporting synthetic UI/UX evaluation.

items.name: DragOn: A Benchmark and Dataset for Drag-Based GUI Interactions
items.summary: DragOn supplies drag-grounding training data and a held-out benchmark for highlighting text, selecting cells, resizing elements and moving sliders. It evaluates existing vision-language models and a model fine-tuned on the drag tasks.

items.name: MacArena: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on an Online macOS Environment
items.summary: MacArena runs computer-use tasks through Apple’s virtualization framework on Apple Silicon, combining task ports with macOS-native workloads. It distinguishes the ported and native subsets when examining agent performance and cross-platform transfer.

items.name: Signal-Driven Observation for Long-Horizon Web Agents
items.summary: Proposes Signal-Driven Observation: a separate call selects relevant DOM elements and selectors, and a detector requests new observations only after meaningful browser events or failures. The paper frames observation timing and compression as an architectural research problem for long-horizon web agents.

items.name: StainFlow: Entity-Stain Tracking and Evidence Linking for Process Rewards in GUI Agents
items.summary: StainFlow tracks visually verifiable task entities through GUI trajectories to identify phases and retrieve focused evidence windows. Its process-reward model is tested for both online policy learning and trajectory-completion judgments.

items.name: Self-evolving LLM agents with in-distribution Optimization
items.summary: Introduces Q-Evolve, which derives step-wise rewards from an in-distribution critic for LLM agent learning; WebShop is one of its interactive evaluation settings.

items.name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
items.summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.

items.name: RunAgent SuperBrowser: A Theory of Autonomous Web Navigation Grounded in Human Browsing Behaviour
items.summary: SUPERBROWSER combines screenshot-based target proposals with separate orchestration, planning and action roles. A bounded ledger and context-eviction process retain recent actions, task facts and checkpoints during browser execution.

items.name: WeaveBench: A Long-Horizon, Real-World Benchmark for Computer-Use Agents with Hybrid Interfaces
items.summary: WeaveBench requires agents to combine GUI, command-line and code operations within long tasks on an Ubuntu desktop. A trajectory-aware judge checks deliverables and interaction evidence, including shortcut behavior that outcome-only grading can miss.

items.name: AliyunConsoleAgent: Training Web Agents in Real-World Cloud Environments via Distillation and Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: AliyunConsoleAgent trains browser agents to verify documented procedures against changing cloud-console UIs through trajectory distillation and online GRPO. Provisioned rollout environments and backend audit-log checks support training and outcome evaluation.

items.name: iOSWorld: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Phone Agents
items.summary: Introduces a native iOS simulator benchmark with persistent user data, multi-app tasks, and personalization-dependent phone workflows.

items.name: WebChallenger: A Reliable and Efficient Generalist Web Agent
items.summary: WebChallenger builds a hierarchical DOM-derived page representation for selective observation, reusable site maps and compound actions. The framework combines these mechanisms without model fine-tuning and evaluates generalization across multiple web-agent benchmarks.

items.name: GUI-AC: Enhancing Continual Learning in GUI Agents
items.summary: GUI-AC uses grounding certainty to adjust advantage weighting and policy-clipping bounds during continual reinforcement fine-tuning. Its mechanisms aim to suppress noisy confidence updates while retaining exploration under shifting GUI domains and resolutions.

items.name: MemVenom: Triggered Poisoning of Multimodal Memories in Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces MemVenom, a black-box attack that plants coordinated text and image content in web-agent memory to trigger retrieval and redirect later actions.

items.name: Workflow-GYM: Towards Long-Horizon Evaluation of Computer-use Agentic tasks in Real-World Professional Fields
items.summary: Workflow-GYM evaluates long GUI workflows in professional software. Its analysis examines failures such as omitted stages, accumulated errors and goal drift during specialized end-to-end work.

items.name: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: HiViG combines a compact history of completed actions with a visually grounded critic that checks proposed coordinates before execution. Its evaluations separate history-related planning failures from errors caused by targeting the wrong screen element.

items.name: Speculative Rollback Correction for Quality-Diverse Web Agent Imitation
items.summary: Speculative Rollback Correction lets a student web agent execute short branches before teacher review localizes harmful deviations. Verified continuations and localized corrections feed supervised training while an archive retains diverse successful solutions.

items.name: CAPED: Context-Aware Privacy Exposure Defense for Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: CAPED filters mobile screenshots before upload by combining task requirements, screen context and parsed UI elements to mask incidental private content. AndroidWorld and a controlled seeded privacy evaluation examine leakage reduction alongside task utility and prototype costs.

items.name: Reasoning for Mobile User Experience with Multimodal LLMs: Task, Benchmark, and Approach
items.summary: Introduces UXBench for diagnosing usability issues from UI screenshots and UI-UX, a reinforcement-trained model for reasoning about those interface problems.

items.name: ComAct: Reframing Professional Software Manipulation via COM-as-Action Paradigm
items.summary: ComAct proposes COM program synthesis as an alternative interface for manipulating professional software and introduces ComCADBench with GUI-based comparison agents. ComActor adds a staged training and correction approach, supported by a Windows-container training platform.

items.name: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
items.summary: StakeBench evaluates prompt-injection harm to different stakeholders in shopping web-agent workflows. Its executable cases separate attack objectives and assess both outcomes and execution processes to reveal how the same attack pattern can affect different parties.

items.name: Benchmarking Web Agent Safety under E-commerce Deceptive Interfaces
items.summary: Introduces WebDecept, a plugin for injecting deceptive e-commerce interface patterns during web-agent tasks and evaluating how multimodal agents respond.

items.name: A Benchmark and Framework for Evaluating Next Action Predictions in Spreadsheets
items.summary: Introduces a benchmark and online evaluation method for predicting the next spreadsheet action from a user's action history, using curated action sequences.

items.name: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents
items.summary: This study finds that full-image visual memory can reduce some state errors while worsening action-level failures. Its AGMem alternative stores local crops associated with successful actions or recovery and evaluates their use in desktop GUI tasks.

items.name: Running the Gauntlet: Hard Agentic Tasks
items.summary: Introduces GauntletBench, a web-based benchmark of vision-intensive tasks in five professional applications for assessing agent perception, 3D reasoning, and generalisation.

items.name: VISTA: View-Consistent Self-Verified Training for GUI Grounding
items.summary: VISTA forms GRPO comparison groups from target-preserving crops of the same GUI instance with exactly remapped target boxes. A conditional, advantage-weighted cross-view anchor supplies additional supervision without entering the group baseline, and evaluation includes view-consistency robustness.

items.name: PhoneHarness: Harnessing Phone-Use Agents through Mixed GUI, CLI, and Tool Actions
items.summary: PhoneHarness routes phone workflows across GUI actions, device-side commands and host tools while retaining auditable execution traces. Its accompanying benchmark checks observable task side effects, separating mixed-action execution from plausible final-answer generation.

items.name: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents
items.summary: Compares online skill and memory augmentations with a vanilla web agent given the same total inference-token budget. Across WebArena and WorkArena settings, it studies when module overhead removes aggregate gains and how rerun variability changes conclusions.

items.name: OSGuard: A Benchmark for Safety in Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Evaluates action-level guardrails and full computer tasks with environment-dependent safety constraints, separating safe completion from nominal success.

items.name: Where Did It Go Wrong? Process-Level Evaluation of Web Agents with Semantic State Tracking
items.summary: Introduces WebStep, a web-agent benchmark that records semantic states behind GUI interactions to analyze exploration, execution accuracy, and decisive errors across task steps.

items.name: LLM-as-Code: Agentic Programming for Agent Harness
items.summary: Proposes Agentic Programming, where code controls agent loops and invokes LLM-as-Code for reasoning; a computer-use case study examines long visual action sequences.

items.name: FraudSMSWalker: Benchmarking Agentic Large Language Models for SMS-to-Webpage Fraud Detection
items.summary: FraudSMSWalker tests browser agents on bilingual SMS-to-webpage fraud judgments while hiding URL and reputation shortcuts. Its controlled chains include difficult benign login/payment cases and evaluate whether classifications remain supported by the visible message and page evidence.

items.name: MyPCBench: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: MyPCBench tests personal-assistant tasks on a Linux desktop with simulated web applications and data for a single fictional persona. A shared computer-and-shell interface enables evaluation of cross-application workflows that depend on personal context and account-like state.

items.name: LabOSBench: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents for Scientific Instrument Control
items.summary: LabOSBench evaluates GUI agents on browser-based scientific instrument simulators with configurable tasks and execution-based checks. Its subtask and end-to-end tests examine feedback-driven adjustment and long workflows without controlling physical instruments.

items.name: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report
items.summary: ProCUA-SFT generates tasks and synthetic trajectories on live desktops seeded with document content, checking task preconditions before rollout. The resulting step-prefix examples are formatted to match inference context and used for supervised GUI-agent fine-tuning.

items.name: Beyond Domains: Reusing Web Skills via Transferable Interaction Patterns
items.summary: Introduces SkillMigrator, a web agent that turns successful interactions into reusable skills and transfers them between sites by matching page layouts and live element references.

items.name: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks
items.summary: PreAct compiles successful screen-interaction runs into guarded state-machine programs for repeated tasks. It validates programs from clean states before storage and returns control to the agent when replayed screen expectations fail, with tests across mobile, desktop and web.

items.name: Trust the Right Teacher: Quality-Aware Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
items.summary: Proposes quality-aware self-distillation for GUI coordinate generation under student-produced prefixes. A correctness-aware gate suppresses coordinate-token supervision outside the target box, while teacher-probability scaling adjusts the remaining signal strength.

items.name: VISUALSKILL: Multimodal Skills for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: VISUALSKILL organizes application-specific text and figures into hierarchical skills retrieved on demand through an MCP tool. Skills combine authored documentation with live UI exploration, and matched multimodal/text-only comparisons test their utility for interface identification and workflow-state verification.

items.name: HANSEL: Extracting Breadcrumbs from Web Agent Trajectories for Interactive Verification
items.summary: HANSEL extracts evidence pages and snippets from browser-agent traces and preserves relevant page state in interactive verification views. It flags untraceable answers and evaluates evidence selection and human verification effort separately.

items.name: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation for GUI Agents
items.summary: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation first lets a policy reach its own off-trajectory states, then uses skill guidance to collect successful continuations. Mixing those continuations with expert traces supplies supervision for recovery states absent from demonstrations.

items.name: Beyond the GUI Paradigm: Do Mobile Agents Need the Phone Screen?
items.summary: This study compares general coding agents using mobile command-line access with reproducible GUI agents on AndroidWorld and MobileWorld. It also supplies oracle CLI analyses and a separate task suite for operations such as bulk changes, filtering and hidden device state.

items.name: MemGUI-Agent: An End-to-End Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agent with Proactive Context Management
items.summary: MemGUI-Agent makes context management an action chosen by the same policy that controls the mobile UI. Structured history, UI-state and recent-step fields are trained from annotated trajectories to retain cross-app facts while limiting context growth.

items.name: MobileForge: Annotation-Free Adaptation for Mobile GUI Agents with Hierarchical Feedback-Guided Policy Optimization
items.summary: MobileForge couples real-app exploration and generated tasks with hierarchical feedback for mobile-agent adaptation. Its optimizer turns trajectory outcomes, step feedback and corrective hints into contextualized GRPO updates, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and a GUI-only MobileWorld split.

items.name: Automating SKILL.md Generation for Computer-Using Agents via Interaction Trajectory Mining
items.summary: Segments and clusters GUI trajectories into inspectable skills, then trains a skill-aware policy from those annotations. Its diagnostic results distinguish readable source-domain clusters from reliable transfer and report limited or absent downstream gains.

items.name: OctoNest: Adaptive Cross-Device Execution through Stateful Control
items.summary: Introduces OctoNest, which coordinates device agents, revises task assignments from execution feedback, and switches local interaction modalities; CAPEBench evaluates cross-device tasks.

items.name: Darwin Mobile Agent: A Roadmap for Self-Evolution
items.summary: Describes asynchronous reinforcement-learning infrastructure using parallel cloud-hosted Android instances, explicit task lifecycles, and persistent-state management for mobile GUI interaction.

items.name: SkillHarness: Harnessing Safe Skills for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces SkillHarness, a framework for computer-use agents to learn and reuse skills under safety constraints when interactions include prompt injections or pop-ups.

items.name: MIRAGE: Stealthy Visual Prompt Injection for Vulnerability Detection in Web Agents
items.summary: MIRAGE evaluates targeted next-action hijacking from adversarial images restricted to legitimate third-party webpage regions. It combines diffusion-based image generation with execution-aware optimization and tests the constrained visual-injection setting on web-agent frameworks.

items.name: When Web Agents Finish but Still Fail: Reproducible Triggers and Trace Diagnostics for Parallel Web Exploration
items.summary: Introduces Parallel WebBench for parallel web exploration and uses verified URL trajectories to diagnose search loops, incomplete answers, and failures after evidence retrieval.

items.name: Fara-1.5: Scalable Learning Environments for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Builds browser-agent training trajectories with live and synthetic environments, solvers, user simulation, and complementary correctness and efficiency verifiers.

items.name: Whose Agent Are You? Multi-Layer Fingerprinting and Attribution of Autonomous Web Agents
items.summary: Builds a logging framework that combines network/protocol fingerprints with browser interaction behavior to attribute web-agent traffic. A decision-tree classifier is evaluated across six agent implementations, human browsing and conventional crawlers.

items.name: ChainWorld: Composing Long-Horizon Desktop Workloads from Atomic OSWorld Tasks
items.summary: ChainWorld composes compatible atomic OSWorld tasks into multi-objective desktop chains while preserving their evaluators. It compares giving the full sequence at once with revealing goals turn by turn, exposing different state and session-management failures.

items.name: MacAgentBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Real-World macOS Desktop
items.summary: Introduces macOS tasks spanning GUI and command-line interaction, with deterministic checks and intermediate-progress scoring for application workflows.

items.name: Agent MechSuits: Mechanistic Subspace Safety Steering for Multi-Turn CLI Agents
items.summary: Introduces Agent MechSuits, a framework that detects unsafe states and steers multi-turn CLI agents through hidden-representation interventions, alongside the MAS trajectory benchmark.

items.name: When AUC 0.998 Is Not Enough: A Candidate Evaluation Protocol for Hidden-State Probes of Indirect Prompt Injection in Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Proposes diagnostic controls for hidden-state probes of indirect prompt injection in multimodal computer-use agents, using a teacher-forced Mind2Web case study.

items.name: ENVS: Environment-Native Verified Search for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
items.summary: ENVS branches over GUI actions in live desktop VMs, verifies successful leaves, and converts them into balanced step-level training supervision. It also introduces OSWorld-Noisy to test recovery from dynamic interruptions while retaining the underlying tasks.

items.name: Capable but Careless: Do Computer-Use Agents Follow Contextual Integrity?
items.summary: AgentCIBench evaluates whether computer-use agents disclose information in ways that violate its original context. Deterministically scored scenarios test nearby sensitive UI content, ambiguous requests and recipient mismatches, including end-to-end agent execution.

items.name: AOHP: An Open-Source OS-Level Agent Harness for Personalized, Efficient and Secure Interaction
items.summary: Introduces AOHP, an Android OS-level harness that treats agents as system actors and provides adaptive interfaces, agent interfaces, and information-flow controls.

items.name: Reinforcement Learning for Computer-Use Agents with Autonomous Evaluation
items.summary: The framework uses a vision-language judge’s final-screen assessment as a terminal reward for GUI reinforcement learning. It models evaluator noise and corrects the reward estimator used by PPO across desktop benchmarks.

items.name: VisCritic: Visual State Comparison as Process Reward for GUI Agents
items.summary: VisCritic compares before/after screenshots through change-aware visual features and an action-conditioned critic. Weakly supervised samples from existing traces train judgments of action success, progress and error type for GUI-agent verification.

items.name: GUI vs. CLI: Execution Bottlenecks in Screen-Only and Skill-Mediated Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: This benchmark matches desktop goals, initial states and final-state verifiers across screen-only GUI and skill-mediated CLI agents. Its experiments separate graphical execution failures from missing CLI skill coverage, including a verifier-guided skill-augmentation condition.

items.name: GUI agent: Guided Exploration of User-Sensitive Screens
items.summary: This short paper develops an explorer agent that expands from a demonstrated GUI task to discover requests likely to reach user-sensitive screens. The proposed exploration supports identifying situations where task execution should be handed back to the user.

items.name: Uncertainty Quantification for Computer-Use Agents: A Benchmark across Vision-Language Models and GUI Grounding Datasets
items.summary: Argus benchmarks post-hoc uncertainty methods for single-step GUI grounding across open-weight and closed-source observation regimes. It tests calibration, rejection, error severity and conformal click regions, finding that uncertainty rankings transfer less reliably across model/interface regimes than across datasets for one model.

items.name: WinDOM: Self-Family Distillation for Small-Model GUI Grounding
items.summary: WinDOM obtains bounding-box supervision from a Windows 11 web reimplementation driven through Playwright, and studies rejection-sampling distillation for small GUI grounders. It treats the depth of the supervised cold start as a GRPO choice, comparing same-size EMA and larger same-family teachers.

items.name: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning
items.summary: PEEU explores web environments and turns hindsight experience into aligned high-level planning supervision. A hierarchical task-decomposition analysis examines why atomic-skill competence alone falls short of planning generalization across websites.

items.name: Ko-WideSearch: A Korean Breadth-Search Benchmark for Exhaustive Set Enumeration by Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces Ko-WideSearch, a Korean web-agent benchmark that asks agents to find every member of a set and fill a table of attributes for each member.

items.name: TUA-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Terminal-Use Agents
items.summary: TUA-Bench evaluates terminal-use agents on general digital tasks, including document editing, email, web information seeking and specialist software workflows. Tasks run in real terminals with deterministic setup and execution-based scoring.

items.name: Bridging VideoQA and Video-Guided Agentic Tasks via Generalized Keyframe Extraction
items.summary: Introduces VG-GUIBench to evaluate GUI agents following video tutorials, and TASKER to select task-relevant keyframes for video-guided tasks and VideoQA.

items.name: Agent-Computer Observation Interfaces Enable Dynamic Computer Use
items.summary: The Agent-Computer Observation Interface separates continuous perception from discrete computer actions using captured frames, audio transcription and persistent visual narration. DynaCU-Bench tests these components on dynamic browser tasks and static controls, with model-specific ablations showing that additional observations can also hurt.

items.name: OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
items.summary: Introduces extended computer-use workflows with realistic artifacts, changing information, hidden state, and partial-progress and safety assessments.

items.name: GUICrafter: Weakly-Supervised GUI Agent Leveraging Massive Unannotated Screenshots
items.summary: GUICrafter first learns grounding from large collections of unannotated screenshots and webpages, then uses a smaller high-quality dataset for reinforcement-learning calibration. The curriculum targets reduced dependence on manually annotated GUI training data.

items.name: SpreadsheetBench 2: Evaluating Agents on End-to-End Business Spreadsheet Workflows
items.summary: Introduces SpreadsheetBench 2, a benchmark of multi-sheet business spreadsheet workflows for agents, covering generation, debugging, and visualization tasks.

items.name: One Forward Beats Two: InnerZoom for Accurate and Efficient GUI Grounding
items.summary: InnerZoom preserves target-region cues from intermediate decoder layers and reinjects a compact evidence state during coordinate decoding. Its single-forward GUI grounder is compared with crop-and-rerun zooming and matched supervised/RL baselines for accuracy and inference cost.

items.name: On the Internet, Nobody Knows You're an LLM Bot: Unmasking Web Agents with Multi-Layer Fingerprinting
items.summary: Evaluates web agents against anti-bot mechanisms on instrumented honeysites and analyzes network, HTTP and browser fingerprints. The study compares resistance to blocking with the ability to distinguish agents, humans and agent implementations.

items.name: LUMOS: A Semantic Operating-System Layer for Accessibility-Grounded AI Agents
items.summary: LUMOS converts native accessibility metadata and browser UI structure into semantic interface blueprints with stable element identifiers and available actions. It combines live pointer-to-element grounding with an observe-act loop constrained to visible-UI primitives.

items.name: PPT-Eval: A Benchmark for Computer-Use Agents on PowerPoint Tasks
items.summary: Introduces PPT-Eval, a benchmark of PowerPoint creation and editing tasks for computer-use agents, with rubrics that score partial progress and presentation quality.

items.name: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Uses failed computer-use trajectories to diagnose failure modes and generate inference-time agent code patches, with light human verification. An OSWorld study evaluates this failure-driven improvement loop without additional model training.

items.name: Xiaomi-GUI-0 Technical Report
items.summary: Describes a mobile GUI agent trained through real-device interaction, corrected failure trajectories, supervised learning, and reinforcement learning.

items.name: What Memory Do GUI Agents Really Need? From Passive Records to Active Task-Driving States
items.summary: Proposes ATMem, an updated execution-state memory for long mobile GUI tasks, and STR-GRPO to train selective memory use; also introduces a mobile task benchmark.

items.name: DigitalCoach: Communication and Grounding Gaps in Human and Agentic Computer Use Coaching
items.summary: DigitalCoach records expert–novice software coaching conversations aligned with screen and input events. Automated and interactive evaluations examine how model coaches differ from humans in explanation, error diagnosis and visual grounding when helping a learner operate software.

items.name: BaRA: Budget-constrained and Reliable Web Data Collection Agent
items.summary: Introduces BaRA, a web data-collection agent that discovers live site links, checks extracted text, images, and videos, and uses history to recover from failures.

items.name: (A)I Sees What You Don't: Exploiting New Attack Surfaces in Third-Party Mobile Agents
items.summary: Analyzes cross-app privilege escalation and visual attack surfaces introduced by third-party VLM-powered mobile agents.

items.name: A Task-State Representation for Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces TSR, a training-free wrapper for long-horizon mobile GUI agents that tracks instructions, subgoal progress, and action outcomes separately from screen observations.

items.name: Do GUI Agents Believe Their Eyes? Diagnosing State-Belief Reliance on Pixels versus Structure
items.summary: Defines visual state reliance and probes whether GUI agents resolve screenshot/structure conflicts using pixels, serialized interface structure or prior beliefs. Paired interventions and live multi-step tests connect misattributed state beliefs to failures and compare consistency-based mitigations.

items.name: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Unified GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces Uni-GUI, a collection of executable desktop and mobile trajectories, and UI-MOPD, which trains a shared policy from its own rollouts using platform-specific teachers. The distillation procedure routes each visited state to the appropriate teacher to preserve distinct interaction conventions.

items.name: Agent Data Injection Attacks are Realistic Threats to AI Agents
items.summary: This study examines agent data injection, where untrusted content impersonates trusted metadata or tool-context data. It reports arbitrary-click vulnerabilities in web agents alongside separate coding-agent attacks, highlighting trust-boundary failures beyond instruction injection.

items.name: Untrusted Content Masking for Web Agents with Security Guarantees
items.summary: Untrusted Content Masking uses DOM structure to redact untrusted webpage regions before agent observation. A sandboxed interaction interface separates privileges so browser actions can proceed under the proposed trust-boundary model without exposing protected content to the planner.

items.name: TurnOPD: Making On-Policy Distillation Turn-Aware for Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Training
items.summary: Proposes TurnOPD, a rollout-depth and loss-budgeting method for training long-horizon language agents; WebShop is one of its evaluation settings.

items.name: WebRetriever: A Large-Scale Comprehensive Benchmark for Efficient Web Agent Evaluation
items.summary: WebRetriever evaluates navigation, knowledge-assisted interaction and end-to-end information-extraction workflows under separate protocols. Its NavEval judge uses richer interaction context to diagnose cases where navigation success and useful task completion diverge.

items.name: Prismata: Confining Cross-Site Prompt Injection in Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces Prismata, a defense for web agents that assigns trust labels to page content and enforces them by redacting content and restricting agent actions.

items.name: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
items.summary: Introduces UniClawBench, a benchmark of proactive agents on bilingual real-world tasks, evaluated in live Docker containers with stepwise checkpoints and simulated user feedback.

items.name: EvoCUA-1.5: Online Reinforcement Learning for Multi-turn Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: EvoCUA-1.5 trains multi-turn desktop agents through online reinforcement learning in executable sandboxes. It combines step-level policy optimization, task filtering and calibration, an adaptive curriculum, and asynchronous rollout handling with staleness control.

items.name: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and Harness for Multimodal Action and Guide Generation
items.summary: MAG jointly evaluates browser task actions and user-facing guides grounded in screenshots through element marks or pixel coordinates. Its harness covers annotation, live evaluation and joint metrics, with an expert-trajectory-augmented GRPO training study.

items.name: The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory
items.summary: The Entry–Propagation–Recovery framework traces where conflicting memory first changes an agent action, how the effect propagates and whether recovery occurs. WebArena and the controlled MemTrapBench separate memory-consumption failures across these stages.

items.name: SCALECUA: Scaling Computer Use Agents with Verifiable Task Synthesis and Efficient Online RL
items.summary: Scales computer-agent reinforcement learning through verifiable task generation, capability-aware rollout allocation, and segmented visual context.

items.name: StructAgent: Harness Long-horizon Digital Agents with Unified Causal Structure
items.summary: StructAgent maintains compact task state and regulates long-horizon execution through verified transitions and progress checkpoints. Its workflow supports evidence-based completion and targeted recovery, with desktop computer-use evaluation and a separate Minecraft extension.

items.name: Designing Agent-Ready Websites for AI Web Agents: A Framework for Machine Readability, Actionability, and Decision Reliability
items.summary: Proposes an agent-ready website design framework for e-commerce browser agents and compares it with a human-oriented site on shopping tasks, outcomes, steps, and token use.

items.name: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
items.summary: KnowAct-GUIClaw combines a host planner with pluggable GUI subagents, attributable experience memory and an evolving skill library. It uses user profiles and feedback for task decomposition and evaluates transfer across Android, iOS, HarmonyOS and Windows.

items.name: A Learning-Rate-Gated Failure of GRPO in a Small Language and Vision-Language Model Web Agent: A Controlled Null and Its Mechanism
items.summary: Studies a controlled setting where GRPO fails to improve a strong small web agent and can reduce text-track performance. Matched reachable-reward tasks and component grafting distinguish limited optimization headroom from learning-rate-dependent failure mechanisms.

items.name: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
items.summary: Introduces PalmClaw, an on-device phone agent framework that manages sessions, memory, and tools, exposing mobile capabilities through structured device-tool calls.

items.name: Multi-Head Latent Control: A Unified Interface for LLM Agent Decision Making
items.summary: Introduces Multi-Head Latent Control, a layer that reads frozen LLM or VLM hidden-state trajectories to signal when an agent should defer, seek clarification, use tools, abstain, or answer.

items.name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
items.summary: Tactile turns accessibility, OCR and visual evidence into explicit desktop targets with executable actions and verification cues. Its execution loop chooses semantic actions or coordinate fallbacks while retaining provenance for replay and diagnosis.

items.name: HyMobileAgent: Data-Environment Co-Scaling for Efficient GUI Agents
items.summary: Combines GUI perception data, instructional videos, real and simulated devices, and planning with reflection to develop a mobile agent.

items.name: Plover: Steering GUI Agents through Plan-Centric Interaction
items.summary: Plover exposes GUI-agent plans and replanning as persistent artifacts that users can inspect and edit during execution. Its planner–executor design supports localized correction through plan edits, language guidance and screenshot-grounded interventions, studied through failure repair and workflow scenarios.

items.name: SeerGuard: A Safety Framework for Mobile GUI Agents via World Model Prediction
items.summary: Uses instruction screening and a safety-augmented world model to assess likely consequences of mobile GUI actions before execution.

items.name: Just A Rather Very Intelligent Spoken Agent
items.summary: Introduces JarvisBench, a benchmark for spoken mediation during long-horizon agent workflows, measuring task collaboration and how users follow ongoing execution.

items.name: EvoGUI: An Evolution-Aware Benchmark for GUI State-Transition Understanding
items.summary: Introduces EvoGUI, which derives temporal ordering, inverse action/value prediction, and successor-discrimination probes from recorded GUI trajectories. Its web-derived benchmark isolates transition understanding from the other abilities involved in end-to-end task success.

items.name: Teach it to stop, not just to click
