items.summary: Studies verifier-guided repair of a 35B computer-use agent across five environments, examining variation across runs and data draws in done detection, GUI clicks, and field entry.

items.name: Sidekick: Designing Communication for Effective Multitasking with Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces Sidekick, a communication interface that uses ambient status cues, multimodal action summaries, and visual and verbal explanations of reasoning to help people monitor computer-use agents. A user study examines progress awareness, error traceability, and multitasking across background and foreground interaction.

items.name: SEE: Structure-aware Exploring & Exploiting for Long-horizon GUI Agent Trajectory Synthesis
items.summary: Introduces SEE, which first explores mobile interfaces to build a screen-and-element transition graph, then composes task trajectories through graph planning and controlled sampling. It studies coverage, loop avoidance, and transfer after training agents on the generated sequences.

items.name: Broken Gates: Re-evaluating Web Bot Defenses in the Age of LLM Agents
items.summary: Measures how autonomous LLM browser agents interact with commercial bot-management and anti-automation defenses on the web.

items.name: DocOps: A Verifiable Benchmark for Autonomous Agents in Complex Document Operations
items.summary: Introduces DocOps, a verifiable benchmark for agents handling complex digital-document workflows, with analysis of state tracking, semantic checks, and structural edits.

items.name: PersonaTrail: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents through Browsing Trails
items.summary: Introduces PersonaTrail, a benchmark for personalized web agents using browsing histories, and PACMem, a structured memory method for guiding navigation.

items.name: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
items.summary: OpenForgeRL connects stateful agent harnesses to reinforcement-learning infrastructure through a model-call recording proxy and isolated rollout containers. Its validation includes browser and computer-use agents, alongside tool-oriented agents, and examines how harness choice affects learned reliability.

items.name: Beyond Sequential Interaction: Benchmarking Parallel Execution and Coordination for GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces ParaGUIBench, with tasks and efficiency measurements for coordinated GUI agents operating separate desktop instances over a shared file system. Its ParaGUI planner-worker system decomposes tasks and dispatches concurrent subtasks for comparison with serial execution.

items.name: StepX-Edge: An On-Device UI Vision-Language Model via Architecture-Training-Deployment Co-Design
items.summary: Introduces StepX-Edge, an on-device UI vision-language model for screen understanding, OCR, question answering, and element grounding on mobile chips.

items.name: StateAct: Program State, before Pixels, for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces StateAct, a code-first computer-use harness that manipulates program state directly and delegates screenshot-and-click subgoals to a GUI agent. An independent completion gate checks saved outputs, while fresh subagents handle subgoals to limit accumulated context.

items.name: SeekJudge: A Practical Reward Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces SeekJudge, which iteratively searches and analyzes GUI trajectories to assess instruction fulfillment. The work combines dense judgment-data synthesis, a step-label benchmark, and reward-server scheduling to study accurate and practical reward feedback for agent training.

items.name: Scaling GUI Agents with Visual State Transitions
items.summary: Introduces State Transition Pretraining, which jointly learns to infer actions from GUI changes and predict future states from current screens and actions. Subsequent instruction-trajectory fine-tuning tests whether these representations transfer to desktop and mobile agent tasks.

items.name: Falsifiable Commitment Planning for Self-Correcting Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces FCPAgent, which attaches confirming and falsifying evidence to each skill-grounded plan step. A plan–test–repair loop checks actions and observations, then localizes contradictions so execution, skills, or plans can be revised at the appropriate level.

items.name: SafeFlow: Semantic Information-Flow Control for Blocking Malicious Propagation in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Introduces SafeFlow, a semantic information-flow defense for multi-agent delegation, evaluated on safety tasks that include harmful web-agent behavior.

items.name: Interactive Reward Agent: GUI Task Evaluation via Environment-State Verification
items.summary: Introduces an Interactive Reward Agent that proposes completion conditions and verifies them using system, application, and GUI tools after execution. GUI-RewardBench provides annotated desktop trajectories for evaluating these evidence-based judgments and their use in reinforcement learning.

items.name: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?
items.summary: Introduces Desktop-Delta Bench, an offline diagnostic of GUI transition understanding using temporal-ordering tasks and before/after action inference. It includes decoy observations to test whether models track the source and task relevance of screen changes.

items.name: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
items.summary: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a benchmark for long-horizon office-suite agent tasks with labor-time and price signals, plus rubric-based code verifiers.

items.name: Echoverse: Deep, Evolving Environments for Training Computer-Use Agents at Scale
items.summary: Introduces Echoverse, which compiles specifications into stateful applications with database-grounded graders and uses rollouts to improve both the environments and agent policies. It examines behavioral depth, targeted interface practice, and environment repair as sources of training value.

items.name: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
items.summary: Describes a foundation GUI agent with combined GUI and command-line actions, large-scale interaction infrastructure, and iterative environment and task generation.

items.name: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed
items.summary: Introduces MemHarness, which trains agents to critique and reconstruct retrieved experience before acting; WebShop is one of two evaluation environments.

items.name: How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Audits failure-scored computer-use trajectories to distinguish agent errors from broken tasks and evaluator false negatives. It organizes reliability issues across task construction, trajectory evidence, scoring, and reporting, then derives corresponding evaluation design practices.

items.name: Why Are GUI Agents Correct but Late? Decode on the Decision-Time Critical Path, Tested with Pre-Compiled Policy Trees
items.summary: Introduces Adaptive Anticipatory Policy Trees, which precompute guarded actions and deadlines during idle periods so transient GUI events can be handled without new text generation. Paired experiments examine when this prepared execution helps and when reactive control remains preferable.

items.name: Rethinking Inference-Time Scaling in Local Computer-Use Agents: Failure Modes and Compute Tradeoffs
items.summary: Examines inference-time scaling for local computer-use models by varying context, step budgets, decomposition, and parallel execution. OSWorld experiments track both task performance and changing failure modes, exposing cases where extra computation extends errors or adds coordination overhead.

items.name: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
items.summary: Introduces OSReward and its harder and multidimensional variants for assessing judgments of computer-use trajectories. It also releases a reasoning-annotated judgment corpus and trains reward models, examining reliability, leniency bias, and evaluation cost.

items.name: Alignment Is Local: A Paired Diagnostic for GUI Agents under User-Side Persuasion
items.summary: Presents a paired diagnostic of prompt guardrails in GUI agents under screen-grounded user persuasion, comparing single-turn probes with four-turn escalation.

items.name: MAGA: Multi-Platform Self-Fusion of GUI Agents via Structured Action Distillation
items.summary: MAGA distills specialized GUI agents into one policy by allocating supervision according to structured-action correctness. A training-only teacher hint supports fusion across mobile, web and desktop settings without changing student inputs.

items.name: From Monoliths to Swarms: A Study of Attack Surface Evolution in the Transition to Multi-Agent Web Systems
items.summary: Categorizes structural attack surfaces that emerge when single-agent browser systems are decomposed into multi-agent web workflows.

items.name: RMSWeb: Reflection, Failure-Mode Mining, and Salvage-DS for Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Introduces RMSWeb, a training recipe for web agents that uses reflection retries, failure-mode mining, and Salvage-DS reward and sampling methods for web actions.

items.name: LongHorizon-Harness: Advancing Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Tasks
items.summary: Introduces LongHorizon-Harness, which maintains verified task state outside an agent's execution context and audits subtasks; its evaluations include OSWorld~2.0.

items.name: Invisible Ink Threats: Adversarial Goals Behind Legitimate Tasks in Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces II-Bench for low-harm indirect prompt injections against computer-use agents and HITLCUA for testing them in virtual-machine and web environments with simulated user review.

items.name: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything
items.summary: Qwen-CUA operates through screenshots and keyboard/mouse events while compressing older visual history into reusable context blocks. Its report combines verifiable task generation, trajectory-based training and separate browser and Bash-augmented studies.

items.name: CUADebug: Diagnosing and Repairing Computer-Use Agent Failures
items.summary: CUADebug combines a failure taxonomy and human-annotated OSWorld failure trajectories with an agent that locates causal steps and proposes corrections from screenshots and action traces. It evaluates root-cause diagnosis separately from controlled task re-execution and failure recovery.

items.name: GUI-Lens: Coarse-to-Fine Cropping for GUI Grounding with General-Purpose VLMs
items.summary: GUI-Lens uses OCR and detected interface components as coordinate references while a general-purpose VLM selects progressively enlarged screenshot crops. Instruction-conditioned checks constrain the crop and click proposals before mapping the final location back to the original screen.

items.name: Screenshots or Tools? Eliciting Tool Use and Managing Multimodal Context in Hybrid GUI-MCP Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: This study separates tool-adoption behavior from task competence in hybrid GUI–MCP agents. It tests tool-use incentives and screenshot-history compression, showing that changed action preferences can coexist with unchanged held-out accuracy.

items.name: MissClick: Execution-Aware Adversarial Attacks on Coordinate Generation in GUI Grounding Models
items.summary: MissClick designs white-box attacks around the numerical effect of coordinate digits on executable GUI clicks. Separate untargeted displacement and targeted place-weighted objectives are evaluated across desktop, web and mobile grounding settings.

items.name: FocusMem: Factorizing Content, Readout, and Trust in Latent GUI Memory
items.summary: Introduces FocusMem, a latent memory interface for GUI agents that separates stored content, state-conditioned readout, and a gate for irrelevant retrieved experience.

items.name: LoginTrap: Uncovering Task-Agnostic Phishing-Style Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks against LLM-based Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces LoginTrap, a black-box indirect-injection evaluation in which attacker-controlled page context and login flows induce unauthorized authentication. It measures end-to-end private-data leakage across web-agent backbones, architectures and defenses.

items.name: "Allow" to Achieve, Over-Privileged Inadvertently: The Unintended Cost of Task-Completion-Driven Pop-up Decisions in Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: This permission-literacy study tests whether mobile GUI agents grant only task-necessary permissions. Controlled changes to task context and requester identity expose authorization biases and the trade-off between suppressing unnecessary and legitimate grants.

items.name: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: StepReflect predicts structured per-action reflections from transition specifications and paired visual evidence. The paper distinguishes offline transition-label accuracy from online task success when the reflection model is integrated into mobile agents.

items.name: Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay
items.summary: Introduces Activity Frames, a deterministic pipeline that turns captured screen activity into typed episodes for computer-use agent memory and routine replay.

items.name: AppDeltaWorld: Transition-Grounded Delta Code World Model for Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: AppDeltaWorld predicts executable code updates for the next mobile UI state, using transition-constrained retrieval and rendered visual assets. It evaluates reconstruction fidelity separately from policy training and adaptation using generated environments.

items.name: The Next Screenshot Knows: Gated Hindsight Distillation for Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: Gated Hindsight Distillation gives a teacher access to the next screenshot during training while the student sees only the available trajectory prefix. Distillation is applied when hindsight repairs a student failure, and the resulting policies are evaluated on Android tasks.

items.name: Routing Is Least Learnable Where It Is Most Valuable: Bounds on Representation Routing for Web Agents
items.summary: Measures the complementarity, cost and rerun variability of six browser observation modes on WebArena and VisualWebArena. Its routing experiments distinguish an oracle cost opportunity from policies that fail to robustly outperform a fixed observation mode.

items.name: WebGrader: Training LLMs for Web Development with Self-Evolving Programmatic Grader
items.summary: Introduces WebGrader, a programmatic grader for website generation that plans interaction flows, runs them in a live browser, and uses observed outcomes as RL rewards.

items.name: StepJack: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agent Safety Against Multi-Step Indirect Prompt Injection
items.summary: Introduces StepJack, a benchmark of indirect prompt injections that split an adversarial goal across pages on a computer-use agent's web navigation path.

items.name: WebRider: Persona-Conditioned Intent Controllers for Live-Web Assistance
items.summary: Introduces WebRider, a live-web agent that maintains intent contracts while carrying out guarded browser actions, and RiderBench for auditing those contracts across websites.

items.name: MemPrism: Task-Conditioned Relational Memory Views for Long-Horizon Agents
items.summary: Introduces MemPrism, which records prior interactions and builds task-conditioned relational memory views for decisions in long-horizon web-agent tasks.

items.name: SynChain: Inducing Computer-Use Agent Systems to Construct Their Own Attack Chains
items.summary: Introduces SynChain, an attack that induces persistent agents to create poisoned skills or memory entries, and CUAChain for evaluating later attack-chain activation.

items.name: AndroidReality: How Far Are Mobile Agents from the Real World?
items.summary: Extends AndroidWorld with controlled state, transition, and action perturbations to test mobile-agent robustness, and studies a training-free introspective recovery mechanism.

items.name: Back to the Future: A workbook time machine for spread sheet creation benchmarks
items.summary: Introduces the workbook time machine to create spreadsheet-object tasks and wtmbench to evaluate spreadsheet manipulation agents using different control interfaces.

items.name: CAP: A Scalable Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Site Browser Agents with Complex Actions and Perception
items.summary: CAP builds cross-site browser workflows by decomposing websites into operation and perception requirements and recomposing them into tasks. Its judge-based evaluation diagnoses complex interactions and visual-perception failures across real websites.

items.name: Not an A11y: How Android Accessibility Exposes Mobile AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injection
items.summary: Demonstrates that unsanitized Android accessibility tree metadata exposes mobile GUI agents to stealthy indirect prompt injection attacks.

items.name: Software Engineering for and with GUI Agent
items.summary: Surveys 336 GUI-agent papers through a software engineering lens, covering architectures, evaluation, and lifecycle concerns in mobile and web settings.

items.name: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
items.summary: This framework separates frozen-model instruction expansion from a trained layout-aware matcher that localizes GUI elements without coordinate regression. Binary text/icon supervision supports the matcher, with evaluations on GUI grounding and Mind2Web element-selection tasks.

items.name: LookAgain: Closed-Loop GUI Grounding with Visually Grounded Reflection
items.summary: LookAgain treats a GUI coordinate as a revisable hypothesis, rendering its marker and a local screenshot patch before confirmation. Reflective supervised trajectories provide a cold start, followed by GRPO using terminal grounding correctness.

items.name: Navigation Alone Is Not Enough: Evaluating Explanatory Assistive UI Agents
items.summary: Introduces NeXUI, an assistive UI-agent benchmark that evaluates navigation together with interface-grounded explanations and user oversight in recorded interface states.

items.name: DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?
items.summary: DSAgentBench evaluates end-to-end data-science workflows spanning analysis, modeling and visualization inside a real desktop environment. Task evaluators check produced analytical and visual artifacts, while the released interface supports screenshot or accessibility observations and GUI actions.

items.name: SkillLens: Visual Skill Cards for Retrieval-Augmented GUI Action Prediction and On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: Introduces SkillLens visual skill cards for retrieved GUI action guidance and CardDistill for training an action-prediction student that runs without retrieval on website tasks.

items.name: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.summary: Introduces a Test-Time Self-Evolving framework for GUI grounding that explores unseen interfaces, reflects on predicted coordinates, and distills those reflections into the model.

items.name: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation
items.summary: MobileJudgeBench compares completion judges against human labels on mobile-agent trajectories. It studies screenshot-sampling baselines, model-dependent error profiles and how judge quality relates to agent rankings and reinforcement-learning rewards.

items.name: CoAdapt-GUI: Joint Workflow Context and Policy Adaptation for Unseen GUI Applications
items.summary: Introduces CoAdapt-GUI, which adapts workflow context and policy from a mobile GUI agent's own rollouts and rewards when it encounters unseen applications.

items.name: SynWeaver: Website-Prior Task and Trajectory Co-Synthesis for Web Agents
items.summary: SynWeaver explores a website to build a map of page states and executable interactions, then learns website priors for task proposals. Joint task/trajectory synthesis revises inconsistent pairs and verifies or repairs the resulting supervision.

items.name: LegacyWorld: Atomicity-Aware Evaluation of GUI Agents for Legacy Workflows
items.summary: LegacyWorld evaluates Windows GUI workflows under an atomicity criterion: finish correctly or fail without persistent unintended changes. It compares expert prompts with prompts derived from recorded golden paths and separates useful completion, safe failure and non-atomic side effects.

items.name: Act2Intention: A Benchmark For Developing Active Mobile Agents Through Inferring User Intention from GUI Actions
items.summary: Introduces intention understanding, prediction, and confirmed execution tasks over mobile GUI trajectories, with a proactive agent combining personalized intention models and experience-guided actions.

items.name: StateM: Reaching 95.3% Raw Accuracy, or a \$15 Frontier Run, on Terminal-Bench 2.1 via Harness Scaling
items.summary: Introduces StateM, a stateful runtime with checked transitions and reusable runbooks for long-horizon agents; its reported evaluations use terminal and business tasks.

items.name: UI-Mate: Advancing Open-Weight Foundation GUI Agents with In-Context Demonstrations
items.summary: Combines environment-grounded training with demonstration-conditioned workflows, and introduces OSWorkerBench for extended office-task evaluation.

items.name: Agentic ESOpt: Fine-Tuning Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Minimal GPU Requirements
items.summary: Introduces Agentic ESOpt, an evolution-strategies fine-tuning framework for long-horizon agents, evaluated on WebArena-Lite web tasks and automatic heuristic design.

items.name: Wuying-Browser-Agent: Real-World Centric Fundamental Long-Horizon Browser Agents
items.summary: Combines a browser execution framework, recovery-oriented supervision, and online reinforcement learning, with a bilingual live-web task benchmark.

items.name: MobileWorldSafety: Benchmarking GUI Agent Safety Against Environmental Injection Attacks in Android Apps
items.summary: Evaluates environmental injection risks in Android tasks using programmatic risk checks and model-based adjudication of ambiguous cases.

items.name: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: ComponentBench evaluates short interactions with canonical web UI components using verified tasks and matched human reference trajectories. Its diagnostic pipeline compares observation/action representations and analyzes structural difficulty, failure patterns and interaction efficiency.

items.name: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
items.summary: Task Model Induction disentangles concurrent activities in screenshot and mouse/keyboard traces, then constructs hierarchical goals and procedural control flow for each task. Evaluation tests reconstruction of observed execution and reuse of derived skills on held-out tasks.

items.name: Towards Faithful Simulation of Human Shopping Behavior
items.summary: Presents RecVerse, a screenshot-based shopping simulation agent with hierarchical memory and trajectory-level RL, alongside USB, an interactive e-commerce GUI trajectory dataset.

items.name: Automated Trajectory Evaluation for Mobile Agents via Step-Level Consequence Reasoning and Aggregation
items.summary: Introduces CRATE, a step-level visual judge for mobile-agent trajectories, and CRATE-S for assessing operational safety from action-conditioned state changes.

items.name: Lexical Coupling in GUI Element Grounding: Sentence Embeddings Track Labels across Mobile and Web
items.summary: Studies whether text-embedding GUI grounding scores reflect semantic matching or recovery of visible labels. Same-screen ranking comparisons with lexical baselines expose differences between deployable fusion, oracle selection, and performance on label-poor targets.

items.name: Beyond Success and Failure: Length-Aware Contrastive Learning for GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces LACL-GUI, a contrastive learning objective that distinguishes trajectory quality within both successful and failed GUI executions. It favors concise successes and uses divergence from successful trajectories to differentiate failures during policy optimization.

items.name: GUI-Primitives: Diagnosing Spatial Reasoning Failures in Vision-Language GUI Grounding
items.summary: Introduces GUI-Primitives, a paired-instruction benchmark that changes a spatial relation while holding the screenshot and anchor fixed. Its diagnostics separate failure to localize either candidate from failure to choose the candidate satisfying the relation.

items.name: Training Needs Trustworthy Worlds: Verified Synthetic Web Environments for Agent Learning
items.summary: Builds synthetic websites with verified navigation, backend state, and feasible tasks to provide reliable supervision for web-agent training.

items.name: Spine-Branch Coordination for Multi-agent Computer Use
items.summary: Introduces Spine-Branch Coordination, which assigns a main task flow to one virtual-machine state and uses parallel branch machines to gather information for computer-use agents.

items.name: ClawProBench: Trace-Aware Evaluation of AI Agents with Runtime Coverage and Frozen Workplace-Style Holdouts
items.summary: Introduces ClawProBench, a trace-aware benchmark for agents on OpenClaw that scores workspace and native-runtime tasks using execution traces, safety checks, and process quality.

items.name: CausalCache: Conditional High-Fidelity Restoration for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces CausalCache, which selects archived screenshots to restore alongside text summaries under a fixed visual-memory budget. A history-gated adapter processes restored images, with evaluation distinguishing standard step limits from longer-horizon and mobile-transfer settings.

items.name: GSAR: Goal-State-Anchor Rewards for Mobile GUI Agents with Self-Evolving Data Synthesis
items.summary: Introduces GSAR, which synthesizes GUI tasks and successful goal states, then annotates task-relevant interface elements as reward anchors. These anchors support offline trajectory verification and online policy training.

items.name: Reflection with Action-Induced Visual Differences for Desktop GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces Evidence-First Reflection, which separates extraction of action-induced screen changes from judgment of whether an operation achieved its objective. It filters visual differences into relevant evidence before a desktop agent’s reflector decides how execution should continue.

items.name: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents
items.summary: Proposes WebMCP-Phalanx, a browser-integrated runtime that binds page-exposed tools to their registering principals and separates content inspection from privileged invocation. It studies lifecycle and prompt-injection attacks, including a timing bypass that motivates validating all visible metadata before tool use.

items.name: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies? AnTrap: Evaluating Agents in Dynamic Adversarial Environments
items.summary: Introduces AnTrap, which injects task-solvable runtime anomalies into Android GUI-agent trajectories using a layered failure taxonomy. It compares model robustness and adversarial reinforcement learning to distinguish recoverable interface traps from persistent contextual failures.

items.name: Task-Adaptive Rubrics for GUI Reward Modeling
items.summary: Introduces AdaptRubric, which retrieves reusable criteria for a GUI task family and then generates instruction-specific checks for concrete values and constraints. It evaluates these adaptive rubrics in offline reward assessment and online agent optimization.

items.name: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
items.summary: Introduces BrowserForge, which combines broad website sourcing, parallel browser sandboxes, and task-proposer/solver interaction to collect verified web trajectories. The pipeline uses page structure during synthesis but trains a policy that acts from screenshots.

items.name: MCP-Driven Accessibility Tree Standardization for AI-Powered Screen Reader Agents
items.summary: Proposes an MCP architecture that presents accessibility trees from Windows, macOS, Android, and web frameworks in a common form for LLM assistive agents interacting with GUIs.

items.name: From Blind Edits to Verified Repair: Building Trustworthy User-Side LLM Agents for Web Accessibility
items.summary: Builds a local browser-extension agent that generates and verifies additive CSS repairs for WCAG web accessibility violations.

items.name: LocalLSTC: A Long Short-Term Control Architecture for Locally Deployed GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces LocalLSTC, a training-free control architecture that maintains persistent task state and uses it to form short execution commitments. Outcomes feed back into that state for progress checks, recovery, and termination in locally deployed desktop agents.

items.name: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games
items.summary: Introduces GameWAM, a model for native game play and GUI control that predicts future visuals and keyboard-mouse actions from synchronized gameplay and GUI trajectories.

items.name: ADeptS-Bench: Measuring the Trustworthiness of Computer Use Agents Across Devices
items.summary: Evaluates interface-embedded threats and whether computer-use agents seek clarification when mobile or desktop instructions are ambiguous.

items.name: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions
items.summary: ASIL exposes application state as structured JSON and provides code-executable semantic actions. Its application benchmark compares this interface with screenshot control and application-native APIs, and studies supervised and reinforcement learning on the structured interface.

items.name: Benchmarking General Mobile Assistants in Challenging Real-World Scenarios
items.summary: Introduces GMA, a benchmark of 300 mobile-assistant tasks across seven applications, and studies how agent context retention and state tracking affect complex workflows.

items.name: WM-R1: Training GUI Agents to Reason and leverage World Models with Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Uses learned world models for mobile-agent training rollouts and for reasoning about the consequences of candidate GUI actions.

items.name: CURA: Certified Runtime Alarms for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces CURA, a telemetry-based runtime monitor that turns computer-use trajectories into sequential failure alarms and can trigger mid-task oversight. Its certificate controls false alarms, while the study separately reports detection performance and limits of retrospective monitoring.

items.name: Iron: Intent-Aligned and Retrospective Dual Learning Framework for Enhancing Generalist Virtual Agents
items.summary: Introduces Iron, a GUI-agent training framework that aligns low-level actions with high-level intent using cycle-consistency rewards. It also repurposes failed trajectories through hindsight reconstruction and evaluates transfer to other digital tasks.

items.name: Learning Simple Test-Time Environments for LLM Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces Test-Time Environment Decomposition, which uses trial interaction to break complex web observations into simpler modules. A label-free adaptation procedure learns from these sub-environments and studies whether their gains compose in full web tasks.

items.name: A Systematic Survey of Agentic Skills: Architecture, Lifecycle, and Security
items.summary: Surveys modular agentic skill architectures, skill lifecycles, and security risks in autonomous tool- and interface-using agents.

items.name: ActReal: System-Level Mobile Agents Challenge Mobile Automation Detection
items.summary: Introduces ActReal, which translates semantic mobile-agent actions into coordinated touch and sensor signals to study automation-detection weaknesses. It evaluates detectors that observe touch events alone or together with inertial measurements under a privileged executor threat model.

items.name: SIR: Self-improving Red-teaming for Compute Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces SIR, which iteratively refines a reusable library of prompt-injection strategies from failed computer-use attack trajectories. Its evaluation uses deterministic system-state checks and counts attacks only when the adversarial objective and legitimate task both complete.

items.name: WebWorld: The Browser as a World Model for Self-Improving Web Code
items.summary: Uses typed browser interaction contracts to accept web-code improvements only when target progress and previously verified capabilities are preserved. Accepted transitions supply self-improvement data.

items.name: UI-Venus-2 Technical Report
items.summary: Describes a GUI foundation agent trained through expanded environments, function-grounded tasks, and trajectory verification with safety-aware execution mechanisms.

items.name: GUI-CC: Benchmarking Contextual Consistency of GUI World Models as Agent Environments
items.summary: Introduces GUI-CC, a benchmark for assessing GUI world models as multi-step agent environments. Separate reference-action and agent-loop tracks test whether generated screens preserve context, plausible transitions, and task progress throughout interaction.

items.name: Are We There Yet? Assessing Computer-Use Agents for Blind Users' Accessible Interaction with Desktop Applications
items.summary: A diary study deploys the screen-reader-accessible OLLA computer-use prototype with blind users across desktop applications. Recorded commands and interaction traces support model comparisons and analysis of grounding, planning, constraint tracking and termination failures.

items.name: Monitoring Web Agents Without Internal Signals: Observable Trajectories and Key-Step Supervision
items.summary: Predicts web-agent failure risk from observable trajectory prefixes using cross-step behavior and black-box consistency queries. Key-step labels preserve valid early prefixes of failed runs, and evaluation tests early intervention and transfer across website categories.

items.name: OmegaUse-SOP: SOP Engineering for Professional Computer Use from Human Demonstrations
items.summary: OmegaUse-SOP converts expert GUI demonstrations into configurable procedures and refines them with domain rules and human input. It records, abstracts, grounds and verifies live execution, with a case study of photovoltaic simulation workflows in PVsyst 7.2.

items.name: WiP: Characterizing and Defending Against Mobile-Agent-Driven MFA Automation
items.summary: Studies how mobile automation can combine authentication factors within one agent environment and evaluates motion sensing as a user-presence signal.

items.name: Efficient GUI Agents: A Systems Survey of Observation, Memory, Action, and Runtime Optimization
items.summary: Surveys GUI-agent efficiency beyond task success: observation, context and memory, action, and planner or runtime cost.

items.name: CA-OPD: Confidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Structured Visual Prediction
items.summary: Introduces CA-OPD, a confidence-guided distillation method for visual prediction, evaluated on GUI grounding and optical character recognition benchmarks.

items.name: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
items.summary: Trains discriminative web world models to distinguish the true next state from outcomes of alternative actions. Branching web trajectories support training, followed by tests of predicted-state matching, process-reward action ranking and end-to-end WebArena-Lite selection.

items.name: Tail-Likelihood Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Introduces Tail-Likelihood Reinforcement Learning (TailRL), an RL objective that favors rare high-reward rollouts; GUI grounding is one of several evaluation tasks.

items.name: Do GUI Agents Know When Not to Act? Enabling Conflict-Aware Termination for Multimodal GUI Agents
items.summary: CONFLICTGUI evaluates termination under instruction conflicts and mismatches between instructions and interface context. CONFLICTGUARD couples feasibility checks with conditional action modulation to reduce unnecessary execution while tracking normal-task behavior.

items.name: ElderBench: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents for Older Adults
items.summary: ElderBench evaluates mobile GUI agents on smartphone requests elicited from older adults, including indirect and underspecified language. Online and offline tests, instruction normalization and linguistic analyses examine how these request patterns contribute to failures.

items.name: From Interaction Traces to Persistent Skills: Online Evolution for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: An online skill-evolution framework turns GUI interaction traces and evaluator feedback into a versioned library of reusable procedures without updating model parameters. Controlled OSWorld comparisons examine both the benefits of shared procedural memory and its domain-dependent instability under repeated revision.

items.name: CUA-Universe: A Scalable and Dynamic Environment for Hybrid GUI+CLI Agents
items.summary: Turns desktop applications into reproducible GUI-and-CLI environments and generates verified hybrid trajectories for agent post-training.

items.name: SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction
items.summary: Introduces SCAFFOLD, which extracts executable skills from web trajectories, composes them into a hierarchy, and compresses redundant skills through behavioral checks. It periodically distills skill-guided trajectories into the policy and studies repeated improvement across web benchmarks.

items.name: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents
items.summary: Proposes an online teaching framework that decides which web-agent episodes warrant a stronger teacher and which trajectory turns merit training. A solvability gate and score-guided trimming aim to preserve first-attempt performance while reducing teaching and training costs.

items.name: Beyond the Verdict: Evidence-Aligned Evaluation of Visual Prompt-Injection Guardrails
items.summary: Introduces Mind2Web-Injection, a benchmark for evaluating web-agent guardrail decisions on instruction-screenshot pairs using evidence boxes and image-side counterfactuals.

items.name: OmniStepBench: Deployment-Aware Agent Evaluation across Modalities and Task Complexity
items.summary: Introduces OmniStepBench, a shared-environment benchmark for evaluating multimodal agents on multi-step tasks, tool use, and delivered artifacts under one scoring protocol.

items.name: Selective Knowledge Control for Continual GUI Agent Learning over Application Streams
items.summary: Introduces activation-conditioned gradient control for GUI agents learning successive applications. It protects inactive application-specific neurons, constrains updates to shared neurons, and accumulates a compact historical state to balance adaptation with retention.

items.name: Improving Proficiency and Efficiency of Android GUI Agents via Self-Generating Tool Actions
items.summary: DroidTool generates application-state tools through proposal, implementation, testing and repair. Relational tests connect the tools’ preconditions and effects, and the resulting tools are evaluated as additions to Android GUI agents.

items.name: FinCUABuild: Can Agents Build Reliable Benchmarks for Dynamic Financial Computer Use?
items.summary: Introduces FinCUABuildBench for assessing financial computer-use task construction and FinCUABuildAgent for generating tasks, environments, and validators.

items.name: APPSim-Bench: Bridging Real-world Apps and Reproducible Evaluation for Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces controlled simulated mobile apps with deterministic backend data and outcome checks for reproducible evaluation of realistic interactions.

items.name: AgentHijack: Visual Patch Attacks on Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: AgentHijack evaluates whether visual patch effects propagate from screenshots through model outputs and action parsing into real environment changes. Its controlled web-page experiments distinguish intermediate attack signals from verified end-to-end consequences.

items.name: GraphDroid: Asynchronous LLM-Based Mobile App GUI Testing via History-Aware Exploration and Hybrid Intent Fulfillment
items.summary: GraphDroid combines clustered memory of visited GUI states with asynchronous test-intent generation. A hybrid executor reserves LLM calls for complex intents and uses heuristics for simpler ones, evaluated through Android app coverage, bug discovery and crash detection.

items.name: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
items.summary: TRACE orders screenshot evidence for monotonic visual-token reduction using layout priors, instruction relevance and feature novelty. Spatial token reserves and incremental KV contraction aim to preserve useful evidence for future GUI targets without repeatedly encoding retired frames.

items.name: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
items.summary: JarvisGUI composes typed input-output task transformations into dynamic workflows spanning Android, Windows and Ubuntu devices. Its virtual-environment benchmark tests transfer of intermediate results, shared state and cross-device dependencies.

items.name: BlueLM-GUI Technical Report: A Real-Device-Centric Flywheel for Self-Improving Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: Describes a mobile-agent training pipeline centered on real-device rollouts, recovery of useful supervision from failures, and evolving evaluation tasks.

items.name: VRL-Bench: Benchmarking agents on computer control tasks under finite trial budgets
items.summary: Introduces VRL-Bench to compare trial-and-error learning for computer-control agents under limited attempts, and VEX² to schedule exploration and exploitation.

items.name: LLaDA-UI: Bringing Block-wise Diffusion to Vision-Language GUI Agents
items.summary: LLaDA-UI adapts block-wise diffusion generation to a vision-language GUI agent through multimodal pretraining and GUI supervised fine-tuning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across multiple platform settings.

items.name: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents
items.summary: OdoBot builds a model of web-application behavior from successful task demonstrations and uses it to guide task execution. Its Canvas LMS evaluation compares token use and completion with existing web agents.

items.name: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents
items.summary: AutoTailor compiles web trajectories into reusable browser-automation APIs, then filters and dynamically revises the capability inventory. WebArena experiments distinguish API-only operation from an agent that can fall back to ordinary reasoning and browser actions.

items.name: PriMobiBench: Characterizing Visual Privacy Leakage in VLM-Driven Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: PriMobiBench evaluates direct privacy leakage and user profiling from mobile GUI screenshot trajectories, supported by the MobiLeak trace dataset. It also tests masking sensitive, task-irrelevant interface elements before cloud processing and measures the resulting privacy and utility trade-off.

items.name: CoArena: Evaluating Computer-Use and Multi-Agent Systems in Real Time
items.summary: Introduces CoArena, an evaluation method where user tasks run concurrently in sandboxed desktops and blind pairwise judgments update a public leaderboard.

items.name: Learning from Reliable Negatives: Confidence-Anchored Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Grounding
items.summary: Confidence-Anchored Learning uses coordinate-token confidence to filter pseudo-supervision for GUI grounding. Its negative-only variant performs label-free test-time updates to reduce reliance on potentially incorrect positive examples.

items.name: RSIAgent: Autonomous Exploration for Recursive Self-improvement in New Environments
items.summary: Introduces RSIAgent, a training-free framework that explores unfamiliar digital interfaces, stores environment-specific action knowledge, and reuses that memory for later tasks.

items.name: AnchorGUI: Asymmetric Memory for Dual-Scale Learning in GUI Navigation
items.summary: AnchorGUI compares expected and observed UI transitions and selectively retains screenshots when they disagree. This asymmetric memory supports immediate correction and focuses cross-attempt experience distillation on likely failure steps.

items.name: CADWorld: Computer-Use Benchmark for Long-Horizon Computer-Aided Design
items.summary: CADWorld evaluates screenshot-and-GUI agents on long FreeCAD workflows, from modeling and assembly to manufacturing and simulation. Executable checks inspect saved engineering artifacts for geometry, constraints, construction structure and downstream state.

items.name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
items.summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.

items.name: When Agents See Differently: Exposing UI Desynchronization Threats in Mobile Agents
items.summary: Investigates mismatches between what humans see on a mobile display and what agents receive through screenshots or accessibility metadata. An automated evaluation framework embeds instruction-agnostic perturbations into functional APK clones and compares static and dynamic agent deviations with human noticeability.

items.name: RiskChainBench: A Benchmark for Obfuscated Platform Message Restoration and Evidence-Grounded Web Investigation
items.summary: Introduces RiskChainBench, pairing obfuscated-message restoration with web-agent investigation of linked sites in labeled local web environments.

items.name: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
items.summary: EvoSkill-GUI revises reusable skill files from execution feedback through an executor–critic loop. It studies how training-free updates to localization, recovery and procedure information help subsequent mobile and desktop tasks.

items.name: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software
items.summary: ERPBench evaluates screenshot-only agents in enterprise software using database values to check the business records produced by their actions. It pairs these state-based checks with a harness for human approval and analyzes cases where visible completion masks incorrect persisted data.

items.name: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents
items.summary: Presents the Verifiable Action Card (VAC), a browser approval mechanism that derives confirmations from pending actions and binds user approval to execution.

items.name: RankGround: Efficient High-Resolution GUI Grounding via Lightweight Reranker-Guided Crop Selection
items.summary: RankGround trains a lightweight reranker to select a promising screenshot crop before one VLM localization call. Ranking supervision uses containment and boundary-aware augmentation, with pointwise and listwise training stages.

items.name: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces
items.summary: Presents Affora, a design system with reusable components and executable checks for interfaces used by computer-use agents, informed by studies of components and visual variation.

items.name: EconSkills: Studying Skill Transfer and Retrieval for Web Agents on Live Economic Data
items.summary: EconSkills converts verified economic-data browsing traces into parameterized procedures with navigation, verification and recovery guidance. Its evaluation separates known-skill transfer from library retrieval, exposing the limits of approximate matches to new tasks.

items.name: A Dual-Process Perspective on Nudge Susceptibility in LLM-Based GUI Agents
items.summary: Studies how automatic defaults and reflective social-influence cues affect GUI-agent shopping decisions under different reasoning configurations. A randomized simulated-shopping experiment finds that reasoning changes the type of susceptibility.

items.name: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: RecreationWorld gives hybrid agents running reference applications to explore and recreate using native GUI controls and coding tools. Its multi-platform benchmark checks interaction-dependent behavior with programmatic and visual assertions, while trajectory-training transfer is evaluated separately.

items.name: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments
items.summary: MintAct trains a visual-agent family for grounding, navigation and tool use across mobile, desktop and web environments. Its shared infrastructure supports trajectory collection and asynchronous online RL while controlling cross-domain sampling and off-policy drift.

items.name: Beyond Task Completion: Training Capable and Safe Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces SCOPE, which trains computer-use agents on ordinary task demonstrations, safe continuations around hazards, and explicit refusals. Its SCOPE-Gen pipeline pairs verifiable tasks with environmental-risk variants to support joint capability and safety training.

items.name: Seeing Through Conflicts: Improving Instruction Hierarchy Alignment in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Studies reinforcement learning for vision-language models facing conflicting instructions across text and images, including evaluation on web-agent safety tasks.

items.name: MATE: Policy-Aware Security Auditing for Mobile Agents via Synthesis-Driven Trajectory Learning
items.summary: Introduces MATE, a policy-conditioned auditor for mobile-agent trajectories, and MATEBench for evaluating whether those trajectories violate app security policies.

items.name: How Many Pixels Is a Digit Worth? Place-Aware Coordinate Entropy for GUI Agent Confidence Estimation
items.summary: PACE weights coordinate-digit entropy by place value to estimate confidence in GUI clicks from one forward pass. It evaluates correctness ranking and selective accuracy against repeated-sampling alternatives on ScreenSpot-Pro and ScreenSpot-v2.

items.name: OSWorld-Pro: Process-based Evaluation for Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Adds annotated intermediate subgoals to computer-use tasks and uses process-oriented evaluation to identify action and progress failures.

items.name: Towards Omni-dimensional GUI Agent Navigation with Masked Trajectory Prediction
items.summary: MaP unifies GUI-navigation objectives by masking and predicting components of multi-turn trajectories. Role-aware adapters address heterogeneous training data, and evaluations compare the approach with direct task-mixture training across navigation benchmarks.

items.name: CAVEAT: Towards Robust Computer-Use Agents in Incentive-Misaligned Environments
items.summary: Introduces CAVEAT, a controlled marketplace benchmark for testing whether delegated agents preserve user objectives when interfaces favor other outcomes. It diagnoses decision failures and studies harness interventions and targeted training to improve resistance to marketplace steering.

items.name: Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents
items.summary: GUI-SD-v2 extends on-policy self-distillation from grounding to multi-turn GUI interaction. It first strengthens responses to privileged guidance, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory support for later actions.

items.name: Guides That Cause Actions: An Offline Study of Guide-Action Mutual Reinforcement in Multimodal Web Agents
items.summary: WebMRE pairs guidance sentences with grounded actions in an offline benchmark derived from successful WebArena traces. Controlled decoding-prefix interventions test how guide content affects action selection, while separating offline prediction metrics from live browser task success.

items.name: Invisible in Space, Visible in Time: Motion Vision CAPTCHA against GUI Agents
items.summary: MVCAP-Bench tests live browser CAPTCHAs whose foreground meaning emerges through motion against dynamic backgrounds. A foreground-only control separates temporal camouflage difficulty from answer format and browser interaction.

items.name: Improving LLM-based Autonomous Web Agents with Filtering
items.summary: Trains HTML-element relevance filters on Mind2Web trajectories and transfers them to WebArena to reduce irrelevant browser context. It also evaluates a zero-shot ColBERT retriever and documents baseline web-agent failure modes.

items.name: Qwen-Planner-Agent: A Closed-Loop AI-for-AI Framework for Real-World Mobile Planner Agents
items.summary: Trains a mobile planner with supervised trajectories and competence-adaptive RL, then couples typed tool execution with memory, skills and offline model-harness refinement.

items.name: Jev-Mobile: Jev as an Executor for Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: Separates occasional visual-language planning from frequent lightweight action selection over an accessibility-tree-based action space.

items.name: The Hard Part Comes After Search: Benchmarking Web Agents on Synthesizing, Organizing, and Displaying Knowledge
items.summary: KNOWS benchmarks browser workflows that retrieve and synthesize information into documents, presentations and spreadsheets. Task-specific evaluators combine deterministic checks with model judgments, distinguishing partial progress from usable end-to-end artifact completion.

items.name: From Tapping to Hopping: Augmenting Mobile GUI Agents with App-Native Deeplinks
items.summary: GUI-Hopper combines verified Android deeplinks with GUI actions, using landing-screen descriptions, hybrid trajectory training and reinforcement learning to select navigation shortcuts and recover through GUI control.

items.name: OpenVAM: Open-World Visual Attention Modeling with VLMs
items.summary: Combines dense saliency prediction with explanations of attended elements, including webpage layouts; evaluates human-attention agreement and textual rationales on static inputs.

items.name: CaptchaArena: A Large-Scale, Fine-Grained Dataset for Training Computer-Use Agents on Interactive CAPTCHAs
items.summary: Introduces CaptchaArena, a dataset of execution-verified interactive CAPTCHA solutions with screenshot–action trajectories, reasoning annotations, and pixel masks for irregular targets. The work trains a single policy across CAPTCHA types using supervised learning followed by verifier-reward reinforcement learning.

items.name: ScreenHaystack: Finding Blind Zones in GUI Grounding
items.summary: Moves controlled target icons across high-resolution interfaces to diagnose spatial blind zones in grounding models and study targeted augmentation.

items.name: REBASE: Device-Cloud Experience Coherence for GUI Agents Across App Updates
items.summary: Introduces REBASE, a device–cloud protocol for repairing cached GUI experience after app updates. It combines cloud replay, device-side step verification, and progressively richer failure reports to produce repairs tied to application versions.

items.name: PastForward: Faster On-Device GUI Agents via Computational Experience Reuse
items.summary: Introduces PastForward, which reuses earlier output sequences as verified decoding proposals and starts future action computation from predicted GUI transitions. Screen checks determine whether speculative computation and cached model states can be retained.

items.name: From Trajectories to Grounded Preferences: Process Preference Synthesis via Interaction Element Graphs for Web PRMs
items.summary: Introduces SURFPRM, which turns web demonstrations into an interaction-element graph for synthesizing grounded negative actions. Its contrastive preference data trains process reward models to distinguish plausible on-page alternatives and guide downstream trajectory search.

items.name: DashAct: A Progressive Diagnostic Benchmark for GUI Agents in Interactive Dashboard Analysis
items.summary: Diagnoses dashboard-agent failures by progressively restoring interaction context, next-action support, and visual target information within the same task.

items.name: Learning from Others, Acting for You: Cross-User Memory Sharing for LLM Agents
items.summary: ShareMem consolidates reusable experience across users while keeping preference retrieval user-bound; its web evaluation predicts target elements and actions on recorded Mind2Web states.

items.name: CUA-SWE: When Computer-Use Agents Meet Visual Software Engineering
items.summary: Introduces CUA-SWE, a benchmark and execution environment that combines code changes with graphical interaction and visual inspection of running software. Task-specific tests verify repairs and changes whose required information may be available only through the application interface.

items.name: The GUI Is Not the State: Diagnosing State Aliasing in GUI World Models
items.summary: Introduces StateAliasBench to isolate GUI world-model ambiguities in which matching visible screens and actions can lead to different futures. It augments frozen world models with structured state recovered from interaction history and evaluates the effect on prediction and agent execution.

items.name: CUA-Sandbox: Efficient Environments for Computer-Use Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Introduces CUA-Sandbox, which separates each rollout’s mutable state from shared initialized software runtimes. State-scoped execution and transactional resets or branches aim to reduce training-environment costs while retaining original interfaces and evaluators.

items.name: AgentTell: Behavioural Side-Channel Leakage in Browser-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces AgentTell, a benchmark for privacy leakage through browser actions after an agent learns a private fact on another website. It examines whether agents choose revealing options despite nondisclosure instructions and whether their final reports accurately describe that behavior.

items.name: ORBIT: A Framework for Multi-Agent Safety and Security Evaluations
items.summary: Inspect-based framework that varies multi-agent roles, communication, attacks and defenses, with BrowserGym and virtual-desktop GUI adapters alongside coding and other tool scenarios.

items.name: Relevance Does Not Imply Applicability: Experience Activation for Personal GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces ExpActivator, which matches the current GUI state to relevant historical states before supplying past actions as guidance. A separate activation rule decides whether a recurring user intent is warranted by the current time and situation or should be withheld.

items.name: Probe to Act: Elevating Browser-Use Agent via Active Visual Probing
items.summary: Introduces Probe to Act, which lets browser agents request visual evidence linking DOM handles and screen regions before committing an operation. It retains selected interaction evidence as memory and studies both prompted use and distillation into open models.

items.name: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions
items.summary: Introduces GUITAR, which groups visually different screens into functional states and analyzes agent failures over a state-transition graph. It uses the resulting bottlenecks to diagnose recurring mobile and web errors and evaluate targeted guidance.

items.name: Same Tasks, Different Apps: Why Mobile GUI Agents Fail to Generalize?
items.summary: Introduces AnyAppBench, a live Android benchmark that holds user goals fixed while changing the application used to achieve them. It combines category-controlled task pairs with failure annotations to distinguish task understanding from application-specific execution skill.

items.name: One Rollout Is All You Get: Fully Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Agents
items.summary: Defines a test-time adaptation setting with one counted attempt per arriving GUI task and no ground-truth feedback. Its SOLO method filters or relabels completed episodes, then updates a small adapter from a short window of the agent’s own experience.

items.name: LongPuzzleBench: Evaluating GUI Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Puzzles
items.summary: LongPuzzleBench evaluates coherent long-horizon planning on persistent visual puzzle boards through native GUI actions. It compares GUI-only and code-assisted agents and uses controlled hints and memory diagnostics to examine decisions that preserve or eliminate future solutions.

items.name: Before Acting, Change the State: Prospective State Intervention for Web Agents under Deceptive Interfaces
items.summary: Introduces Veer, a runtime defense that changes task-relevant web state when an otherwise valid proposed action would produce an unauthorized consequence. It plans a prospective intervention and grounds and verifies its execution before the base agent continues.

items.name: WebPageBench: Event-Level Verification and Controlled UI-Variant Generation for Web Agents
items.summary: Verifies web tasks through typed interface events and generates controlled UI variations while preserving instructions and success conditions.

items.name: PhoneCLI: From App Interfaces to Callable Commands for Mobile Agents
items.summary: Introduces PhoneCLI, which explores mobile app interfaces and compiles navigation paths into reusable commands without internal app APIs or instrumentation. At execution time it verifies compiled paths and falls back to a visual agent for open-ended interaction or failed navigation.

items.name: SPECTRA: On-Device Cognitive Perturbation and Trajectory Analysis for Autonomous Edge-Cloud GUI Grounding
items.summary: Introduces SPECTRA, an edge-cloud GUI grounding framework that uses visual perturbations and trajectory analysis to decide when to request a cloud model.

items.name: Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions
items.summary: BreakingWeb pairs solvable browser tasks with controlled environment interventions that preserve the goal, target and backend success criterion. The paired evaluations isolate robustness failures, including agents declaring completion without the required state change.

items.name: Structured Interaction, Visual Localization, and Robust Execution for Complex Web Tasks: A Technical Report on the WebRetriever Challenge
items.summary: Describes a WebRetriever agent that combines semantic webpage operations with visual localization when structured representations are insufficient. Hierarchical context management and fault-aware execution support processing tasks across concurrent browsers.

items.name: SCOUT: Synergizing Reasoning and Tool-Use for Computer-Use Safety
items.summary: Introduces SCOUT, a safety verifier that first derives task-specific completion and safety rubrics from a computer-use trajectory, then actively probes the resulting environment for evidence. It evaluates whether these two stages detect harmful consequences that screenshots alone can miss.

items.name: AdaptArena: Evaluating Test-Time Personalization of Web Agents
items.summary: Introduces AdaptArena to test whether web agents can infer unstated user preferences from relevant past trajectories and carry those preferences into new tasks. Its AdaptiveAgent baseline separates preference-retrieval challenges from failures in downstream web execution.

items.name: PrecogUI: Proactive GUI Agents via Pre-cognitive Simulation and Experience Retrieval
items.summary: Presents PrecogUI, which retrieves prior anomaly and success patterns and predicts symbolic UI transitions before choosing actions. It also introduces InterfereBench, generated for evaluating long GUI workflows with disruptive events and recovery requirements.

items.name: Neuro-Symbolic Computer Use: Learning Reusable Policies for Reliable and Efficient Execution
items.summary: Learns reusable computer-use policies that encode stable workflow logic in programs while delegating grounding and state checks to neural models. Policy iteration executes variants, diagnoses failures, revises the program, and adds verification before state-changing actions.

items.name: SCA: Spatial Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning of GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces Spatial Credit Assignment, which uses click coordinates to refine group-relative reinforcement-learning updates for GUI grounding. It distinguishes failed clicks by spatial evidence while leaving the deployed action policy unchanged.

items.name: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
items.summary: Introduces MatToolBench, a Windows-based materials-science benchmark combining GUI operation, scientific-software scripting, and database queries. Expert-defined subcriteria support partial-credit scoring, while the evaluation examines domain knowledge gaps and cross-tool handoff failures.

items.name: Absorbed in Inertia: Activation Analysis for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Studies repetitive, unproductive actions in desktop agents through their internal activation states. It proposes Reset, Reroute, Restore, a context intervention that temporarily resets an agent’s trajectory and later restores it to help escape repeated ineffective behavior.

items.name: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
items.summary: Introduces professional engineering tasks across software domains, with GUI and CLI access and artifact checks for geometric, physical, and design validity.

items.name: HybridCUA: Learning to Orchestrate GUI and CLI for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Trains computer agents on verified GUI, command-line, and interleaved trajectories to learn when and how to combine interaction modes.

items.name: RealGUINoise: An Interactive Cross-Platform Benchmark for GUI Agent Robustness under Real-World Interface Noise
items.summary: Evaluates interactive GUI agents under varied realistic interface noise, comparing task completion, safety, and behavior with clean-environment runs.

items.name: SimTrace: Grounded Multimodal User Trajectories Generation for Online User Modeling
items.summary: Introduces SimTrace, a framework that generates synthetic multimodal web clickstreams by pairing a computer-use client agent's actions with web observations and user context.

items.name: StateFork: Branchable Infrastructure for Agent Exploration
items.summary: Introduces StateFork and Waypoint for branching and restoring terminal-agent sessions so agents can explore multiple paths while preserving execution state.

items.name: Action Conditioned Bisimulation For GUI Agent Memory
items.summary: Defines a GUI-memory merge rule that treats two states as equivalent only when shared actions lead to matching outcomes and successor states. The training-free method replaces observation-similarity merging and is tested in closed-loop MiniWoB++ interaction.

items.name: Talk2Agent: Benchmarking Voice Interfaces for Text Agents
items.summary: Introduces Talk2Agent, a benchmark of spoken instructions for computer-use tasks that measures whether voice interfaces preserve task-critical information. It pairs human speech with an execution-free intention-based metric and checks how that metric relates to downstream task completion.

items.name: ReSAIL: Mitigating Collapse in Iterative Agent Self-Distillation
items.summary: Introduces ReSAIL, an augmentation for iterative agent self-distillation that selects informative interaction steps; it also tests GUI-agent action prediction.

items.name: Learning Reliable GUI Agents under Imperfect Priors
items.summary: Combines structured GUI exploration with training designed to tolerate imperfect retrieved experience. It builds state-transition graphs and synthetic task trajectories, then injects realistic forms of interface drift so agents learn when to rely on or reject prior guidance.

items.name: OSWorld-Science: A Benchmark of Computer Use Agents for Learning and Using Scientific Software
items.summary: Benchmarks computer agents on scientific-software workflows with task-specific checks of application states and generated research artifacts.

items.name: ComputerSD: Online Self-Distillation from Real-Time Feedback for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Introduces ComputerSD, which turns feedback from executed GUI transitions into online self-distillation guidance and step-level scores. A GUI analyzer supplies these signals, which are combined with trajectory-level reinforcement learning in asynchronous training.

items.name: cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Standardizes virtual machines, interaction pipelines, and agent interfaces to compare computer-use speed, cost, and task performance.

items.name: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
items.summary: Improves GUI-agent execution code by analyzing action effects and repeated-task failures, then validating bounded changes with frozen model weights.

items.name: AutoGUIWorld: Image Generators as Visual World Models for GUI Agent
items.summary: Introduces AutoGUIWorld, which combines task planning and image editing to synthesize action-grounded GUI trajectories without running the depicted software. It filters generated transitions and tests whether training on them improves agents operating real desktop and scientific applications.

items.name: Auditing Web Agent Evaluation on WebArena-Lite: Human Review of Outcomes and Trajectories
items.summary: Audits WebArena-Lite outcomes and trajectories with human review to identify automatic-evaluator false negatives and the first consequential execution errors. It also studies explicit execution-state memory and procedural guidance, showing why final task scores can miss substantial differences in agent behavior.

items.name: Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents
items.summary: Studies how to route different parts of GUI experience into model weights or runtime context. It separates locators, procedures, state facts, and lessons, then predicts their destination from recurrence and dependence on the current state.

items.name: DeskForge: Dense Supervision from Desktop Environments for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Generates dense desktop supervision by varying real application scenes and combining screenshots, accessibility trees, and window geometry.

items.name: How To Train Your World Model: Fine-tuning vs RAG for LM-based World Modeling
items.summary: Compares fine-tuned, retrieval-based and hybrid language-model world models for next-observation prediction and action selection in text environments including WebShop.

items.name: WebUIProof: Benchmarking WebUI Code Generators with UI-Agent Execution Harness
items.summary: Introduces an execution-based benchmark for generated web interfaces, with a headless-browser UI-agent harness that checks DOM interactions and functional assertions.

items.name: When to Compile a Computer-Use Agent? Measuring Payback and Making Compilation Decisions for Token Efficiency
items.summary: Introduces PACE, a protocol and online decision rule for deciding when repeated GUI procedures are worth compiling into programs. It accounts for failed compilation attempts, measured per-use savings, uncertain reuse, and execution costs under an explicit cumulative budget.

items.name: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites
items.summary: Describes WebFovea, a vision-based live-web agent whose execution loop checks action parsing, browser effects, feedback accuracy, and observation delivery. The report analyzes failures such as coordinate mismatches and silent control interactions and documents corresponding harness changes.

items.name: Securing Computer-Use Agents Against Branch Steering Attacks
items.summary: Introduces STEER-Bench to study branch-steering attacks that manipulate untrusted web data toward hazardous paths already permitted by an agent’s plan. Its COBRA architecture combines trusted branching plans with advance constraints on the parameters and destinations each branch can use.

items.name: HyperBrowseComp: A Multilingual and Multimodal Stress Test for Web-Browsing Agents
items.summary: Introduces HyperBrowseComp, a multilingual benchmark for browsing agents that must connect evidence across open-web sources, including videos, scans, images, and maps.

items.name: Control OSWorld: An AI Control Environment for GUI Computer Use Agents
items.summary: Pairs OSWorld tasks with harmful side objectives to evaluate monitors that detect malicious behavior in computer-use agent trajectories.

items.name: CUAWright: A Minimal Unified Interface for Digital Agents
items.summary: Studies a minimal terminal-based execution framework that lets digital agents construct tools and manage context across browser, desktop, and CAD tasks.

items.name: MedImageOSWorld: Benchmarking GUI Agents for Medical Image Consoles
items.summary: Evaluates GUI agents in simulated medical-imaging consoles, separately checking workflow completion and acquisition outcomes against hidden anatomical targets.

items.name: Recurrent Latent Visual Search for GUI Grounding
items.summary: Introduces ReLaViS, which performs recurrent visual search inside a grounding model by repeatedly querying screenshot tokens and feeding the resulting spatial evidence back into the model. Coarse-to-fine supervision is constructed from existing interface-element annotations.

items.name: TeleTune: Evolving Agent Skills From Offline Telemetry
items.summary: Introduces TeleTune, which edits a textual skill library using held-out action prediction on offline software-use logs with missing goals or interleaved tasks. The learned workflows also guide retrieval of demonstrations for subsequent web-agent execution.

items.name: Imagine to Act: High-Fidelity Data Synthesis via Image Editing World Model for Scalable GUI Agent Training
items.summary: Introduces Infinite-Dreamer, which learns action-conditioned screenshot editing from structured descriptions of GUI changes and uses it to synthesize robustness examples and multi-step trajectories. The synthetic data trains a mobile GUI agent evaluated on AndroidWorld, MobileWorld, and AndroidControl-Curated.

items.name: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling
items.summary: Introduces CLIFT, which certifies agent-generated verification signals against training-time judges and reuses them for per-step rewards and trajectory selection. At inference, a frozen question bank helps compare candidate web rollouts without querying an external judge.

items.name: DIBench: Benchmarking Decision Integrity of GUI-based Mobile Agents Under Deceptive Injections
items.summary: Evaluates whether deceptive UI content steers mobile agents away from instruction-consistent choices, using paired benign and injected decision states and decision-integrity metrics.

items.name: AMBER: Training Long-Horizon Web Agents through Append-Only Memory
items.summary: Introduces AMBER, an append-only memory framework in which a web agent learns to reason, act, and retain evidence using outcome-reward reinforcement learning. It studies whether preserving entries avoids the loss of facts and corrective feedback seen with rewritten memory.

items.name: PlaySuite: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Interactive Visual Intelligence
items.summary: Introduces PlaySuite, a closed-loop video-game benchmark that evaluates interactive visual agents, including computer-use agents, over extended play.

items.name: Decoupling What from Where: How Should a Small GUI Grounding Model Receive the Action Type?
items.summary: Compares ways to condition a small GUI grounding model on action type under matched training conditions on Android in the Wild. The study traces apparent gains to a coordinate-serialization choice and reports limited evidence that the gains persist with predicted action types.

items.name: Can Agents Work for Everyone? Cross-User Reliability for Mobile GUI Agents in Personalized User Interfaces
items.summary: Introduces PAIR for controlled evaluation of mobile GUI agents across user-conditioned application states and RePAIR for training from cross-user subgoal outcomes. The study examines failures when personalized interfaces change which items an agent must identify.

items.name: nanoMuse: An Open-Source Personal Agent for Every Device You Own
items.summary: Presents nanoMuse, an open-source personal agent designed to act on phone and computer screens, with a shared conversation, action-checking Sentinel, and readable file memory.

items.name: AdvSim2Real : Training Web Agents Against Adaptive Prompt Injection in a Web World Model
items.summary: Presents AdvSim2Real, which jointly adapts web-task curricula, prompt-injection adversaries, and agent policies inside a frozen web world model. It evaluates robustness against an unseen adversary and transfer from simulated interaction to a real browser.

items.name: Adversarial Images Hijack Web Agents from Visual Grounding to Browser Execution
items.summary: Introduces WebMirage, a visual red-teaming framework that models webpage element competition and action post-processing to test whether manipulated grounding decisions lead to executed browser actions.

items.name: Secure-CUA: Controlling Untrusted Influence in Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Proposes Secure-CUA, which commits to per-action transactions before reading untrusted page content and separates content queries from GUI target selection. The paper formalizes its protection assumptions and evaluates benign task utility on WebArena.

items.name: AgentTime: Can Agents Estimate and Control Their Own Runtime?
items.summary: Evaluates duration following, runtime forecasts and elapsed-time estimates in native agent harnesses, including OSWorld desktop tasks, with external timers, native graders and work-versus-wait analysis.

items.name: AgentHorizon: Evaluating Agentic Judges for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Tasks
items.summary: Introduces AgentHorizon, a benchmark for judging long computer-use trajectories using closely related instructions paired with recorded actions and screenshots. It tests whether judges can detect constraint violations and distinguish successful tasks from similar but incompatible requests.

items.name: Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling: When Weight Training Should Begin
items.summary: Studies when to improve an LLM agent's runtime harness or train its weights by classifying failed trajectories; WebArena-Lite supplies a web-task transfer test.

items.name: DeltaReplay: Task-Relative Memory Reuse for Mobile GUI Agents
items.summary: Introduces DeltaReplay, which stores mobile GUI trajectories as transition graphs and decides at each step whether to reuse an action, substitute task-specific parameters, or defer to the base agent. This supports reuse of partially matching experiences without rewriting stored memory.
